Found 2026-08-03 tracing component reachability while scoping #1259.

## The baseball calendar renders a Documents panel wired entirely to golf tables

Baseball's calendar reuses golf's `PremiumCalendarClient` verbatim. That component still renders `EventDocumentsSection`, which talks to golf actions and golf tables — so on a baseball event the panel can never load or save anything.

**Chain (all value imports, verified):**

```
src/app/baseball/(dashboard)/dashboard/calendar/page.tsx:268
  → CalendarFairway.tsx:228
    → BaseballCalendarWrapper.tsx:3-8
      → src/components/shared/calendar/PremiumCalendarClient.ts    (re-export shim, .ts)
        → src/components/golf/calendar/PremiumCalendarClient.tsx
          → MobileEventSheet.tsx:631      (mobile)
          → EventDetailModal.tsx:1038     (desktop)
            → EventDocumentsSection
```

This is deliberate reuse, documented at `CalendarFairway.tsx:13`:

> the interactive grid (`BaseballCalendarWrapper` → `PremiumCalendarClient`) is a SHARED component and is reused verbatim inside the new frame per the migration playbook §3.5.

The sharing is fine for the grid. The documents panel came along with it.

## Why it cannot work on baseball

`EventDocumentsSection` renders whenever an event is open — the only gate is `{!isCreating && event && …}` — and it is sport-agnostic in its props (`eventId`, `teamId`, `isCoach`) but not in its data layer:

- it imports `getDocuments` from `@/app/golf/actions/documents`
- `actions/event-documents.ts:65-69` queries `golf_event_documents` joined to `golf_documents`
- its own docstring: *"Coaches get an 'Attach document' affordance that pops a picker over the team's existing golf_documents"*

Given a baseball `eventId` and `teamId`:

- the list query returns nothing, always — so players see a permanently empty Documents section
- coaches (`isCoach`, lines 165/215) get an **"Attach document"** control whose picker is populated from `golf_documents` filtered by a baseball `team_id`, so it is always empty
- even if a document were selected, `golf_event_documents` has an FK to `golf_events` and a `golf_event_documents_assert_same_team` trigger (`event-documents.ts:147`), so the write cannot succeed

Live data is consistent with nobody ever having got anything out of it: `golf_event_documents` has **0 rows**.

## Confidence

This is from static tracing plus the live table counts — **I did not reproduce it in a browser.** `.env.local` holds only golf demo credentials (`GOLFHELM_*`), so I could not sign into a baseball account, and I did not create or touch one to get around that. Every link in the chain above is a value import I read directly, and the render gate is unconditional on sport, so I am confident in the mechanism; I just have not seen the pixels.

## Proposed fix

Pick one:

1. **Gate the section by sport.** Pass a capability flag through `PremiumCalendarClient` (it already takes a `capabilities` prop — `PremiumCalendarClient.tsx:1375` passes `resolvedCapabilities`) and render `EventDocumentsSection` only when the host is golf. Smallest change, honest result: baseball simply has no documents panel.
2. **Make it sport-aware.** Baseball has its own documents surface (`baseball_documents`, and `20260630180100_baseball_documents_capability`), so the section could take the action pair as props and work on both. Larger, but it gives baseball a feature it currently only appears to have.

Option 1 is the right immediate move; option 2 is a product call.

## Related

- #1259 — the golf `file_url` is built with `getPublicUrl()` against a private bucket. Not reachable through *this* panel (it can never render a row), so the two are independent; the announcement card is the live consumer there.
- Worth noting for whoever picks this up: golf itself no longer uses `PremiumCalendarClient` at all — the golf calendar page renders `FairwayCalendar`, which has no document surface. So this shared component is now effectively baseball-only while still being golf-shaped inside.
title: [LOW] Baseball calendar renders a Documents panel wired to golf tables — always empty, and its coach 'Attach document' control cannot work

body:
Found 2026-08-03 auditing storage buckets after #1259. Verified by role impersonation against the live database with non-vacuous controls.

## Every uploaded file in the `documents` bucket is readable — and deletable — by any authenticated user, across both sports

Production's policies on `storage.objects` for this bucket have no tenant dimension whatsoever:

```sql
POLICY "Documents accessible to authed users"      SELECT  TO authenticated  USING (bucket_id = 'documents')
POLICY "Authenticated users can upload documents"  INSERT  TO authenticated  USING (bucket_id = 'documents')
POLICY "Authenticated users can update documents"  UPDATE  TO authenticated  USING (bucket_id = 'documents')
POLICY "Authenticated users can delete documents"  DELETE  TO authenticated  USING (bucket_id = 'documents')
```

The predicate is only "is this the documents bucket". Membership of the owning team is never consulted.

This one bucket holds **both sports** — `golf-documents/<team_id>/…` and `baseball-documents/<team_id>/…`.

## Reproduced, with a control that makes the point by itself

Impersonating the demo golf player (`7f13c6f0-e097-4e2d-b881-70f7712a093e`, one team, no staff role):

| | visible to this player | actually exists |
|---|---|---|
| `golf_players` | 7 | 61 |
| `golf_rounds` | 94 | 299 |
| `baseball_players` | 1 | 35 |
| **`golf_documents` (metadata rows)** | **1** | **5** |
| **`storage.objects` in `documents`** | **11** | **11** |

Read the last two rows together. The `golf_documents` **table** is correctly scoped — this player sees 1 of 5 rows. The **files those rows point to** are 11 of 11, including **4 baseball files** from a different sport and a different tenant.

So the metadata is protected and the payload is not. Anyone who signs up gets read access to every document any team has ever uploaded.

The table-level numbers above are the control: the same impersonated session is demonstrably subject to RLS everywhere else, so this is not a superuser bypass or a vacuous probe.

**Not tested: DELETE.** I did not attempt a destructive operation against production. The DELETE policy carries the identical `bucket_id = 'documents'` predicate as the SELECT policy I did verify, so unauthorized deletion follows from the same reasoning — but I am flagging it as inference, not observation.

## The fix is already written, merged, and never applied

`supabase/migrations/20260728173939_documents_storage_bucket_rls.sql` exists on `main` and replaces exactly these four policies with team-scoped ones:

```
CREATE POLICY documents_select_team_scope
CREATE POLICY documents_insert_manage_scope
CREATE POLICY documents_update_manage_scope
CREATE POLICY documents_delete_manage_scope
```

None of them exist in production:

```sql
select count(*) from pg_policies
where schemaname='storage' and tablename='objects' and policyname like 'documents_%_scope';
-- 0
```

and the migration is absent from `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations`. The bucket itself exists because it was created out-of-band (dashboard), which is why nothing looked broken.

## A second migration is unapplied in the same way

`supabase/migrations/20260801080000_golf_attachments_storage_bucket.sql` — merged as `0f2255433`, *"fix(storage): create the golf-attachments bucket — message attachments have never worked (#1181)"* — is also not applied:

```sql
select count(*) from storage.buckets where id='golf-attachments';  -- 0
select count(*) from golf_message_attachments;                     -- 0
```

So the #1181 fix shipped to `main` on 2026-08-01 and golf message attachments are **still** broken in production two days later, for the original reason: the bucket does not exist.

I diffed every migration file dated on or after 2026-07-25 against `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations`, verifying each apparent gap by checking whether its objects actually exist rather than trusting filename matching. Six looked unapplied; four were false positives (applied under a different recorded name — `shot_detail_rls_correlated` → `golf_shot_detail_rls_correlated`, plus the avatars policies, the `on_auth_user_created` trigger, and `baseball_team_members_select`, all present). **These two are real.**

## Why this class keeps happening here

Merging to `main` does not apply a migration — they are applied manually. Both of these were written by someone who found a genuine hole, reviewed, and merged, and then the last step never happened. Nothing in CI or on any dashboard reports "migrations on main that are not in `schema_migrations`", so an unapplied fix is indistinguishable from a shipped one when reading the repo.

## Proposed fix

1. **Apply `20260728173939_documents_storage_bucket_rls`.** This is the security repair and it is one command. I deliberately did not apply it myself — it is a production schema change to a shared database, and it warrants the `db-migration-reviewer` pass before it goes in.
2. **Apply `20260801080000_golf_attachments_storage_bucket`**, which also fixes #1181 for real.
3. **Add a drift check** that fails when a migration file on `main` has no row in `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations`. That is the control that would have caught both of these, and it generalises beyond storage. The existing `src/test/schema/storage-buckets-tracked.test.ts` asserts a bucket is *created by a tracked migration* — it cannot tell whether that migration was ever run, which is precisely the gap here.
4. While applying (1), note that the golf `documents` read path is separately broken — see #1259, where `file_url` is built with `getPublicUrl()` against this private bucket.

## Related

- #1259 — golf document attachments undownloadable (`getPublicUrl` on a private bucket). Same bucket, different layer.
- #1261 — `baseball_videos` bucket missing entirely, and the guard test blind spot.
- #1258, #1257 — the other cross-tenant RLS findings from tonight.
title: [HIGH] Every uploaded document is readable+deletable by any authenticated user across both sports — the team-scoping migration was merged but never applied to prod

body:
Found 2026-08-03 extending the #1259 investigation — auditing every `getPublicUrl` call site against the bucket it targets.

## Baseball video upload writes to a storage bucket that does not exist

`src/components/features/video-upload.tsx:131`:

```ts
const result = await supabase.storage.from('baseball_videos').upload(fileName, file, {
  cacheControl: '3600',
  upsert: false,
});
if (result.error) throw result.error;
...
const urlData = supabase.storage.from('baseball_videos').getPublicUrl(fileName);
```

There is no `baseball_videos` bucket:

```sql
select id from storage.buckets where id in ('baseball_videos','baseball-videos');
-- 0 rows
```

The full bucket list is `avatars, baseball-imports, course-images, documents, helm-bridge-feedback, lifting-nutrition, logos, recruit-documents`. Supabase answers an upload to a missing bucket with `{"statusCode":"404","error":"Bucket not found","code":"NoSuchBucket"}` — the same shape I captured live on #1259.

## It is reachable, and it is the only upload path

- `/baseball/dashboard/videos` → `src/app/baseball/(dashboard)/dashboard/videos/page.tsx:86` renders `VideoLibraryClient`
- `src/components/baseball/video/VideoLibraryClient.tsx:529` renders it for **players**:
  ```tsx
  {showUpload && !isCoach && (
    <VideoUpload onUploadComplete={...} onCancel={...} />
  )}
  ```
- The component is file-only — it holds `const [file, setFile] = useState<File | null>(null)` and offers no URL alternative, so there is no working path around it.

## It has never worked

```sql
select (select count(*) from baseball_videos) as video_rows,
       (select count(*) from storage.objects where bucket_id='baseball_videos') as objects;
-- video_rows = 5, objects = 0
```

All 5 existing rows are seeded external URLs (`https://demo.baseballhelmdemo.com/videos/…`), not uploads. Zero objects have ever been stored. So this is broken-and-unused rather than users hitting errors today — the same category the storage-bucket test already uses for `expense-receipts`.

**Not observed live:** `.env.local` carries only golf demo credentials (`GOLFHELM_*`), so I could not sign into a baseball player account to click the button. The failure is established from the code path plus the absent bucket, not from a UI reproduction. I did not create an account or touch a real one to get around that.

## The guard that exists to catch this is defeated by a name collision

`src/test/schema/storage-buckets-tracked.test.ts` was written for exactly this defect, and it passes. The reason is `isTracked()`:

```ts
function isTracked(id: string): boolean {
  return (
    /INSERT\s+INTO\s+storage\.buckets/i.test(blob) &&
    new RegExp(`['"]${escaped(id)}['"]`).test(blob)
  );
}
```

Both tests run against `blob`, the whole concatenated migration corpus, and they are never correlated with each other:

1. *Does any migration anywhere insert into `storage.buckets`?* — yes, e.g. `20260801080000_golf_attachments_storage_bucket.sql`.
2. *Does `'baseball_videos'` appear in quotes anywhere?* — yes, at `supabase/migrations/20260624002000_baseball_videos_coach_rls_and_recruiting_check.sql:36`:
   ```sql
   AND tablename  = 'baseball_videos'
   ```
   That is the **table** `baseball_videos`, in a policy-existence guard. It has nothing to do with storage.

So any bucket id that happens to share a name with a table — or appear in any comment, policy or index anywhere in migrations — is reported as tracked. The test's own failure message is emphatic that `KNOWN_MISSING_BUCKETS` must not be used to paper over a real gap, which makes it worth fixing the detector rather than adding a line.

This also means the guard's coverage is weaker than it reads for every other bucket it currently blesses.

## Proposed fix

1. **Tighten `isTracked()`** so the id must appear inside an actual bucket-insert statement, not anywhere in the corpus. Something like matching the insert statement and checking the id within it:

```ts
function isTracked(id: string): boolean {
  const inserts = blob.match(/INSERT\s+INTO\s+storage\.buckets[\s\S]{0,600}?;/gi) ?? [];
  const q = new RegExp(`['"]${escaped(id)}['"]`);
  return inserts.some((stmt) => q.test(stmt));
}
```
   Re-running after this change will likely surface other falsely-blessed buckets; each deserves the same treatment.

2. **Decide the bucket.** Either create `baseball_videos` in a tracked migration with player-scoped RLS — the deliberate pass `golf-attachments` got in `20260801080000` is the model — or point the component at an existing bucket. Note the same public/private tension called out for `expense-receipts` and in #1259: the code calls `getPublicUrl`, so a private bucket needs the read path to sign on demand.

3. Until the bucket exists, the upload control should not present as functional — the failure currently surfaces as a thrown storage error rather than an explanation.

## Related

- #1259 — golf documents call `getPublicUrl` on the private `documents` bucket. Same audit, different failure: there the bucket exists and the URL kind is wrong; here the bucket is absent entirely.
- #1179 — `expense-receipts`, the known missing bucket already tracked in `KNOWN_MISSING_BUCKETS` with a deliberate rationale. Not a duplicate of this.
title: [MEDIUM] Baseball video upload targets a storage bucket that does not exist — and the guard test that should catch it passes on a table-name collision

body:
Found 2026-08-03 checking role-denial surfaces as a player against the production build.

## Every "this surface isn't for you" screen prints its heading and sentence twice

`src/components/fairway/feedback/FeatureUnavailable.tsx` passes the same two strings to both of its children:

```tsx
<ViewHeader title={title} description={message} />
<EmptyState
  icon={<Lock className="h-7 w-7" strokeWidth={1.75} />}
  title={title}
  description={message}
  action={...}
/>
```

`ViewHeader` renders title + description as the page masthead. `EmptyState` renders the *same* title + description again inside the centred lock card. The component's docstring describes the intent as "a ViewHeader masthead over an EmptyState body" — the anatomy is right, but feeding both the identical strings turns it into a verbatim repeat.

## What the player sees

On `/golf/dashboard/qualifiers/new`, measured in the DOM (both copies `display: block`, `visibility: visible`, non-zero boxes — this is not a hidden responsive duplicate):

```
"Create Qualifier"                                        x=502 y=135 696x52
"Only coaches create qualifiers. You can see the ones
 your coach has scheduled on the Qualifiers page."        x=658 y=407 384x48
```

Rendered: a left-aligned `Create Qualifier` headline with the sentence under it, then ~220px of blank space, then a lock icon with `Create Qualifier` and the exact same sentence again, then the CTA.

## Affects every consumer, not one page

Confirmed as a player on four routes — each shows exactly one duplicated block:

| route | duplicated text |
|---|---|
| `/golf/dashboard/qualifiers/new` | "Only coaches create qualifiers…" |
| `/golf/dashboard/settings/coaching-intelligence` | "Coaching Intelligence settings are part of the coach toolkit…" |
| `/golf/dashboard/whats-new` | "What's New is a coach-only feature…" |
| `/golf/dashboard/intelligence` | "The Brief aggregates team-wide signals for coaches…" |

Other call sites that will show the same thing: `coachhelm/page.tsx` (two), `rounds/new/page.tsx`, `settings/coaching-intelligence/layout.tsx`.

Control: the same sweep over `/roster`, `/tasks`, `/announcements`, `/travel`, `/documents`, `/settings` as the same player found **zero** duplicated blocks — so this is specific to `FeatureUnavailable`, not a general layout fault.

## Proposed fix

Pick one surface to carry the copy. The masthead already establishes where you are, so the smaller change is to stop repeating it in the card:

```tsx
<ViewHeader title={title} description={message} />
<EmptyState
  icon={<Lock className="h-7 w-7" strokeWidth={1.75} />}
  action={...}
/>
```

Alternatively keep the EmptyState as the whole message and drop the `ViewHeader` description. Either way it is a one-line change in the shared component and fixes all eight call sites at once.

Severity P3 — cosmetic, no functional impact. Filing because it is on the surface a user hits precisely when they are already confused about why they can't get somewhere, and it reads as a rendering bug.
title: [LOW] Every role-denial screen renders its heading and message twice — FeatureUnavailable feeds the same strings to ViewHeader and EmptyState

body:
Found 2026-08-03 testing announcements-with-attachments end to end against the production build, as coach then as player.

## Golf document attachments cannot be opened — the stored URL points at the public endpoint of a private bucket

A player clicks an attachment on an announcement and lands on a raw JSON error page:

```json
{"statusCode":"404","error":"Bucket not found","message":"Bucket not found","code":"NoSuchBucket"}
```

## Root cause

The `documents` storage bucket is **private**:

```sql
select id, public from storage.buckets where id = 'documents';
-- documents | false
```

But `golf_documents.file_url` is built with `getPublicUrl()`, which just string-formats `/storage/v1/object/public/<bucket>/<path>` without checking that the bucket is public. Six write/read paths in `src/app/golf/actions/documents.ts` do this:

| line | function |
|---|---|
| 310 | `createDocumentImpl` |
| 432 | `saveTextDocumentImpl` |
| 686 | `uploadNewVersionImpl` |
| 796 | `getDocumentVersionsImpl` |
| 865 | `revertToVersionImpl` |
| 1147 | `uploadGolfDocumentImpl` |

So every persisted `file_url` is a dead link. Live data confirms it — of 5 golf documents, **5 use the public shape and 0 are signed**:

```sql
select count(*) filter (where file_url like '%/object/public/documents/%') as public_url_docs,
       count(*) filter (where file_url like '%token=%')                    as signed_url_docs
from golf_documents;
-- public_url_docs = 5, signed_url_docs = 0
```

The files themselves are fine. `storage.objects` holds every one of them at the right size — this is purely the URL form.

## Two consumers render that URL directly

1. `src/components/fairway/pages/announcements/FairwayPlayerAnnouncementCard.tsx:423`
   ```tsx
   const url = d.document?.file_url;
   ...
   onClick={() => { if (url) void openExternalUrl(url); }}
   ```
2. `src/components/golf/calendar/EventDocumentsSection.tsx:203`
   ```tsx
   <a href={row.document.file_url} target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">
   ```

Both open the dead URL in a new tab.

## Reproduced live

As the coach, on the demo team, I uploaded a PDF and posted an announcement with it attached. Persistence is correct:

```sql
select title, recipients, attachments from ... where created_at > now() - interval '20 minutes';
-- "QA attach 05:24:09" | recipients = 1 | attachments = 1
```

Then signed in as the player (Cole Bennett), expanded the announcement, and clicked the attachment:

- the **Attachments** section renders, the document name shows, the button is **enabled** (`disabled={!url}` passes, because a non-empty string *is* present — it's just a non-working one)
- clicking opens a new tab to
  `https://<project>.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/documents/golf-documents/6ecdd1a6-…/430d3e8e-….pdf`
- that tab renders the `NoSuchBucket` JSON above

Confirmed independently with `curl` and no auth at all — the same 404 for my uploaded file *and* for a pre-existing seeded document, with a nonexistent-path control also 404 (so the bucket genuinely does not serve public objects).

## Baseball does this correctly

```sql
select count(*) filter (where file_url like '%/object/sign/%') as sign_endpoint,
       count(*) filter (where file_url like '%token=%')        as signed_shape
from baseball_documents;
-- 4 of 4 on both
```

Baseball persists signed URLs; golf persists public ones against the same private bucket. (This is the third finding tonight where baseball is the correct reference and golf is not — see #1257 and #1258.)

## What still works

`getPreviewUrlImpl` (lines 1047 and 1080) is the one path that uses `createSignedUrl(path, 3600)`, so the Documents page's own preview/download is expected to be fine. I could not drive that control in automation — the document rows render as unlabelled buttons — so I am **not** claiming it works or is broken; I only verified it takes a different code path.

## Impact

Any golf document surfaced outside the Documents page is undownloadable: announcement attachments and calendar-event attachments. Today that is 1 announcement attachment and 0 event attachments in the database, so almost nobody has hit it — but it fails 100% of the time whenever the feature is used, and it fails *silently*, with an enabled-looking button and a JSON error page rather than an in-app message.

## Proposed fix

1. Stop persisting a URL at all. `file_url` is a derived value with a security-relevant lifetime; storing it means it is either permanently wrong (today) or a permanently valid bearer token (if it were signed with a long TTL). Persist `storage_path` and mint a short-lived signed URL at read time — which is exactly what `getPreviewUrlImpl` already does and what baseball effectively does.
2. As the minimal change: replace `getPublicUrl` with `createSignedUrl` in the six sites above, and have both consumers request a fresh URL rather than reading `file_url`.
3. Make `disabled={!url}` meaningful — a dead URL should not present as an enabled button. Failing that, surface an in-app error instead of navigating to raw storage JSON.
4. Backfill: the 5 existing rows need their `file_url` regenerated (or the column dropped in favour of `storage_path`).
5. Add a regression test asserting no `golf_documents.file_url` matches `/object/public/` while the bucket is private.
title: [MEDIUM] Golf document attachments are undownloadable — file_url uses the public endpoint of a private bucket (NoSuchBucket)

body:
Found 2026-08-03 sweeping every PERMISSIVE policy in the database for trivially-true predicates, after #1257 turned one up. Verified by role impersonation against the live database with a non-vacuous control.

## Every authenticated user can read every golf coach's name, email and phone

`golf_coaches` has four policies. Three are correctly scoped to the owner. The fourth is not:

```sql
POLICY golf_coaches_insert_own  INSERT  USING (user_id = auth.uid())
POLICY golf_coaches_update_own  UPDATE  USING (user_id = auth.uid())
POLICY golf_coaches_delete_own  DELETE  USING (user_id = auth.uid())
POLICY golf_coaches_select_all  SELECT  USING (true)          -- <--
```

Policies are OR'd, so `USING (true)` makes the whole table world-readable to any signed-in user. The table carries `full_name, email, phone, title, bio`.

## Reproduced

Impersonating the demo player (a Demo University Golf player, one team, no staff role):

```sql
SET LOCAL ROLE authenticated;
SELECT set_config('request.jwt.claims',
  '{"sub":"7f13c6f0-e097-4e2d-b881-70f7712a093e","role":"authenticated"}', true);
```

| table | visible to this player | actually in the DB |
|---|---|---|
| `golf_players` | 7 | 61 |
| `golf_rounds` | 94 | 299 |
| `golf_documents` | 0 | — |
| **`golf_coaches`** | **15** | **15** |

The first three rows are the control, and they matter: tenant isolation is demonstrably working on the data tables — this player sees only their own team's players and rounds. `golf_coaches` is the one table where they see **100% of the platform**, spanning **12 organizations**, including **10 email addresses and 3 phone numbers**.

I counted rather than selected. I did not read any individual's contact details, and nothing was modified.

## Baseball is, again, the correct reference

`baseball_coaches` has exactly the policy golf should have:

```sql
POLICY baseball_coaches_select  SELECT  TO authenticated
  USING (auth.uid() = user_id OR shares_my_baseball_organization(organization_id))
```

This is the second finding tonight (with #1257) where the golf policy is open and its baseball twin is right.

## Nothing in the application depends on the open policy

I checked all **180** `from('golf_coaches')` call sites. **178** filter by `user_id = <caller>` or by a specific `id`/`in` list. The two that don't:

- `src/lib/admin/data/users.ts:258` — uses `createAdminClient()` (service role, bypasses RLS entirely) and is documented `CALLER must have passed requireSuperAdmin()`.
- `src/app/golf/actions/onboarding.ts:164` — an `INSERT`, governed by `golf_coaches_insert_own`, not the SELECT policy.

So the breadth is unused. Tightening it is not a behaviour change.

## Proposed fix, dry-run before proposing

The obvious predicate is wrong. `get_user_golf_organization_id()` resolves the org by reading `golf_coaches`, so it returns NULL for a player — using it alone would hide a player's own coaches (breaking author names on announcements, messaging, roster). The predicate needs a player path:

```sql
DROP POLICY golf_coaches_select_all ON public.golf_coaches;

CREATE POLICY golf_coaches_select ON public.golf_coaches
  FOR SELECT TO authenticated
  USING (
    user_id = (SELECT auth.uid())
    OR organization_id = public.get_user_golf_organization_id()
    OR organization_id IN (
         SELECT t.organization_id FROM public.golf_teams t
         WHERE t.id IN (
           SELECT m.team_id FROM public.golf_team_members m
           JOIN public.golf_players p ON p.id = m.player_id
           WHERE p.user_id = (SELECT auth.uid())
         )
       )
  );
```

Evaluated as a plain SELECT against live data before proposing it:

| role | sees today | would see | orgs |
|---|---|---|---|
| demo player | 15 | **2** | 1 |
| demo coach | 15 | **2** | 1 |

Both roles keep exactly their own organization's coaches. Worth considering folding this into a `shares_my_golf_organization(uuid)` helper to mirror baseball, since the same predicate will be wanted elsewhere.

## Severity

P2, not P1. It is a genuine cross-tenant read of PII, but it is read-only and college coaching-staff emails are frequently published on athletics sites anyway. The parts that are *not* public are the phone numbers and the implied roster of which schools are on the platform.

It compounds with #1257 though: that issue lets an attacker join any team, and this one hands them the staff directory to go with it.

## Also swept, not bugs

The same scan flagged 21 other trivially-true policies. All are either `TO service_role` (correct) or read-only reference data with no tenant dimension: `golf_courses`, `golf_course_holes`, `golf_course_tees`, `golf_drills`, `golf_metrics`, `golf_pga_standards`, `golf_global_patterns`. `organizations_select_all` is also `USING (true)` but the table holds only public branding (name, division, conference, colors, logo) — no contact data — so I am not filing it.

One that is worth a second opinion but that I am not filing as a security issue: `golf_course_tee_holes_insert WITH CHECK (true)` lets any authenticated user insert tee/hole rows into the shared course library. That is a data-integrity concern for a global reference table rather than a tenant boundary, and I could not show user-visible harm from it tonight.
title: [MEDIUM] Every authenticated user can read every golf coach's name, email and phone — golf_coaches SELECT policy is USING (true)

body:
Found 2026-08-03 probing RLS boundaries between roles and tenants. Verified by role impersonation against the live database, with own-tenant controls on every probe.

## Any authenticated player can join any team in the platform, without its join code

Two policies share the same flawed predicate — `join_code IS NOT NULL` — and together they compose into a cross-tenant authorization hole.

**1. Every team and every join code is world-readable to any signed-in user.**

`golf_teams`:

```sql
POLICY golf_teams_select_by_join_code  SELECT  TO authenticated
  USING (join_code IS NOT NULL)
```

RLS policies are OR'd, so this permissive rule completely overrides the correctly-scoped sibling `golf_teams_select USING (is_golf_team_coach(id) OR is_golf_team_player(id))`.

Impersonating the demo player (Demo University Golf), reading teams from other organizations:

| team | join_code |
|---|---|
| Codex Golf | `HTUAHX85` |
| Denison University Golf | `8JCXH3ZX` |
| Guilford College Men's Golf Team | `PXGF5L` |
| Hampden-Sydney Golf | `R8JPP2BJ` |
| Lenoir-Rhyne University Golf | `MZEY6MD8` |
| MU Women's Golf | `JGXMRD2T` |
| Piedmont University Golf | `BEU4S459` |

All 13 teams and 27 organizations are visible. These are real schools, not fixtures.

**2. The join itself never checks that you supplied the code.**

`golf_team_members`:

```sql
POLICY "Players can join teams"  INSERT  TO authenticated
  WITH CHECK (
    EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM golf_players gp
             WHERE gp.id = player_id AND gp.user_id = auth.uid())
    AND
    EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM golf_teams gt
             WHERE gt.id = team_id AND gt.join_code IS NOT NULL)   -- <-- only that a code EXISTS
  )
```

The second clause asserts the team *has* a join code. It never compares one. A `WITH CHECK` clause cannot see the code the user typed, so this predicate can never do what it was written to do.

## Reproduced

As the demo player (`auth.uid() = 7f13c6f0-…`, a Demo University Golf player), inserting into a team belonging to a different organization, supplying no code:

```sql
SET LOCAL ROLE authenticated;
SELECT set_config('request.jwt.claims', '{"sub":"7f13c6f0-…","role":"authenticated"}', true);

INSERT INTO golf_team_members (team_id, player_id, status)
VALUES ('<other org team>', '<my player id>', 'active');
-- INSERT SUCCEEDED
```

Note for anyone re-testing: the same statement **with a `RETURNING` clause fails** with `new row violates row-level security policy`, because `RETURNING` additionally needs SELECT on the new row and `golf_team_members_select_v5` does not yet grant it. That false negative is what nearly made me dismiss this — the write itself is permitted.

I ran this against **"QA Test Golf Team"** (0 members, clearly a fixture), not a real school, and deleted the membership immediately. Verified afterwards: total memberships back to the baseline 51, QA team back to 0, demo player back to exactly one team. **No real organization's data was read or modified at any point.**

Controls, so none of the above is a vacuous probe: as the same impersonated user, own player row = 1, own rounds = 19, foreign player row = 0, foreign rounds = 0. Tenant isolation on the *data* tables is otherwise working correctly — it is the membership edge that is open.

## Blast radius

Membership is the key to almost everything. 19 policies across 18 tables gate on `get_current_player_team_ids()` / `is_golf_team_player()`:

```
golf_rounds, golf_holes, golf_shots            — full performance history
golf_conversations                             — team messaging
golf_documents, golf_announcement_documents,
golf_event_documents                           — uploaded files
golf_events, golf_event_attendance             — schedule + who attended
golf_tasks, golf_announcement_tasks
golf_qualifiers, golf_qualifier_entries,
golf_qualifier_round_courses
golf_team_members                              — the roster itself
golf_team_coach_staff, golf_team_saved_courses, golf_teams
```

So a single unauthorized insert converts into read access over another school's roster, every round/hole/shot their players have recorded, their documents, and their conversations.

There is a second consequence: per `src/lib/golf/signup-gate.ts`, a team `join_code` is also accepted as the **platform signup access code**. Leaking all of them leaks the signup gate for everyone.

## Proposed fix

1. **Delete `golf_teams_select_by_join_code`.** A `USING` clause cannot implement "look up the team matching the code I typed" — it can only widen visibility. Replace it with a `SECURITY DEFINER` function that takes the code and returns just the matching team:

```sql
CREATE FUNCTION public.golf_team_by_join_code(p_code text)
RETURNS TABLE (id uuid, name text, organization_id uuid)
LANGUAGE sql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = '' AS $$
  SELECT t.id, t.name, t.organization_id
  FROM public.golf_teams t
  WHERE upper(t.join_code) = upper(trim(p_code))
$$;
REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.golf_team_by_join_code(text) FROM PUBLIC, anon;
GRANT  EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.golf_team_by_join_code(text) TO authenticated;
```

Note it does not return `join_code`.

2. **Rewrite the join policy to require proof of the code.** The join flow should go through a `SECURITY DEFINER` RPC that takes the code, resolves the team itself, and inserts — so the code is verified server-side and never has to be re-checked in a `WITH CHECK`. Then narrow `"Players can join teams"` to only what that RPC does, or drop it in favour of the RPC.

3. **Rotate every existing `join_code`.** They have been readable by every authenticated user, and they double as signup access codes.

4. Add an RLS regression test: an authenticated player must NOT be able to `SELECT` a team they are not on, and must NOT be able to `INSERT` a membership for a team whose code they did not supply.

## Scope check

Baseball's equivalent (`baseball_teams` / roster) should be audited for the same pattern before this is closed — I have not checked it yet.
title: [HIGH] Any authenticated player can read every team's join_code and join any team without it — RLS predicate is 'join_code IS NOT NULL'

body:
Found 2026-08-03 checking whether the UI degrades honestly against the three known-broken integrations.

## CoachHelm has produced zero AI output for 8 days and nothing anywhere says so

```sql
select max(created_at) filter (where not fallback_to_template) as last_successful_llm_call,
       count(*) as calls_30d,
       count(*) filter (where fallback_to_template) as fell_back
from golf_coachhelm_llm_calls where created_at > now() - interval '30 days';
```

| last successful LLM call | calls (30d) | fell back to template | real LLM |
|---|---|---|---|
| **2026-07-26 02:54:04Z** | 83 | **54** | 29 (all before 07-26) |

Every LLM call since **26 July** has fallen back to a deterministic template. Per-day, the last seven days are **100% fallback**. Total model spend in 30 days: **$1.92**, all of it before the cutoff.

The reason is recorded in `error_logs`:

> `compose() fell back to the template: AI features are unavailable: the Vercel AI Gateway account is out of credit. Retrying will not help until it is topped up.`

That message is excellent — it distinguishes a config/billing fault from a transient error and says retrying won't help. The problem is that **nobody is reading it.**

## The UI is honest. That is exactly why this went unnoticed.

I want to be clear that the product is not lying to users. `HeroNarrativeCard` gates on the full condition:

```ts
const verified = r.ok && !!r.used_llm && !!r.citations_verified;   // :72
...
{usedLlm && ( /* ✨ CoachHelm badge */ )}                          // :120
data-used-llm={usedLlm ? 'true' : 'false'}                         // :164
```

When the model is unavailable the card renders the deterministic template **without** the "✨ CoachHelm" attribution. A template is never passed off as AI. `refuseUnbilledCompose` (`v3/llm.ts:342`) deliberately returns the same shape "so every existing consumer degrades down the path it already handles… with no error state."

That is the right call for the player. It also means the failure is completely silent: the pages still render, nothing errors, and the only outward difference is a missing sparkle nobody is looking for.

## The monitoring gap

`/admin/health` is the surface that should catch this. Today it shows:

```
COACHHELM   1 amber
  CoachHelm Engine ↑ 1
```

One amber dot, driven by a single logged warning — for a subsystem that has been **completely dark for 8 days**. The board's own methodology note says it uses "2-window hysteresis — a single blip never flips a dot", which is right for error counts and wrong for this: a 100%-fallback rate is not a blip, but it produces almost no error volume because the fallback is a *successful* code path that logs one throttled warning.

There is no AI-availability metric anywhere — not on `/admin/health`, not on the cron board, not in the Cup of Helm digest.

The irony is that the data is already perfect. `golf_coachhelm_llm_calls.fallback_to_template` is written on every single call, so the availability rate is one `GROUP BY` away.

## Proposed fix

1. **Add an "AI availability" row to `/admin/health`**, computed directly from the existing column:

```sql
select 1.0 - (count(*) filter (where fallback_to_template))::numeric / nullif(count(*),0)
from golf_coachhelm_llm_calls where created_at > now() - interval '24 hours';
```

Red at 0% availability, amber below ~80%. This is a *rate*, not an error count, so it should bypass the error-count hysteresis — one dark day is worth showing.

2. **Alert on the transition, not the volume.** The existing message already asserts "retrying will not help until it is topped up" — that specific class (provider account fault, already classified by `classifyProviderFault`) deserves to page once, loudly, rather than being throttled like a recurring error.

3. **Put it in the 7am Cup of Helm digest.** "CoachHelm AI: 0% availability, last successful call 8 days ago" is exactly the kind of line that digest exists for.

4. Separately and obviously: top up the Vercel AI Gateway account. That is the actual repair — but the reason this issue is worth filing is that without 1–3, the next outage is equally invisible.

## Related

Same shape as #1255 (`/admin/billing` looks functional while production has no Stripe keys) and the Inngest credential rejection — three integrations degraded, none of them visible on a dashboard. Worth considering one "integrations" health panel covering all three.
title: [MEDIUM] CoachHelm AI has been 100% template-fallback for 8 days and no dashboard shows it — the availability data already exists, nothing reads it

body:
Found 2026-08-03 checking whether the admin surfaces disclose the three known-broken integrations.

## `/admin/billing` presents a fully working invoice form. In production it cannot work.

The page renders the complete Create-invoice flow with no caveat anywhere:

> **Billing — Create invoice**
> Bills a school or program via Stripe Invoicing. The customer pays on Stripe's hosted invoice page. **Stripe Tax is applied automatically where you hold an active registration.**
> School / program Name\* · Billing email\* · Address\* · City\* · State / province · Postal code\* · Country (ISO-2)\* · Line items · Days until due · Apply Stripe Tax · Email the invoice · **[Create invoice]**

Nothing on the page indicates the integration is unavailable. The copy actively asserts capability ("Stripe Tax is applied automatically").

**Production has no Stripe configuration at all.** Enumerated all 61 production environment variables:

```
$ vercel env ls production | awk 'NR>2{print $1}' | grep -i stripe
(no output)
```

Zero of 61 match "stripe" — neither `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` nor `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`.

`getStripe()` (`src/lib/stripe/server.ts:21-29`) throws on a missing key:

```ts
const secretKey = process.env.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY?.trim();
if (!secretKey) {
  throw new Error('STRIPE_SECRET_KEY is missing. Set a restricted API key (rk_...) in your environment.');
}
```

So in production the admin fills in a school name, billing email, full street address, city, state, postal code, country, and every line item — then hits Create invoice and gets a failure, with no way to have known beforehand.

## Corroborating: the webhook half is already visibly dead

The same missing configuration is producing errors in production right now. Over the last 4 days, **every HTTP 500 on the entire project is this one route**:

```
requestPath                 count
/api/webhooks/stripe          50
```

with 42 matching entries in `error_logs`: `[Stripe Webhook] STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET is not configured`. The route's own behaviour is correct — refusing to process a webhook it cannot verify is right — but it means Stripe events are being rejected and retried indefinitely, so billing state never syncs even for invoices created some other way.

## The configuration is inverted

Local `.env.local` **does** carry both `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` and `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, and the secret key is an **`rk_live_…` restricted key** — live mode, not test.

So today: a developer's laptop can bill real customers, and production cannot bill anyone. I did not submit the form for exactly this reason — on this machine it would have created a genuine invoice against the live Stripe account.

Two separate things worth deciding on:

1. Production is missing the keys it needs.
2. Local development holds a **live-mode** key. If that is deliberate, fine — but a test-mode key (`rk_test_…`) locally would mean nobody can accidentally invoice a real school while clicking around, which is precisely the risk I just had to steer around.

## Proposed fix

1. **Set `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` and `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` in Vercel production.** This is the actual repair; everything below is about failing honestly until then.
2. **Gate the form on configuration.** `/admin/billing` should check for Stripe configuration server-side and, when absent, render an explicit disabled state — "Stripe is not configured in this environment" — instead of a form that looks ready. The pattern already exists elsewhere in this codebase: `supabase-rate-limit.ts` returns a `reason` string for a missing env var rather than throwing, precisely so callers can distinguish a config fault from a real failure. Same idea here.
3. **Surface it on the Bridge health board.** `/admin/health` already does honest reporting ("Features with no feature-tagged data yet render neutral, never red or fake-green") — a "Billing / Stripe" row reading red on missing configuration would have caught this without anyone opening the billing page.
4. Consider switching local development to a test-mode key.

## Verified honest while here (not bugs)

- `/admin/golf/tracer` degrades correctly — the panel renders **"This panel — temporarily unavailable"** rather than blanking the page. (It does print the raw framework error text into the UI, which is rough for a human reader but it is an admin-only surface.)
- `/admin/jobs` cron board: every job `ok`, 20/20 runs, and it explicitly refuses to alarm on jobs with no history — "A job with no row yet reads 'awaiting first run' (neutral) — never a red alarm until it has actually missed its schedule."
- `/admin/health`: 16 of 17 admin routes render clean, and the board's stated methodology (2-window hysteresis, neutral for no data) is the honest design.
title: [MEDIUM] /admin/billing shows a fully working invoice form, but production has zero Stripe env vars — the failure only appears after the admin fills in the whole invoice

body:
Found 2026-08-03 testing Lift Lab role separation against the production build.

## An athlete sitting idle on /lifting/dashboard makes 173 HTTP requests per second

Measured over a clean 10-second window with the page simply open and untouched, athlete vs coach on the identical URL:

| | **Athlete** | Coach (control) |
|---|---|---|
| mainFrame navigations | **242** (24.2/sec) | 2 (0.2/sec) |
| document HTTP requests | **37** (3.7/sec) | 1 (0.1/sec) |
| **all HTTP requests** | **1,735 (173.5/sec)** | 98 (9.8/sec) |
| final URL | `/lifting/dashboard` | `/lifting/dashboard` |

The 37 *document* requests are the important number — these are real full page loads, not client-side re-renders. The page is reloading itself roughly four times a second, indefinitely. It never settles.

An earlier 8-second observation logged **2,621** mainFrame navigations before I cut it off.

The coach on the exact same URL loads once and stops. This is entirely role-dependent.

## Who hits it

Any authenticated user with a `helm_lifting_athletes` row and **no** `helm_lifting_coaches` row and **no** `helm_lifting_org_viewers` row:

```
user 7f13c6f0-… (rinin376):  athlete_rows=1  active_coach_rows=0  viewer_rows=0
```

They are not bounced out — the page renders, showing the coach shell (Home / Today / Command / Athletes / Programs / Exercises / Sessions / Readiness / Check-Ins / Groups / Import / Settings) with the banner:

> **Coach** · **View-only mode** — You can see all lifting data but cannot make changes. Invite a lifting coach…

…and then loops.

## Impact

- The user's tab is pegged; the page visibly never finishes loading.
- **173 requests/second per affected user, against your own server.** That is a self-inflicted load problem, not just a client annoyance — one athlete leaving the tab open is a sustained request flood, and it burns Vercel function invocations and Supabase quota for as long as it is open.
- The role banner is also wrong on its own terms: the user is greeted as "Coach" (`displayName = coachRow?.full_name ?? 'Coach'` in `dashboard/page.tsx:165`) when they are an athlete with no coach row.

## What I could NOT pin down

I did not find the line that re-triggers the load, and I want to be straight about that rather than guess:

- The guard in `src/app/lifting/(dashboard)/dashboard/page.tsx:124-151` resolves `orgId` from a coach row, then an `helm_lifting_org_viewers` row, and `redirect('/lifting/login')` if neither exists. This user has neither — yet the final URL is `/lifting/dashboard` and view-only content renders, so `orgId` is being resolved by some path I did not trace.
- `/lifting/login` does **not** auto-redirect authenticated users (it renders a signed-in state with a sign-out button), so this is *not* a login↔dashboard bounce.
- `grep` for `router.refresh()` / `location.reload()` across `src/components/lifting/` turns up nothing unconditional on the dashboard route itself — the hits are in realtime-subscription handlers (`LiveWeightRoomClient`) and explicit user actions.

So: symptom measured precisely and reproducible with a control; trigger not yet located. The most likely shape is a redirect that resolves differently between the server render and the client, each correcting the other.

## Reproduction

```
node scratchpad/lift-loop.mjs athlete   # 173 req/s, 37 document loads / 10s
node scratchpad/lift-loop.mjs coach     # 9.8 req/s, 1 document load  / 10s
```

Sign in at `/lifting/login` as a user who is a lifting **athlete only**, land on `/lifting/dashboard`, and count `page.on('request')` over a fixed window.

## Related

Lift Lab coach onboarding is separately blocked (#1253 — `helm_lifting_coaches` has no INSERT policy). That matters here because the *fix* for this issue is probably "send a non-coach somewhere sensible", and right now there is nowhere sensible to send them: they cannot become a coach, and there is no athlete-facing Lift Lab surface in the route tree (all 19 routes are `/lifting/dashboard/*` coach surfaces plus auth pages).
title: [HIGH] Lift Lab athlete on /lifting/dashboard hits an infinite reload loop — 173 HTTP req/sec, 37 document loads per 10s (coach: 1)

body:
Found 2026-08-03 testing Lift Lab end-to-end against the production build.

## A correctly-invited Lift Lab coach cannot finish onboarding. Ever.

`helm_lifting_coaches` has RLS enabled and **no INSERT policy for any role**:

```sql
select policyname, cmd, roles from pg_policies
where schemaname='public' and tablename='helm_lifting_coaches';
```

| policy | cmd | roles | expression |
|---|---|---|---|
| `hlc_select` | SELECT | authenticated | own row OR `helm_lifting_can_view_org(...)` |
| `hlc_update` | UPDATE | authenticated | `user_id = auth.uid()` |
| `hlc_delete` | DELETE | authenticated | `false` |
| — | **INSERT** | — | **does not exist** |

`relrowsecurity = true`, and a query for any `INSERT`/`ALL` policy on the table returns **zero rows for every role**. Under RLS, absent policy = denied.

`completeLiftingCoachOnboarding` (`src/app/lifting/actions/onboarding.ts:75`) writes through the **RLS-bound** client:

```ts
const supabase = await createClient();            // NOT createAdminClient()
...
await fromUntyped(supabase, 'helm_lifting_coaches').upsert(insert, {
  onConflict: 'user_id,organization_id',
  ignoreDuplicates: false,
});
```

An upsert with no existing row takes the INSERT branch, and the INSERT branch is denied. So the row can never be created through the product.

## Reproduced end to end

Signed in as a user with **no** `helm_lifting_coaches` row, then:

1. `/lifting/coach` with no invite → the UI correctly says **"No invitation found — Enter your invite code or ask your head coach to invite you"** and the submit button is **disabled**. Guard works.
2. Inserted one valid `helm_lifting_coach_invites` row (pending, unexpired) for that email.
3. Reloaded `/lifting/coach` → org picker correctly populated: `["Select your school / organization", "Demo University Golf"]`, submit **enabled**. The invite lookup works.
4. Filled the form, submitted → **`Failed to save profile. Please try again.`**
5. Verified afterwards: `helm_lifting_coaches` row count unchanged, no row for that user. (Probe invite deleted; nothing left behind.)

Supporting circumstantial evidence: there are only **2** `helm_lifting_coaches` rows in the entire database. Consistent with the UI path never having worked — the existing ones were almost certainly created by seed/SQL.

## Careful: the obvious fix reintroduces a privilege-escalation hole

I checked whether this was exploitable in the other direction first, and it is not — but only by accident, and the accident is exactly what is being fixed.

`completeLiftingCoachOnboarding` takes `organizationId` **straight from the client** and validates only `if (!user)`:

```ts
const insert = {
  user_id: user.id,
  organization_id: organizationId,   // <- client-supplied, unvalidated
  status: 'active',
  onboarding_completed: true,
};
```

There is no server-side check that the caller was invited to that organization. Today that is harmless because RLS denies the insert to everyone. **If someone "fixes" onboarding by adding a permissive INSERT policy** — e.g. `with check (user_id = auth.uid())` — then any authenticated user can POST this action with any `organizationId` and mint themselves an `active` coach of any organization, seeing its athletes, programs, sessions and readiness/check-in data.

The invite check currently lives only in the client component, which is not a security boundary.

## Proposed fix — one policy that solves both

Put the invite requirement in the policy, so it fixes onboarding and closes the escalation path in the same change:

```sql
CREATE POLICY hlc_insert ON public.helm_lifting_coaches
  FOR INSERT TO authenticated
  WITH CHECK (
    user_id = (SELECT auth.uid())
    AND EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM public.helm_lifting_coach_invites i
      WHERE i.organization_id = helm_lifting_coaches.organization_id
        AND lower(i.email) = lower((SELECT auth.jwt() ->> 'email'))
        AND i.status = 'pending'
        AND i.expires_at > now()
    )
  );
```

Then, independently, add the same invite check server-side in `completeLiftingCoachOnboarding` so the action does not rely solely on RLS, and mark the invite `accepted` on success (it currently stays `pending` forever, so an invite is reusable).

Worth an RLS regression test alongside it: an invited user CAN insert their own row; an uninvited user CANNOT; and nobody can insert a row for a different `user_id`.

## Severity

Filed HIGH because it is a total functional block on the coach-facing half of a product — not a degraded experience, an impossible one — and because the natural fix is a footgun. It is not a live security hole today.
title: [HIGH] Lift Lab coach onboarding is impossible — helm_lifting_coaches has no INSERT policy, so even an invited coach gets 'Failed to save profile'

body:
Found 2026-08-03 sweeping all 19 Lift Lab routes against the production build.

## Every single Lift Lab page 400s on its own logo

19 of 19 routes emit a failed request. It is the same one every time:

```
400 GET /_next/image?url=%2Fhelm-lifting-logo.png&w=32&q=75
body: The requested resource isn't a valid image.
```

Cause: **`public/helm-lifting-logo.png` does not exist.**

```
$ test -f public/helm-lifting-logo.png && echo exists || echo MISSING
MISSING
```

Its siblings are all present — `public/helm-baseball-logo.png`, `public/helm-golf-logo.png`, `public/Helm-Logo-New-Main.png`. Lift Lab is the only product whose logo asset was never added.

## Referenced in six places

```
src/components/lifting/shell/LabShell.tsx:59           width={32} height={32}   <- the shared shell
src/app/lifting/(auth)/login/page.tsx:136              width={56} height={56}
src/app/lifting/(auth)/signup/page.tsx:104             width={56} height={56}
src/app/lifting/(auth)/forgot-password/page.tsx:97     width={56} height={56}
src/app/lifting/(auth)/reset-password/page.tsx:122     width={56} height={56}
src/app/lifting/(onboarding)/coach/page.tsx:146        width={56} height={56}
```

`LabShell` is why the count is 19/19 rather than 5 — it wraps every dashboard route, so the broken logo is in the header of the entire product. The five auth/onboarding pages break it independently, which means it is also the **first thing a new Lift Lab user sees on the login screen**.

All six use `next/image` with `priority`, so it is fetched eagerly on every page and fails before anything else paints.

## What the user sees

The pages themselves render fine — nav, content, everything works. The logo slot falls back to the `alt` text ("Helm Lifting Lab"), so the product looks unfinished rather than broken. Every page load also puts a 400 in the network log, which is noise for anyone debugging something real in this product.

To be clear about severity: **nothing is functionally broken.** This is cosmetic. It is filed because it is on 100% of pages of a whole product including its sign-in screen, and the fix is to add one file.

## Fix

Add `public/helm-lifting-logo.png`, matching the dimensions/treatment of `public/helm-baseball-logo.png` (the closest sibling — same `next/image` usage at 32px in-shell and 56px on auth screens).

If a Lift Lab mark does not exist yet, the honest interim is to point those six references at an existing Helm mark (`Helm-Logo-New-Main.png`) rather than leave a 404ing asset in the shell — a wrong-but-present logo reads as intentional; a missing one reads as broken.

Worth a cheap guard afterwards: a test that every `next/image` `src` beginning `/` resolves to a real file under `public/`. That would have caught this the moment the reference was added, and would catch the next one.

## Noticed while here

`public/helm-golf-logo.png alias` — a file whose name literally ends in `" alias"` (a macOS Finder alias that got committed). Not referenced by anything I could find, so it is dead weight rather than a bug, but it is the kind of thing that confuses an asset audit later.
title: [LOW] public/helm-lifting-logo.png does not exist — all 19 Lift Lab pages 400 on the logo, including the sign-in screen

body:
Found 2026-08-03 sweeping every golf route as both roles against the production build.

## Two routes crash React on 100% of coach visits

| Route | Coach | Player |
|---|---|---|
| `/golf/dashboard/settings/notifications` | **#310 on 3/3** | clean 0/20 |
| `/golf/dashboard/team-hub` | **#310 on 3/3** | clean 0/20 |

```
Minified React error #310  ("Rendered more hooks than during the previous render")
  at aT      (chunks/4bd1b696….js)
  at Object.oi [as useMemo]
  at t.useMemo (chunks/93489-….js)
  at k        (chunks/93489-….js)
```

Chunk `93489` disassembles to Next.js router internals (`InvariantError`, `addLocale`, `pageshow`) — the throw is inside the framework's client router during the server `redirect()`, not in an app component.

Measured, not inferred: 20/20 coach loads crashed, 0/20 player loads did. The player renders these pages normally; only the redirect path breaks.

## This is a known bug whose mitigation missed these two

`/golf/dashboard/my-development/page.tsx` documents both the crash and the fix:

> **BELT-AND-BRACES (2026-07-22):** next.config.mjs `redirects()` now intercepts this path at the framework routing layer, before this page ever renders — *the fix for the React #310 "rendered more hooks" crash on client-navigation into bare redirect() shims.*

I scanned all 15 golf routes that redirect a coach, 3 loads each:

- **13 clean** — `/golf/admin`, `/admin/crm`, `/admin/demo-sessions`, `/dashboard/alerts`, `/analytics/coachhelm`, `/development`, `/hub`, `/insights`, `/my-development`, `/my-game-profile`, `/my-insights`, `/my-standing`, `/patterns`
- **2 crash, every time** — the two above

Every one of the 13 clean routes is listed in `next.config.mjs` `redirects()`. Neither crasher is (`grep -c "team-hub\|settings/notifications" next.config.mjs` → **0**).

## Why they were missed, and why the existing fix cannot be applied

The 13 are *bare shims* — an unconditional `permanentRedirect()` to a fixed destination, so they can be hoisted into `next.config.mjs` and never render.

These two are **real pages with a role-conditional redirect**:

```ts
// team-hub/page.tsx
const session = await getGolfSessionProfile();
if (!session) redirect('/golf/login');
const { player } = session;
if (!player) redirect('/golf/dashboard');       // coaches → main dashboard

// settings/notifications/page.tsx
if (!session.player) redirect('/golf/dashboard/settings');
```

The destination depends on who is asking, and `next.config.mjs` `redirects()` cannot read the session — so the config-layer fix is structurally unavailable here. They were not an oversight in a list; they are a case the existing fix does not cover.

## Impact

The coach does land on the right page (`/golf/dashboard` and `/golf/dashboard/settings` respectively), so this is not a dead end for the user. What it costs:

- An uncaught React error on every coach visit to either route.
- **It is flooding error tracking.** While reproducing this I watched Sentry's own ingest endpoint return **HTTP 429** — Sentry is rate-limiting this project because of the volume. That is worth noting on its own: a 429 from the ingest means other, real errors are being dropped.
- Any user landing mid-transition sees a flash of the error state.

I originally mis-read those 429s as the *cause* of the crash. They are the consequence — recording that so the next person does not chase it the same way.

## Proposed fix

The role check has to happen somewhere that can see the session but is not a rendering Server Component:

1. **Move the guard into middleware** — the natural analogue of the config-layer fix for the 13. `src/proxy.ts`/middleware already resolves the Supabase session, so a coach hitting `/golf/dashboard/team-hub` or `/settings/notifications` can be redirected before the route renders at all.
2. Or **stop redirecting and render for both roles.** The notifications page header explains it deliberately chose redirect over "an explanatory near-empty card … a dead end (audit W4 — no blank pages)". A coach-appropriate panel would satisfy both that audit and this bug — coaches already have working notification settings on the general Settings page.
3. Whatever the route, add these two to the existing redirect-crash regression coverage so the next page with a conditional role redirect is caught. A cheap guard: assert that no route in the app throws a `pageerror` on load for either role.

## Also verified while here (not bugs)

- `/baseball/dashboard/settings/{audit,imports,integrations}` emit a Server Components error for players **by design** — capability is enforced server-side and `error.tsx` renders the correct state ("You may not have the manage-settings capability"). Working as intended.
- `/baseball/dashboard/stats/games` produced one #310 during a full sweep but **0/14 isolated retries and 0/3 sequence replays** — not filed, unreproducible.
title: [HIGH] React #310 on 100% of coach visits to /team-hub and /settings/notifications — the known redirect-crash fix cannot cover a role-conditional redirect

body:
Found 2026-08-03 walking coach + player onboarding end-to-end against the production build on the isolated Pat Edwards demo clone.

## Read this first: NOT currently reachable

I want to be precise about severity, because the failure mode looks alarming and isn't. **No user can hit this today.** I had to manufacture the state by flipping `onboarding_completed` directly in the database.

Verified before filing:
- `grep -rn "from('golf_coaches')" src | grep insert` returns **exactly one** call site — `completeCoachOnboarding` itself.
- Every failure branch in that action rolls back completely (coach + org + team), and an outer `catch` re-runs the rollback for a throw between steps.
- Signup does **not** pre-create a `golf_coaches` row — `auth.ts` only `select`s it.
- No staff-invite flow creates coach rows.
- Live data: **zero** coaches currently have `onboarding_completed = false`.

So this is a latent fragility to harden, not an outage. Filing it because the fix is small and the failure is unrecoverable-by-the-user if anything ever does create that state.

## The fragility

`src/app/golf/actions/onboarding.ts:164-173` creates the coach profile with an unconditional insert:

```ts
const { data: coach, error: coachError } = await supabase
  .from('golf_coaches')
  .insert(coachData)
  .select('id')
  .single();

if (coachError || !coach) {
  await logServerError(`[Onboarding] Coach creation failed: ...`);
  await supabase.from('organizations').delete().eq('id', org.id);   // rollback
  return { success: false, error: 'Failed to create coach profile. Please try again.' };
}
```

If a `golf_coaches` row already exists for the user, that insert violates the unique constraint on `user_id` and the whole wizard dead-ends.

## Reproduced

With `golf_coaches.onboarding_completed` set to false for a user who already has a coach row:

1. Log in → correctly redirected to `/golf/coach`
2. Step 1 "Set up your program" — School/Organization is required and **empty** (not prefilled from the existing `organization_id`). Continue is correctly disabled until it is filled.
3. Fill it, Continue → Step 2 "Your profile" (Full Name correctly prefilled "Pat Edwards")
4. **Complete Setup → `Failed to create coach profile. Please try again.`**

Retrying does the same thing forever. Each attempt creates a fresh organization, fails on the coach insert, then deletes the org it just made — so the user is stuck with a generic "try again" that cannot ever succeed, and no way out of the wizard.

Confirmed the rollback is genuinely clean: org/team/coach/member counts were identical before and after (27/13/15/61/51), and zero rows matching the marker name I used. The code does not leak orphans.

## Suggested hardening

Make the write idempotent and prefill what already exists:

1. **Upsert instead of insert**, on the `user_id` conflict target — `completeCoachOnboarding` is semantically "make my coach profile correct and mark me onboarded", which is naturally idempotent.
2. **Prefill step 1 from the existing profile** when one is present. The player wizard already does this (it prefilled name, grad year, handicap, hometown, state for the same clone), so the two wizards behave inconsistently. Reusing the existing `organization_id` also avoids minting a second organization for a coach who already has one.
3. If the insert is kept, surface a distinguishable message for the duplicate case rather than "Please try again" — a retry loop the user cannot win is worse than an honest "your profile already exists, contact support".

## Verified working while here

Both wizards are otherwise in good shape:

- **Player (3 steps, not 4):** About you → Your profile → Done. Prefills every known field, required-field validation holds (Continue is `disabled` with First/Last cleared), completes and persists correctly (`onboarding_completed` + `profile_complete` both true, all values intact), **zero console errors**.
- **Coach (3 steps):** Program → Profile → Done. Required-field gating on School/Organization works, Full Name prefills, Men's/Women's + Division/Conference render correctly.
title: [LOW] completeCoachOnboarding INSERTs unconditionally — a pre-existing coach row would dead-end the wizard unrecoverably (latent, not reachable today)

body:
Found 2026-08-02 auditing every golf surface at phone and tablet widths against the production build.

## The layout is fine. The touch targets are not.

First, the good news, because it scopes this issue: across **15 coach routes + 10 player routes × 3 viewports** (390×844 iPhone 14 Pro, 375×667 iPhone SE, 768×1024 iPad mini) there were:

- **0** instances of horizontal overflow
- **0** console errors
- **0** navigation failures

So this is not a responsive-layout problem. It is specifically that interactive controls are sized for a mouse.

## Measured, on the production build

`/golf/dashboard/roster` at 390×844, measuring each control's own border box (padding included — what a finger actually hits):

| Control | Size | Count |
|---|---|---|
| `Set intent for <player>` | **88 × 20** | 7 — one per roster row |
| `Player status: Active. Change status` | **76 × 24** | per row |
| `Search players` (the `<input>` itself) | **314 × 20** | 1 |
| Sort headers — `Name`, `Avg score`, `Handicap`, `Rounds` | **~70 × 30** | 4 |
| `Add focus area`, `Export` | **~110 × 36** | 2 |

Team-wide, the most repeated offender is `Collapse navigation` at **24 × 24**, which appeared on 25 route/viewport combinations.

Others in the 28–30 px band, across surfaces: `View as table` (116×28), filter chips on documents/announcements/qualifiers — `Schedule`, `Tournament`, `Policy`, `Urgent`, `Has tasks`, `Practice`, `Qualifier`, `All` (all ~30 px tall), `All stats` (84×28), `View all` (81×28).

The reference floor is 44×44 CSS px (Apple HIG) / 48×48 dp (Material). A 20 px-tall button is under half of it.

## Why this one matters

`Set intent` and the status toggle are not decorative — they are the primary per-row actions on the roster, and they are **20–24 px tall stacked in a list**, which is the worst case for mis-taps: adjacent rows are within a thumb's contact patch, so a miss doesn't just do nothing, it hits the neighbouring player's control.

There is real evidence people are on touch devices: the Capacitor `Keyboard` plugin errors in `error_logs` came from actual Android sessions on `/golf/login` and `/golf/dashboard`.

## Explicitly NOT part of this

Two things my first pass flagged that are false positives, recorded so nobody re-files them:

- `Skip to main content` (32×16) — a visually-hidden skip link, only rendered on keyboard focus. Correct as-is.
- `INPUT 1x1` — a hidden file input behind a styled button. Correct as-is.

## Proposed fix

The per-row roster actions are the ones worth fixing first; the rest is a sweep.

1. Establish a minimum touch box in the Fairway primitives rather than per-call-site — a `min-h-11 min-w-11` (44 px) floor on `Button` at `size="sm"`/icon variants, or a shared `touch-target` utility that pads the hit area without changing the visual size (`::after` inset expansion is the usual trick where the visual chip must stay 30 px).
2. Fix `Set intent` and `Player status` on the roster first — highest interaction density, smallest targets.
3. Add a guard so this cannot regress: the audit that produced this table is a Playwright pass measuring `getBoundingClientRect()` on every `button, a[href], [role=button], input, select` and failing on `< 44` after excluding `sr-only`/hidden. Worth promoting into `e2e/mobile-viewports.spec.ts`, which already exists.

Note the sweep will surface the 28–30 px chips too; those are a judgement call — a filter chip is lower-stakes than a row action, and pure padding growth there would cost layout density. The `::after` hit-area expansion keeps both.
title: [MEDIUM] Roster per-row actions are 20-24px tall on phones — primary controls are half the 44px touch floor

body:
Four dev-dependency **majors** were bundled into dependabot's #1191 alongside twelve safe patch/minor bumps. The safe twelve landed in #1247 (merged); these four are held at their current ranges and each needs its own deliberate upgrade.

Filed 2026-08-02 so the blocker is recorded somewhere durable — a dependabot PR gets closed and recreated, taking its comment thread with it.

## The hard blocker: TypeScript 7

```
Error: typescript-eslint does not support TS 7.0.
```

That is the whole reason #1191 failed 14 checks. `typescript` `^5.9.3 → ^7.0.2` cannot land until `typescript-eslint` ships TS 7 support upstream — it is not a config problem on our side, and there is no local workaround short of dropping typescript-eslint, which would gut the lint rules.

**This one is externally gated. Do not retry it until typescript-eslint announces TS 7 support.**

## The four

| Package | Held at | Proposed | Why it needs its own pass |
|---|---|---|---|
| `typescript` | `^5.9.3` | `^7.0.2` | Blocked upstream (above). A language major also means new errors surface across ~900 files. |
| `jsdom` | `^28.0.0` | `^29.1.1` | The DOM test environment for the whole vitest suite. A major here can change layout/API behaviour under thousands of component tests at once. |
| `globals` | `^14.0.0` | `^17.7.0` | Three majors at once. Feeds the ESLint flat config's global declarations; a wrong set produces either phantom `no-undef` errors or silently stops catching real ones. |
| `@testing-library/jest-dom` | `^6.9.1` | `^7.0.0` | Matcher API major. Removed/renamed matchers fail loudly, which is fine — but the blast radius is every assertion using them. |

## Suggested order

1. **`@testing-library/jest-dom` 7** — smallest, self-contained, failures are loud and local.
2. **`globals` 17** — lint-only; verify by diffing `npm run lint` output before/after rather than trusting a clean exit.
3. **`jsdom` 29** — run the full suite plus the timezone-shifted shards; that is where DOM-env regressions showed up last time.
4. **`typescript` 7** — only once `typescript-eslint` supports it. Expect real work.

One at a time, each with its own PR. The reason #1191 failed is precisely that they were bundled: one hard blocker took twelve unrelated, healthy bumps down with it.

## Context

- #1247 — the twelve safe bumps, merged (`360290346`)
- #1191 — the original bundle, closed in favour of this issue
