body:
Found 2026-08-02 while automating a login against the local dev server. Not specific to automation — it is a real hydration race, automation just hits the window reliably.

## Filling the login form before hydration completes submits an empty email

Sequence:

1. Navigate to `/golf/login`, wait for `input[type=email]` to exist.
2. Fill email + password. Verified in the DOM immediately afterwards:
   `{ email: 'rinin376@gmail.com', pwLen: 13, btn: [{ t: 'Sign in', dis: false }] }`
3. Click **Sign in**.
4. Page returns **"Invalid email or password"**.

The credentials were correct — the identical pair signs in fine when the form is filled a couple of seconds later. What actually reached the server was an empty email, which `login_attempts` recorded verbatim:

```
 email | failed_attempts | last_attempt                  | last_user_agent
-------+-----------------+-------------------------------+------------------------------
 ''    |        1        | 2026-08-02 16:43:38.503+00    | …HeadlessChrome/150.0.0.0…
```

A blank-email row in `login_attempts` is the fingerprint. Adding a settle delay plus a re-read of the input values before clicking makes it pass every time, which confirms the diagnosis: the fill lands on the pre-hydration DOM, React hydrates and resets the controlled inputs to their initial empty state, and the submit carries the empty state.

## Why it matters beyond automation

- A fast typist on a cold/slow page load — first visit, no warm cache, poor connection — can plausibly type and hit Enter inside the same window and get a spurious "Invalid email or password". They retype it, it works, and they conclude the app is flaky.
- It is **misattributed as a credential failure**. The user is told their password is wrong when the app dropped the input.
- It **pollutes the lockout ledger**. These land in `login_attempts` under a blank email, so the failure is not counted against the right identity — and that bucket accumulates failures across every user who hits the race. Given the lockout is 10 failures / 30 min and is shared across golf + baseball, a shared junk bucket is the wrong place for them.

## Proposed fix

Any of these, cheapest first:

1. Disable the submit button (or the whole fieldset) until the client component has mounted — a `useEffect`-set `hydrated` flag. The form is already a client component; this is a few lines and makes the race unhittable.
2. Guard the submit handler: if email or password is empty, don't call the server action — surface an inline field error instead of a credential failure. This also stops the bogus `login_attempts` rows.
3. Server side, reject empty-email submissions before they reach the attempt ledger, so the blank bucket never accrues failures.

(1) + (2) together fix both the user-facing symptom and the ledger pollution.

## Note for anyone writing e2e against this

`page.fill()` immediately after `waitForSelector` is not sufficient on this form. Fill, wait, re-read the input values, and only then click — otherwise the spec fails intermittently with "Invalid email or password" against perfectly good credentials.
title: [MEDIUM] Login form hydration race submits an empty email — user is told "Invalid email or password" and the failure is logged against a blank identity

body:
Found 2026-08-02 while testing the focus-area / goal progress loop on the demo account (player Cole Bennett).

## Goals created by the auto flow have no baseline, so their (correct) progress bar can't render

`FairwayGoalCard` computes progress the right way — `(current - baseline) / (target - baseline)`, with an honest "Not started — baseline captured" state (`src/components/fairway/pages/coachhelm/FairwayGoalCard.tsx:160-190`). But it bails first:

```ts
if (g.baseline_value === null || g.target_value === null || g.current_value === null) {
  return null;   // no percentage at all
}
```

Cole Bennett's only active goal:

```
title                          | metric_id            | baseline_value | current_value | target_value | state
Goal — putts_made_3_5ft_pct    | putts_made_3_5ft_pct | NULL           | 46.5          | 68.5         | active
```

and the card renders `Baseline —  ·  Now 47%  ·  Target 69%` with no progress indicator.

## Scale

```sql
select state, count(*), count(*) filter (where baseline_value is null) from golf_goals group by state;
```

```
 state    | goals | null baseline
----------+-------+---------------
 missed   |  16   |      8
 achieved |   2   |      0
 active   |   1   |      1
```

**9 of 19 goals** (and the only currently-active one) have no baseline. The pattern is clear from the titles: hand-authored/seeded goals ("Short Putting Consistency (3-6 feet)", "Wedge Distance Control (80-120 yards)") carry baselines of 82 and 28; auto-generated ones titled `Goal — <metric_id>` all have `baseline_value = NULL`.

So the whole class of goals the system creates for itself is the class that can't show progress.

## Cause

Whatever path emits the `Goal — <metric_id>` rows sets `target_value` and `started_at` but never captures the player's observed value at creation into `baseline_value`. The reading is available at that moment — it is the same `loadPlayerStandingMap` value the evaluator reads on its very next pass — it is just not persisted.

Note the evaluator itself is fine: it writes `current_value` + appends a snapshot, and correctly leaves `baseline_value` alone.

## Proposed fix

1. At goal creation, capture the current observed standing/windowed value into `baseline_value` (same instant `started_at` is stamped). If no reading exists yet, leave it null and let the card keep its honest empty state — do **not** substitute the target or zero.
2. Backfill the 9 existing rows where a first snapshot exists: `snapshots[0].value` is the earliest observed reading and is a defensible baseline. For rows with no snapshots, leave null.
3. Consider a not-null-once-started constraint, or at least a guard test, so an auto-created goal can't ship without one.

Related: #1240 — the mirror-image problem on focus areas, which have the write path but **no baseline column at all**. Fixing both together would let the two surfaces finally share one progress formula.
title: [LOW] Auto-created goals have baseline_value = NULL — 9 of 19 goals (incl. the only active one) render no progress bar at all

body:
Found 2026-08-02 running the full coach-prescribes → player-accepts → player-plays loop on the demo account (coach `njrini99@`, player Cole Bennett).

## Finishing a round does not move any focus area or goal — you have to wait for tomorrow

Reproduced end to end:

1. Coach prescribed **"Fairway accuracy off the tee"** for Cole Bennett — `fairways_hit_pct`, current **61**, target **66**. Row lands `status='proposed'`, `started_at=null`. ✅
2. Cole accepted it from "Prescribed for you" → `status='active'`, `started_at=2026-08-02 16:36:47Z`. ✅
3. Cole played **two complete 18-hole rounds** through the real round-entry wizard, both dated today, both `status='completed'`, both with a populated `golf_round_stats_cache` row:

```
round_id   | total_score | fairways_hit | fairways_total
d00fd97f…  |     70      |      12      |      14
10cbccd9…  |     71      |      11      |      14
```

Pooled that is 23/28 = **82.1%**, comfortably past the 66 target.

4. Reloaded the player card **and** the coach board. Both still showed:

> Fairways Hit % — Now **61** → Target **66**

and the DB agreed — `current_value` still `61`, `updated_at` still the acceptance timestamp. Nothing had moved.

5. Invoked `POST /api/cron/v3/standing-refresh` by hand with the `CRON_SECRET`:

```json
{ "stale_caches_refreshed": 2, "goals_progressed": 1, "focus_areas_progressed": 1 }
```

`current_value` immediately became **82** — the correct windowed figure — and both surfaces then rendered `Now 82 → Target 66`.

**The engine is correct. It is simply never invoked except once a night.**

## Cause

`grep -rn "runFocusAreaProgressForPlayers\|runGoalProgressForPlayers\|evaluateAndPersistGoals\|evaluateAndPersistFocusAreas" src` finds exactly **one** non-test caller:

```
src/app/api/cron/v3/standing-refresh/route.ts:392  const summary      = await runGoalProgressForPlayers(goalPlayerIds);
src/app/api/cron/v3/standing-refresh/route.ts:397  const focusSummary = await runFocusAreaProgressForPlayers(goalPlayerIds);
```

scheduled in `vercel.json` at `"20 2 * * *"` — 02:20 UTC, once a day.

Neither the round-submit path nor the page render drives it:

- `postRoundTrigger` (`src/lib/coachhelm/v2/post-round-trigger.ts`) never touches `golf_player_focus_areas` or `golf_goals` — `grep` for either returns nothing.
- No Inngest function references the drivers.
- `submitGolfRoundComprehensive` does `revalidatePath('/golf/dashboard/coachhelm')` etc. (`golf.ts:2044-2052`) — so the pages re-render, but they re-render the same stale numbers.

The two page-view hooks that used to exist were removed deliberately, and there is now a test locking that in (`src/app/golf/actions/__tests__/player-coachhelm-dashboard-readonly.test.ts:57-60`):

```ts
it('does not recompute and persist progress as a side effect of rendering the player route', () => {
  expect(playerRouteSource).not.toContain('evaluateAndPersistGoals');
  expect(playerRouteSource).not.toContain('evaluateAndPersistFocusAreas');
});
```

That removal was right on its own terms — a GET should not write, and the sibling `persistPatterns: false` change in the same spec exists because a page-read write raced the coachhelm crons into a live 40P01 deadlock. **The problem is that nothing replaced it.** The design moved from "3 triggers" (coach page view, player page view, nightly cron) down to one, and the one that remains is the slowest.

## Net effect

The core promise of the feature — "accept this and we'll track it for you" — is up to ~24 h behind. A player finishes a round, opens My Development to see whether it helped, and the bar has not moved. A coach checking in after practice sees the same stale number. The most likely reading from either seat is that the feature is broken.

It also makes the Program-pulse "N active focus areas have no recent progress" banner noisier than it should be, since freshly-improved areas stay stale-looking until the next morning.

## Proposed fix

Drive it from the **round submit**, which is the real state change and is already a write path (so it reintroduces none of the read-path-writes problem the removal was guarding against):

- In the existing post-submit background work in `submitGolfRoundComprehensive` — right beside the `postRoundTrigger(admin, …)` call, which already runs under the admin client with the player id in scope — call `evaluateAndPersistGoals(playerId)` + `evaluateAndPersistFocusAreas(playerId)`, then revalidate. Both are idempotent and same-day deduped, so this composes safely with the nightly cron rather than replacing it.
- Alternatively route it through Inngest alongside the other post-round work, if the concern is keeping submit latency flat — the drivers are two queries plus a small update per area.

Keep the nightly cron as the durability net for players who improve without submitting anything (standing recomputes, team-average shifts).

Related: #1239 (most areas carry an unrecognised metric so they would not move even with a prompt trigger), #1240, #1242.
title: [HIGH] Focus-area and goal progress only advances on the nightly cron — finishing a round moves nothing until the next day

body:
Found 2026-08-02 during an end-to-end focus-area test on the demo account (coach `njrini99@`, player Cole Bennett).

## A player 56% worse than target sees a full progress bar reading "100% there"

No setup needed — this is live on the demo data right now. Cole Bennett's active focus area:

```
title                                 | target_metric         | current_value | target_value | status
Wedge Distance Control (80-120 yards) | Avg proximity 80-120y | 28            | 18           | active
```

Proximity is lower-is-better: 28 ft against an 18 ft target means he is **56% worse** than the objective, and the value has not moved since April. Both surfaces render it as complete:

- player — `/golf/dashboard/coachhelm?view=development`
- coach — `/golf/dashboard/intelligence?view=players&playersTab=areas`

> Avg proximity 80-120y — Now **28** → Target **18** — **100% there**

progress bar full, `aria-label="Avg proximity 80-120y: 100% toward target"`.

## Cause

`getProgressPercent` (`src/components/fairway/pages/coachhelm/areaTypes.ts:367`) picks its formula from `isLowerIsBetter`:

```ts
if (isLowerIsBetter(targetMetric)) {
  if (current <= target) return 100;
  return Math.round((target / current) * 100);          // 18/28 -> 64%  (correct)
}
if (target < 0) return 0;
return Math.min(100, Math.round((current / target) * 100));  // 28/18 -> 156 -> clamped to 100
```

`isLowerIsBetter` (`areaTypes.ts:321`) resolves in three steps and `'Avg proximity 80-120y'` fails all three:

1. `getMetricRenderConfig(...)` → null — not a v3 registry id
2. `findMetric(...)` → null — the catalog's entry is label `Proximity to Hole` / key `proximity`, so the legacy free-text label does not match
3. keyword fallback — `LOWER_IS_BETTER_KEYWORDS` (`areaTypes.ts:291`) is `['putt','penalty','bogey','score','three_putt']`; none appear in the string

→ returns `false`, the metric is treated as higher-is-better, and **being further from the target makes the bar fuller**. The clamp at 100 hides how wrong it is: anything ≥ the target value reads as done.

The docblock above `isLowerIsBetter` describes it as "a real direction lookup against the canonical registries, NOT a naive keyword guess" — which is true for the first two steps, but step 3 still is a keyword guess, and its default when everything misses is the unsafe direction.

## Blast radius

Every lower-is-better focus area whose `target_metric` resolves in neither registry. Live today:

```
target_metric          | active areas | actual direction
avg_proximity_ft       |      2       | lower is better -> INVERTED
Avg proximity 80-120y  |      1       | lower is better -> INVERTED
```

Three of the fifteen active areas team-wide. The failure is silent and confident: a coach scanning the development board sees a completed objective, and the player sees the same. This is worse than the area simply not tracking (#1239) — it reports the opposite of the truth.

## Proposed fix

Two parts, both worth doing:

1. **Make the unknown case safe.** When direction cannot be resolved, do not render a directional bar at all — show the `Now → Target` pair with no percentage, the same way an area with no target renders "No target set yet". Defaulting to higher-is-better is a coin flip that is currently landing wrong for every proximity metric. A missing bar is recoverable; a confidently wrong one is not.
2. **Widen the keyword net** as a stopgap — `proximity`, `distance`, `dispersion`, `avg_prox` — and normalize the legacy free-text ids onto catalog keys so step 2 starts hitting (#1239).

Worth adding a table-driven unit test over the distinct `target_metric` values actually present in the DB, asserting the resolved direction matches the metric's real direction.

Related: #1240 (the same function computes a ratio rather than progress from baseline), #1239 (these exact ids also never auto-track).
title: [HIGH] Focus-area progress bar inverts for unrecognized lower-is-better metrics — a player 56% worse than target renders "100% there"

body:
Found 2026-08-02 during an end-to-end focus-area test on the demo account (coach `njrini99@`, player Cole Bennett).

## The Trend cell on a focus area is always "—"

Every focus-area card — coach board and player card alike — renders:

> Trend **—**  (`aria-label="Progress trend for <title>: not enough data"`)

This is true even for an area that has demonstrably moved. The test area "Fairway accuracy off the tee" went from `current_value` 61 → 82 after two completed rounds, and the card still showed Trend **—** on both surfaces afterwards.

## Cause

Focus areas persist a **scalar** and nothing else. The tracker writes only:

```ts
.update({ current_value: next, updated_at: nowIso })   // progress-drivers.ts, evaluateAreas
```

There is no history column on `golf_player_focus_areas` — no `snapshots`, no time series — so there is literally nothing for a trend to be computed from. The "not enough data" copy is accurate; it will just never become anything else.

Goals, by contrast, carry `golf_goals.snapshots jsonb` and the evaluator appends a dated, same-day-deduped entry on every pass (`src/lib/coachhelm/v3/goals/evaluator.ts`), which is what lets `FairwayGoalCard.tsx:198` draw a real trajectory.

## Net effect

Low severity on its own — the number is correct, only the trajectory is missing. But it removes the one signal that would tell a coach *which direction* an area is moving, which is the whole point of a development plan. It also compounds #1239: an area that can never track and an area that is tracking well look identical in the Trend column.

## Proposed fix

Mirror the goals model: add a `snapshots jsonb` column to `golf_player_focus_areas` and have `evaluateAreas` append `{ date, value }` (same-day deduped) alongside the `current_value` write. Both paths already run in the same function, so this is a small addition rather than new infrastructure — and it would give the coach board a real sparkline instead of an em dash.

If a full history is unwanted, even a `previous_value` + `previous_value_at` pair would let the card show direction, which is most of the value.

Related: #1239, #1240 (focus areas also lack the `baseline_value` that goals have — same underlying "focus areas have a thinner state model than goals" theme).
title: [LOW] Focus-area Trend is permanently "—" — areas persist only a scalar current_value, with no snapshot history to trend
[MEDIUM] Focus-area progress bar is current/target, not progress from baseline — a new area reads "92% there" on day zero

body:
Found 2026-08-02 during an end-to-end focus-area test on the demo account (coach `njrini99@`, player Cole Bennett).

## 8 of the 10 targeted active focus areas can never move

`golf_player_focus_areas.target_metric` is free text, and the auto-tracker recognises exactly two namespaces (`src/lib/golf/progress-drivers.ts`, `evaluateAreas`):

1. **legacy catalog** — `isWindowableFocusMetric()`, i.e. one of the 7 keys in `WINDOWABLE_FOCUS_METRIC_KEYS` (`src/lib/coachhelm/focus-areas/catalog.ts:215`), matched by key **or** display label
2. **v3 registry standing fallback** — `isMetricId()` from `src/lib/coachhelm/v3/metrics/registry.ts`

Anything in neither namespace is skipped forever — deliberately, and honestly (the driver never fabricates a value). The problem is how much of the live data lands there:

```sql
select target_metric, count(*) from golf_player_focus_areas
where status = 'active' group by target_metric order by 2 desc;
```

```
 target_metric          | active | recognised by
------------------------+--------+----------------------------------
 (null)                 |   5    | n/a — no target set
 three_putt_chain       |   3    | NEITHER
 make_pct_5_10          |   2    | NEITHER
 avg_proximity_ft       |   2    | NEITHER
 putts_made_3_5ft_pct   |   1    | v3 registry  ✅
 Avg proximity 80-120y  |   1    | NEITHER (catalog label is "Proximity to Hole")
 fairways_hit_pct       |   1    | catalog key  ✅
```

Confirmed absent from the v3 registry:

```
$ for m in three_putt_chain make_pct_5_10 avg_proximity_ft putts_made_3_5ft_pct fairways_hit_pct; do
    grep -c "'$m'" src/lib/coachhelm/v3/metrics/registry.ts; done
three_putt_chain      -> 0
make_pct_5_10         -> 0
avg_proximity_ft      -> 0
putts_made_3_5ft_pct  -> 1
fairways_hit_pct      -> 0   (but IS a catalog windowable key)
```

So of 15 active focus areas team-wide, 5 have no metric at all and 8 of the remaining 10 carry an id that matches nothing. **Two are trackable.**

## Net effect

This is exactly what the coach Program-pulse banner reports:

> **8 active focus areas have no recent progress**
> Cole Bennett — Lag putts → 3-putt cascade · Cole Bennett — 3-5 ft putting: 47% · Cole Bennett — Wedge Distance Control (80-120 yards)

The banner is telling the truth; it is surfacing a broken pipeline rather than coach neglect. A coach prescribes an area from an insight, the player accepts it, and the bar is frozen at whatever value was captured at creation for the rest of its life.

Nothing in the current tree writes `avg_proximity_ft`, `make_pct_5_10` or `three_putt_chain` — `grep -rn` across `src/` finds no producer. They are legacy/seeded values, or come from an insight-prescription path that has since been removed. The canonical spellings that *would* resolve are e.g. `putt_make_pct_5_10ft` / `approach_proximity_average`.

## Proposed fix

1. **Backfill** the orphaned ids onto canonical ones (`avg_proximity_ft` + `Avg proximity 80-120y` → the registry proximity id; `make_pct_5_10` → `putts_made_5_10ft_pct`; `three_putt_chain` has no scalar equivalent — it is a narrative insight, so it should carry a null metric and render "No target set yet" instead of pretending).
2. **Constrain the write path.** `target_metric` should be validated against the union of the two namespaces at insert time — any create flow (coach modal, player self-create, `createFocusAreaFromInsight*`) should either resolve to a known id or store `null`. A silently unrecognised id is indistinguishable in the UI from a working one.
3. Add a cheap guard test asserting every distinct non-null `target_metric` in the DB resolves via `findMetric()` or `isMetricId()`, so this cannot silently regrow.

## Verified working

The two recognised areas track correctly. A focus area on `fairways_hit_pct` created and accepted during this test moved from 61 → 82 after two rounds, windowed to exactly the rounds played since `started_at` (pooled 23/28 = 82.14% → 82) rather than the diluted 15-round career average. The engine is right; the vocabulary feeding it is not.
title: [MEDIUM] 8 of 10 targeted active focus areas can never track — target_metric holds ids that match neither the catalog nor the v3 registry

body:
Filed for visibility after testing the Tasks surface on 2026-08-02: recurring tasks were on the test list and turn out not to exist at all.

## Current state

- `golf_tasks` has no recurrence columns: `id, team_id, assigned_by, assigned_to, title, description, task_type, due_date, status, completed_at, priority, created_at, updated_at, reminder_at, reminder_type, reminder_sent, category`
- `grep -n "recurr\|rrule\|repeat" src/app/golf/actions/tasks.ts` -> no matches
- The Create task dialog has no repeat control (Title, Description, Due date, Reminder, Assign to only)

So a coach who wants "log 3 putting sessions, every week" has to create the task manually each week.

## Worth noting: the pattern already exists next door

Recurring **events** are fully implemented — `src/app/golf/actions/recurring-events.ts`, with tests (`recurring-events.test.ts`). Whatever recurrence model that uses (and its expansion/instantiation strategy) is the obvious template for tasks, rather than inventing a second one.

`golf_task_templates` also exists, but templates are a different thing — a reusable definition you instantiate on demand, not a schedule.

## Suggested scope if picked up

1. Recurrence fields on `golf_tasks` (or a `golf_task_recurrences` table) matching whatever shape `recurring-events.ts` settled on.
2. Repeat control in the Create/Edit dialog.
3. Instantiation — decide up front whether instances are materialised ahead of time (like the events path) or generated lazily, and make sure per-instance completion in `golf_task_assignments` stays scoped to the instance.
4. Interaction with reminders: each instance needs its own `golf_task_reminders` row. See #1231 — the reminder path is currently completion-blind, and recurrence would multiply that.

Not urgent; filing so it is tracked rather than rediscovered.
title: [FEATURE GAP] Recurring tasks are not supported — no recurrence columns, no UI, no expansion logic

body:
Small user-visible defects collected during the 2026-08-02 in-browser test matrix. Grouped because each is a one-line fix.

## 1. Pluralization — "1 players", "1 expenses"

- Announcements list: an announcement targeted at one player renders **"1 players"** on the card. The compose dialog gets it right ("1 player selected") — only the card is wrong.
- Travel expenses panel: a trip with one expense renders **"1 expenses"** under Total Expenses.

Both need the same conditional-plural treatment already used elsewhere in the codebase (e.g. `${n} round${n === 1 ? '' : 's'}` in `golf.ts`).

## 2. New Round offers to restore a draft with zero holes

Starting a fresh round pops the recovery modal:

> **Recover Unsaved Progress?**
> Found locally saved data with **0 completed holes**. This data may have been saved when the app was interrupted.
> [Discard] [Restore]

Offering to restore nothing is pure friction on an otherwise clean start, and it trains players to dismiss a dialog that matters when it has real data in it. Suppress the prompt when the recovered draft has 0 completed holes (just discard silently), or at minimum don't offer "Restore" for an empty draft.

## 3. "Action needed" badge persists on an acknowledged announcement

After a player acknowledges an ack-required announcement, the card correctly flips its counter to `1/1 ack` and the **filter chips** for `Unread` and `Action needed` disappear — but the **"Action needed" badge on the card itself** remains. The card simultaneously reads "Action needed" and "1/1 ack".

Badge should clear once the viewing player's own acknowledgement is recorded.

## 4. Approach miss grid: two buttons both render the letter "L"

In the approach miss-direction 3×3 grid, `↑ L` (Long) and `← L` (Left) both display "L"; only the arrow glyph distinguishes them. The `aria-label`s are correct ("Long", "Left"), so this is visual only — but at a glance in the field the two are easy to confuse. Consider `Lg`/`Lft`, or dropping the letter and relying on the arrow plus position.

---

All four verified in-browser on Demo University Golf as coach and as Cole Bennett.
title: [LOW] UI polish batch: "1 players" / "1 expenses" pluralization, recovery prompt offering an empty draft, stale "Action needed" badge after acknowledgement

body:
Found 2026-08-02 testing messaging in both roles.

## What happens

The coach↔Cole Bennett direct message thread renders its header as:

```
Cole Bennett
Group conversation
```

Both roles see it — coach side and player side (the player's view also lists the single other participant, "NR Nick Rini", underneath the "Group conversation" label, which makes the mislabel obvious).

## Evidence

```sql
select c.id, c.title, c.is_team_chat, c.is_team_channel,
       (select count(*) from golf_conversation_participants p
        where p.conversation_id = c.id) n
from golf_conversations c where c.id = '3e20827b-…';
```

```
title: "Cole Bennett" | is_team_chat: true | is_team_channel: false | n: 2
```

## Correction to the original diagnosis — the write path is NOT at fault

This issue originally proposed fixing `createGolfConversation`. That was wrong, and reading the code disproves it:

- `createConversation` (`src/app/actions/messages.ts:307`) never sets `is_team_chat` at all. Its own comment says so explicitly: *"a DM sets neither flag (only `createGolfTeamBroadcast` does, which is exactly why broadcasts worked and coach→player DMs did not)"*.
- The flag comes from **`createGolfTeamBroadcast`** (`messages.ts:790`), which sets `is_team_chat: true` and uses `title` as the thread name. A broadcast addressed to exactly ONE player therefore produces a two-person thread carrying the group flag and titled with that player's name — precisely the row observed.

And the flag cannot simply be dropped there: `is_team_chat = true` is load-bearing for the conversation-create RLS workaround documented at `messages.ts:288-306` — it is one of the disjuncts in `golf_conversations_select_v2` that lets the creating coach satisfy the SELECT policy on `RETURNING`. Removing it would reintroduce the 42501 that workaround exists to prevent.

So there is nothing wrong with the stored data, and **no backfill is warranted**. The defect is that the UI treats `is_team_chat` as "is a group", which it is not.

## Fix applied

`src/components/fairway/pages/messages/MessageThreadPane.tsx` — derive the subtitle from the participant count instead of the flag:

- `> 2` participants → "Group conversation"
- `== 2` → "Direct message"
- unknown (0) → no subtitle, rather than guessing

`headerName` is deliberately left on `conversation.title`: broadcast-derived rows carry empty `participant_ids`/`participant_names`, so flipping `is_group` itself (in `use-golf-messages.ts`, where it is hardcoded `true` for every `is_team_chat` row) would make the header fall through to "Unknown User" — strictly worse.
title: [LOW] 1:1 direct messages are labelled "Group conversation" (is_team_chat=true on a 2-participant DM)

body:
Surfaced 2026-08-02 from a `severity: error` server log while exercising the app against production Supabase.

## The log

```
[ServerErrorLogger] { severity: error,
  traceMessage: "[RateLimit] check_rate_limit_atomic is not deployed … 
                 y 20260801100000_auth_rate_limits_atomic_rpc.sql.",
  action: checkRateLimit }
```

## Confirmed against production

```sql
select p.proname
from pg_proc p join pg_namespace n on n.oid = p.pronamespace
where p.proname = 'check_rate_limit_atomic' and n.nspname = 'public';
-- []  (zero rows)
```

The function is absent. Migration `20260801100000_auth_rate_limits_atomic_rpc.sql` exists in the repo but has not been applied to prod.

## Why it matters

- `checkRateLimit` is falling back on every invocation and emitting at `severity: error`, so this is generating continuous error-log/Sentry noise that will mask real auth failures.
- The migration name says *atomic* — the point of the RPC is to make the check-and-increment a single atomic operation. Running on the fallback means the limiter is presumably a non-atomic read-then-write and is racy under concurrent attempts, which is exactly the property an auth rate limiter needs. Related in kind to #1207 (LLM budget check-then-act race).

This is also consistent with the existing note that `login_attempts` lockout (10 failures / 30 min) is shared across golf + baseball and localhost + prod — the limiter is load-bearing for the real account.

## Proposed fix

Apply `20260801100000_auth_rate_limits_atomic_rpc.sql` to production (Supabase MCP `apply_migration`), then re-verify:

```sql
select proname from pg_proc p join pg_namespace n on n.oid=p.pronamespace
where proname='check_rate_limit_atomic' and nspname='public';
```

and confirm the `checkRateLimit` error stops appearing.

Worth a quick audit for siblings while there — this is the second time recently that prod has been found missing objects the migrations create (per the "grep migrations before authoring one" lesson: prod being broken means a fix is *unapplied*, not absent). `supabase migration list` against prod would show whether `20260801100000` is the only one outstanding.
title: [MEDIUM] check_rate_limit_atomic RPC does not exist in production — migration 20260801100000 is unapplied and auth rate limiting is degraded

body:
Found 2026-08-02 after submitting a round and reconciling the player stats cache.

## What happens

After a round submit, Cole Bennett's cache row read:

```
rounds_in_calculation: 16
round_ids_included:    [<the one round just submitted>]   -- length 1
```

Every aggregate on the row (`scoring_average` 75.53, `putts_per_round` 32.90, `fairways_hit/total` 131/212) was computed over all 16 rounds, but the column that claims to record which rounds went into the calculation listed one.

## Root cause

`round_ids_included` shares a variable with `rounds_this_season` inside the `update_player_stats_complete()` trigger:

```sql
v_season_start := make_date(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(MONTH FROM CURRENT_DATE) >= 8
                            THEN EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CURRENT_DATE)::INTEGER
                            ELSE (EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CURRENT_DATE) - 1)::INTEGER END, 8, 1);

SELECT COUNT(*), ARRAY_AGG(rsc.round_id ORDER BY r.round_date DESC)
INTO   v_rounds_this_season, v_round_ids
FROM   golf_round_stats_cache rsc
JOIN   golf_rounds r ON r.id = rsc.round_id
WHERE  rsc.player_id = v_player_id AND r.round_date >= v_season_start;
```

So it is a **season** list, not a calculation list. Today is 2026-08-02 and the season boundary is 2026-08-01, so only the brand-new round qualified — hence 1 vs 16.

Confirmed both directions:
- `rounds_this_season` was also 1 on the same row.
- After deleting the test round, the recomputed row reads `rounds_this_season: 0`, `round_ids_included: {}` (length 0), `rounds_in_calculation: 15`.

## Why it looked like a bug worth chasing

The column's `COMMENT` asserts the opposite of what it holds:

```
COMMENT ON COLUMN public.golf_player_stats_cache.round_ids_included
  IS 'Array of round IDs included in the calculation for verification';
```

Control across all players: every other cache row has `array_length(round_ids_included) == rounds_in_calculation` (12/12, 15/15, 11/11, 16/16 …). That equality holds only because those players happen to have all their rounds inside the current season window — it is coincidence, not invariant. Two rows already diverge (16 vs 1, and one player at 11 vs 0), and **every** row will diverge as the 2026-27 season fills in.

## Blast radius

Low: `grep -rn "round_ids_included" src --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx` returns only the generated `database.ts` type. No application code reads it. The cost is purely that a column explicitly labelled "for verification" cannot be used to verify anything, and anyone debugging a stats-cache discrepancy will be misled by it.

## Proposed fix

Pick one:

- **(a)** Rename to `season_round_ids` and correct the `COMMENT` to say season-scoped. Cheapest, matches actual behavior.
- **(b)** If provenance is genuinely wanted, add a second `ARRAY_AGG` over the same population `rounds_in_calculation` counts and store that, leaving the season array alone.

(a) unless someone actually wants the provenance.

## Adjacent note (probably not worth fixing)

`golf_player_stats_cache` is only refreshed by a trigger on `golf_round_stats_cache`, so deleting a row straight out of `golf_rounds` leaves the player cache stale. I hit this during cleanup and had to force a recompute by touching a `golf_round_stats_cache` row. Not reachable from the product — `deleteInProgressRound` only handles in-progress rounds — but it will bite anyone doing manual data surgery.
title: [LOW] golf_player_stats_cache.round_ids_included is season-scoped, not calculation provenance — its name and COMMENT are both wrong

body:
Found 2026-08-02 adding an expense to the Palmetto Qualifier itinerary as coach.

Entered one expense: description `QA TEST EXPENSE`, amount `123.45`, vendor `QA Vendor`, date `2026-07-08`, paid by Team.

## Bug 1 — expense date is off by one in the UI

The stored row is correct:

```
expense_date: 2026-07-08   amount: 123.45
```

The Expenses panel renders it as **"Jul 7, 2026"**.

The CSV export is also correct, which localises the fault precisely to the display layer:

```csv
Date,Category,Description,Vendor,Amount,Paid By,Notes
2026-07-08,other,"QA TEST EXPENSE — delete me","QA Vendor",123.45,team,""
```

Classic date-only/UTC bug: `new Date('2026-07-08')` parses as UTC midnight and renders as Jul 7 20:00 in EDT. Every expense will read a day early for any negative-UTC-offset user — i.e. every US user.

There is already a helper for exactly this pattern elsewhere in the repo — `parseLocalDate` in `src/app/baseball/(dashboard)/dashboard/dev-plan/DevPlanClient.tsx`, whose comment reads *"Parses a date-only 'YYYY-MM-DD' string as LOCAL midnight (not UTC midnight), avoiding the off-by-one."* Worth promoting to a shared util and using it here.

## Bug 2 — money totals are rounded to whole dollars

With the single $123.45 expense, the panel shows:

- **Total Expenses: `$123`** ("1 expenses")
- Breakdown by Category -> Other: `$123`
- Payment Status -> Team Paid: `$123`

while the line item itself correctly shows `$123.45`.

Cents are dropped from every aggregate. This is a budget/reimbursement surface, so the drift is real: 20 expenses averaging ~50c of truncation is ~$10 off, and the number a coach reads as "Total Expenses" will not reconcile against the CSV or against receipts.

## Proposed fix

1. Parse `expense_date` as local midnight (shared `parseLocalDate` util) before formatting.
2. Format currency aggregates with 2 decimals — sum in cents (integer) or use `Intl.NumberFormat(..., { style:'currency', currency:'USD' })` on the exact sum, rather than rounding to whole dollars.

## Verified working, for contrast

- Expense create persists correctly (amount, category, vendor, date, `paid_by`, itinerary link).
- CSV export is correct and properly quoted, with a trip header row and a sensible filename.
- The Details/Expenses tab switch works (an earlier apparent failure was a synthetic-click artifact, not a bug).

## Minor, same surface

"1 expenses" should be "1 expense" — same pluralization gap as the announcements card ("1 players"). Bundled in the polish issue.
title: [MEDIUM] Travel expenses: date renders one day early and totals silently drop cents

Found 2026-08-02 creating a task as coach on Demo University Golf.

## What happens

The Tasks page has a category filter bar (`All categories · administrative · compliance · development · practice · preparation · travel`) and task cards render a category badge. But the **Create a task** dialog has no category field — its only inputs are Title, Description, Due date, Reminder, and Assign to (All team members / Specific players).

So every task created through the UI lands with `category = NULL` and can never match any filter.

## Evidence

Created one task through the dialog, then counted its occurrences in the DOM under each filter:

| filter | task visible |
|---|---|
| All categories | **yes** |
| administrative | no |
| compliance | no |
| development | no |
| practice | no |
| preparation | no |
| travel | no |

DB confirms `category: null`. Category is only ever written when a task is instantiated from a template — `src/app/golf/actions/tasks.ts:1039`:

```ts
category: template.category,
```

`createTask` itself never sets it.

There is also no "Uncategorized" / "No category" filter option, so a coach who filters by anything loses **all** hand-created tasks with no indication they exist. On this team that is silent — the count chips (`All 10 / Active 7 / Completed 3`) do not change when a filter is applied, so nothing signals that rows were dropped.

## Proposed fix

Pick one:

- **(a)** Add a category selector to the Create/Edit task dialog, defaulting to none, using the same six values the filter bar offers. `updateTask` already supports `updates.category` (`tasks.ts:860`), so the edit path is half-built already.
- **(b)** If categories are meant to be template-only, remove the filter bar for non-template tasks, or add an explicit "Uncategorized" chip so filtered-out tasks are discoverable.

(a) is the better fit given the filter UI already exists and edit already accepts the field.

## Adjacent gap (separate, filed for visibility)

There is no recurring-task support at all: `golf_tasks` has no recurrence columns (`id, team_id, assigned_by, assigned_to, title, description, task_type, due_date, status, completed_at, priority, created_at, updated_at, reminder_at, reminder_type, reminder_sent, category`) and `grep -n "recurr\|rrule\|repeat" src/app/golf/actions/tasks.ts` returns nothing. Recurring **events** exist (`recurring-events.ts`); recurring tasks do not.
title: [MEDIUM] Tasks created from the UI get no category, so they are invisible under every category filter

body:
Found 2026-08-02 creating a task as coach and completing it as the assigned player.

## Two defects that compound

**1. `golf_tasks.status` is never rolled up from its assignments.**

Created a task assigned to one player, with a due date of 2026-08-09 and a reminder at 2026-08-08 09:00. The player marked it complete. Result:

```
title                     | task_status | assignment_status | completed_at
QA TEST TASK — delete me  | pending     | completed         | 2026-08-02 12:08:05+00
```

Every assignment on the task is `completed` (1 of 1, UI shows "Completed / 100%"), but the parent `golf_tasks.status` stays `pending` forever. The task list derives its badge from assignment progress, so the UI looks right — the column is just dead and misleading.

**2. The reminder path has zero completion awareness.**

`getDueReminders` (`src/app/golf/actions/task-reminders.ts:449-457`) filters on exactly two things:

```ts
.from('golf_task_reminders')
.select(`*, task:golf_tasks(*)`)
.eq('sent', false)
.lte('scheduled_for', new Date().toISOString())
```

No filter on task status, no filter on assignment status. `grep -n "completed\|status" src/app/golf/actions/task-reminders.ts` returns **nothing** — the whole file is completion-blind, and so is `/api/cron/task-reminders`.

## Net effect

A player who completes a task before its reminder date still gets the reminder email + push on the scheduled date. My test task is the live proof: assignment completed 2026-08-02, reminder scheduled 2026-08-08, `sent=false`, nothing in the path that would skip it. (I deleted the row as part of cleanup, so it will not actually fire.)

Because defect 1 makes `golf_tasks.status` unusable as a filter, fixing 2 alone by adding `.eq('task.status','pending')` would not work either.

## Proposed fix

1. Roll the parent status up when the last assignment completes — either in `completeTaskAssignment` (recompute and write `golf_tasks.status` + `completed_at` when no `pending` assignments remain) or via a trigger on `golf_task_assignments`, which also backfills correctly.
2. In `getDueReminders`, skip reminders whose task has no outstanding work — join `golf_task_assignments` and drop rows where every assignment is `completed`. Do this at the query rather than at send time so the batch limit isn't consumed by dead reminders.
3. Consider per-assignee reminders: on a team task where 6 of 7 players are done, the 6 should not be reminded. Today `golf_task_reminders` is per-task, so this needs an assignee dimension to be fully correct.

## Also noticed while here

`golf_tasks.reminder_type` is `NULL` while `golf_task_reminders.reminder_type` is `'in_app'` for the same task — the denormalized copy on the parent is not written. Minor, but it is the same "parent row not maintained" pattern.

## Verified working

Reminder scheduling itself is correct, including timezone: entering `2026-08-08T09:00` locally stored `2026-08-08 13:00:00+00` and the player's task card rendered "Reminder · Aug 8 9:00 AM".
title: [MEDIUM] Task reminders fire for already-completed tasks — no completion check anywhere in the reminder path, and golf_tasks.status never rolls up

body:
Found 2026-08-02 auditing player notification settings.

## What happens

Settings -> Notifications renders an EMAIL/PUSH matrix. **Announcements is the only row with a blank (`—`) PUSH cell** — there is no `Announcements push` switch in the DOM (verified by enumerating every `[role="switch"]`: Quiet mode, Messages email/push, Events & reminders email/push, Announcements email, Tasks email/push, CoachHelm AI email/push).

But announcements **do** send push — `src/app/golf/actions/announcements.ts:327`:

```ts
await sendBulkPushNotification('team_announcement', recipientUserIdsForPush, { … });
```

and that type is gated by `push_events`, not by anything announcement-specific (`src/lib/notifications/push.ts:38-43`):

```ts
case 'team_announcement':
case 'qualifier_created':
case 'qualifier_updated':
case 'event_rsvp_reminder':
case 'round_submitted':
  return 'push_events';
```

## Why this is a real bug, not a design choice

Two user-visible consequences:

1. A player reading the settings matrix reasonably concludes announcements never push. They do.
2. A player who turns off **Events & reminders push** to stop calendar noise also silently stops receiving announcement pushes — including urgent ones and ones that require acknowledgement — with no switch that says so.

The codebase has already fixed this exact bug once, for CoachHelm, and the comment right above the mapping describes it (`push.ts:44-48`):

> *Was grouped under `push_events` — copy/paste drift from before CoachHelm push had its own settings toggle. A user who left "CoachHelm AI" push ON but "Events & reminders" push OFF never received insight pushes even though the switch they saved has nothing to do with `push_events`.*

Announcements is the same defect, unfixed.

## Proposed fix

Add a `push_announcements` delivery key, map `team_announcement` to it in `pushDeliveryKeyFor()`, and render the switch in the Announcements row so the matrix has no blank cell. Default it on, to preserve today's effective behavior for existing users.

Note `qualifier_created` / `qualifier_updated` / `round_submitted` are also bundled under `push_events` with no dedicated switch — worth checking whether those want the same treatment while the mapping is open.

## Related, verified working

Preference persistence itself is fine: toggling `Announcements email` off wrote `email_announcements: false` to `users.notification_preferences` and toggling it back restored it.
title: [MEDIUM] Announcements send push notifications but have no push toggle — silently governed by the "Events & reminders" switch

body:
`npm test` on `fix/deepsec-wave2-security` is **red: 14 failures across 5 files** (923 files passed, 8743 tests passed, 14 failed).

## The failures

All 14 are one cluster, in the exact module chain that `4ad0ccc5f` refactored (`fetch-all-rows.ts` -> `admin/rls-denial.ts` -> `server-error-logger.ts`):

- `src/lib/admin/__tests__/rls-denial.test.ts` — 5 failed
- `src/lib/supabase/__tests__/fetch-all-rows.test.ts` — 5 failed
- `src/lib/baseball/__tests__/with-baseball-action-observability.test.ts` — 2 failed
- `src/app/baseball/actions/__tests__/lifting-v11-rls-denial.test.ts` — 1 failed
- `src/app/golf/actions/__tests__/golf-save-partial-round.test.ts` — 1 failed

Representative assertion:

```
FAIL src/lib/admin/__tests__/rls-denial.test.ts > maybeCaptureRlsDenial
     > emits a warning event with source=rls_denial for a denial
AssertionError: expected "vi.fn()" to be called 1 times, but got 0 times
 -> src/lib/admin/__tests__/rls-denial.test.ts:37
     expect(captured).toBe(true);            // passes
     expect(mocks.logServerEvent).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);  // 0
```

`maybeCaptureRlsDenial` returns `captured === true` while `logServerEvent` fires **zero** times.

## Root cause

`4ad0ccc5f` moved the logger behind a lazy, fire-and-forget dynamic import so `server-only` code would stop landing in the client graph (`src/lib/admin/rls-denial.ts:106`):

```ts
if (typeof window === 'undefined') {
  void import('@/lib/server-error-logger')
    .then(({ logServerEvent }) => logServerEvent(/* … */))
    .catch(() => {});
}
```

The function returns `true` synchronously; the log resolves a microtask later. The assertions run before that, so the mock shows 0 calls. Previously the import was static and the call was synchronous.

That commit's own message states *"typecheck, lint and all 8755 unit tests passed"* — measured **before** the change. The suite was not re-run after, so the regression shipped onto the branch unnoticed. It is the same "green gate proved nothing" theme as #1223.

## Why this is not purely a test-timing artifact

The lazy import also adds a module-load tick before the write. In a Fluid/serverless instance that is torn down once the response flushes, an RLS denial can now be lost that previously had a better chance of being recorded. Worth deciding deliberately rather than by accident, since the whole point of `maybeCaptureRlsDenial` is that denials are observable.

## Proposed fix — pick one deliberately

- **(a) Keep fire-and-forget, fix the tests.** Have the 14 tests await a microtask flush (`await Promise.resolve()` / `await vi.waitFor(...)`) before asserting. Preserves the non-blocking production behavior the commit intended.
- **(b) Make the capture awaitable.** Have `maybeCaptureRlsDenial` return the promise (or add an `await`-able variant) and await it at the call sites that can afford to. Restores durability, but touches sync call sites.
- **(c) Break the client-graph dependency properly** — the follow-up `4ad0ccc5f` itself suggests: stop `fetch-all-rows.ts` dragging the admin logger into every client bundle. That would let the static import and `server-only` both come back legitimately and is the only option that removes the root cause.

I did not apply a fix: (a) vs (b) changes production semantics for RLS-denial durability, and that is the commit owner's call.

## Repro

```bash
npx vitest run src/lib/admin/__tests__/rls-denial.test.ts
# Tests  5 failed | 5 passed
```

Fails in isolation, so it is deterministic and not test-order dependent. None of the 5 failing files imports anything changed by the messaging fix on this branch (verified).
title: [HIGH] 4ad0ccc5f regressed 14 tests: maybeCaptureRlsDenial reports captured=true while logging nothing

body:
Found while playing a full 18 through the tracker as Cole Bennett (live demo data, 2026-08-02) and reconciling every row against a hand-computed scorecard.

## What happens

The shot tracker classifies **every** non-tee, non-green shot as `shot_type='approach'`, based on its position in the hole rather than on distance or intent. Two consequences, both reproduced:

**1. Layups on par 5s become "approach misses."** A 270y second shot on a 520y par 5 is a normal layup. The tracker labels it `Approach · Fairway` and — because the result is `fairway`, not `green` — **requires** a miss direction before `Next shot` enables ("Choose a miss direction"). There is no "laid up" / "not a miss" option; the 3×3 grid is Long/Short/Left/Right only.

**2. A penalty on the tee re-labels the replayed tee shot as an approach.** After `+ Penalty` on hole 14 (par 4, 375y), shot 1 is `shot_type='penalty'` and shot 2 — still played from the tee, still 375y out — is written as `shot_type='approach'`, `lie_before='tee'`, `miss_direction='short'`.

## Evidence

`approach_miss_details` for the one round I played — **4 of 8 rows are not approach shots**:

| hole | shot | dist_before | result | miss_direction | what it actually was |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | 2 | 270 yds | fairway | short | layup on a par 5 |
| 9 | 2 | 275 yds | fairway | short | layup on a par 5 |
| 13 | 2 | 260 yds | fairway | short | layup on a par 5 |
| 14 | 2 | **375 yds** | fairway | short | **tee shot after a water penalty** |
| 5 | 2 | 160 yds | sand | short_right | genuine |
| 6 | 2 | 170 yds | rough | short | genuine |
| 11 | 2 | 190 yds | rough | short | genuine |
| 16 | 1 | 185 yds | sand | short_left | genuine (par-3 tee) |

Every fabricated row is tagged `short`, because a layup is by definition short of the green. A player who lays up routinely will look like they chronically come up short on approaches.

## Blast radius

Two consumers already defend against exactly this and are fine:

- `src/lib/coachhelm/v2/mining/approach-analytics.ts` — `isRealApproach()` (line ~325) filters `approach_distance_yds > 250`, non-approach lies, and shots that make no material progress. Its own comment already names the bug: *"`approach_miss_details` contains rows for tee shots on par-5s … layups, and malformed rows."*
- `src/lib/coachhelm/v3/themes/shot-drivers.ts:101` — `if (distance > 250) return null; // not an approach`

**`src/lib/utils/golf-stats-calculator-shots.ts` does not.** It picks the approach shot purely by ordinal:

```ts
// golf-stats-calculator-shots.ts:1022
const girAttemptShotNumber = Math.max(holeInfo.par - 2, 1); // par 3 -> 1, par 4 -> 2, par 5 -> 3
let approachShot = normalizedShots.find(s => s.shot_number === girAttemptShotNumber);
```

On hole 14 (par 4 -> shot 2) that selects the 375-yard post-penalty tee shot, then:

- `approachDistance` = **375 yards** (line 1040)
- `approachLie` = `'tee'` normalized to `'fairway'` (line 1047) — so it enters the *fairway* by-lie bucket
- `approachMissDirection` = `'short'` (line 1084)

So the player-facing approach stats record a 375-yard approach from a fairway lie that missed short. Also note hole 14 is silently dropped from `driving_distance_avg` and from `total_fairways` (13 not 14), because its real tee shot is typed `approach`.

## Proposed fix

1. **`golf-stats-calculator-shots.ts`** — gate `approachShot` the same way the miners already do rather than trusting the ordinal: reject when `distance_to_hole_before` exceeds the approach ceiling (the miners use 250y), when `lie_before === 'tee'` on a par 4/5, or when the shot makes no material progress. Ideally extract the existing `isRealApproach()` into a shared helper so all three consumers agree instead of each re-deriving the rule.
2. **Write path (`golf.ts` `approachDetailsPayload`, ~line 1469)** — don't emit an `approach_miss_details` row for a shot that isn't a plausible approach. Fixing the source stops every future consumer from having to defend.
3. **Tracker UI** — add a "laid up / not going at the green" affirmative option so a deliberate layup isn't forced to claim a miss direction, and don't type a post-penalty replayed tee shot as `approach`.

## Repro

New Round -> any 18-hole course -> on a par 5, tee shot to fairway, then a second shot that also finishes in the fairway. `Next shot` stays disabled until you pick a miss direction. Submit, then query `approach_miss_details` joined to `golf_shots` for that round.
title: [HIGH] Shot type is assigned by ordinal, not distance — layups and post-penalty tee shots are recorded as approach misses and corrupt approach stats

body:
Found by driving the real flow in a browser as a player (`rinin376@gmail.com`) at **Rounds → New Round**, then verifying against `golf_rounds` / `golf_shots`.

## 1. The 9-hole selection is not honoured

Repro:
1. Rounds → New Round
2. Click **9 holes**
3. Pick a course from the sheet (I used Poplar Grove) and a tee set (Championship)
4. **Start round →**

Result: the tracker opens on **"Hole 1 of 18"**, renders the full 18-hole scorecard (OUT 9 + IN 9, TOTAL PAR 71), and the saved row has **`holes_played = 18`** (verified in `golf_rounds`).

Likely cause: the tee-set records are 18-hole (`Championship 18 holes 6,450 yds`), and applying a tee appears to overwrite the earlier hole-count choice. Whatever the mechanism, a player who picks 9 holes gets an 18-hole round and there is no way to tell from the setup screen that their choice was dropped.

Related: the exit dialog hardcodes the same assumption — *"round stats are only calculated when you complete the full 18 holes."* If 9-hole rounds are supported at all, that string needs to reflect the actual hole count; if they aren't, the **9 holes** button shouldn't be offered.

## 2. Course library has duplicate and malformed records

Visible in the course picker on this account:

- **`Club at Savannah Habor`** — misspelled (`Harbor`), and it appears in both *Recently Played* and the full list.
- Three separate **Pebble Beach** records with different ratings/slopes — `72.1/133`, `50/120`, `67.1/123` — plus both `Pebble Beach Golf Club` and `Pebble Beach Golf Links` in the library.
- A course rating of **50** is not a plausible value (real course ratings run roughly 65–77), which suggests `course_rating` / `course_slope` accept arbitrary numbers with no range validation.

Duplicate course records fragment a player's history: rounds at "the same" course land under different course ids, so per-course stats and trends silently split.

## What works well (for contrast)

Worth preserving through any fix:

- **Save & exit** is correct. The exit sheet offers *Save for later* / *Delete round* / *Cancel & continue playing* with clear descriptions, and persists `status='in_progress'`, `total_score=NULL`, with completed shots intact and the round resumable. Verified in the DB.
- Progressive disclosure in shot entry is good — choosing `Green (not fringe)` then requires **PROXIMITY TO HOLE (FT)** with the unit spelled out and marked Required.
- Tee selection shows yardage, delta from the longest tee (`−540 yds`), par, rating and slope per set — genuinely useful.
title: New Round: 9-hole selection is silently overridden to 18 holes; duplicate/malformed course records in the library

body:
Found by driving the real flow in a browser as a player (`rinin376@gmail.com`), pasting a schedule into **Classes → Import → Paste Text**, confirming, and then checking `golf_player_classes` and `golf_events` directly.

**The dialog says "3 classes will sync to your calendar" and then "Synced to your calendar." Zero `golf_events` rows are created.**

---

## 1. Silent sync failure — the hardcoded `'Spring 2026'` fallback

`src/app/golf/(dashboard)/dashboard/classes/page.tsx`, `handleConfirmClasses`:

```ts
semester: confirmedClass.semester || 'Spring 2026',
```

The parser leaves `semester` NULL (verified: NULL on all three inserted rows), so **every import falls back to `'Spring 2026'`** — a term that ended in May. The confirm dialog's SEMESTER START DATE defaults to today (August). `parseSemesterDates` then receives start = Aug 2 2026 against a Spring-2026 end of ~May 15 2026, `isValidCustomStart` correctly rejects start-after-end and returns `null`, and no occurrences are generated.

Note this file **already imports `detectSemester`** from `@/lib/utils/schedule-parser` and doesn't use it in this path.

## 2. Sync results are discarded, so the failure is invisible

Same handler:

```ts
await Promise.all(syncPromises);   // results never inspected
...
fairwayToast.success(`${importedCount} classes imported`, { description: 'Synced to your calendar.' });
```

`syncClassToCalendar` returns `{ success, error }`. Nothing reads it. The success toast fires unconditionally, so a total sync failure is reported to the player as success. **Any** fix to #1 should also surface a partial/total sync failure instead of asserting success.

## 3. Parser mangles input that matches the app's own example

The Paste Text placeholder documents this exact format:

```
BUAD 123 - Business Fundamentals
MWF 9:30AM - 10:45AM
HAL 101
Prof. Smith
```

Pasting two classes in precisely that shape produced **four**, and what landed in `golf_player_classes` was:

| `class_name` | `days` | times | `building`/`room` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CHEM 1310 - Untitled Class` | M,W,F ✓ | 13:00–13:50 ✓ | **NULL** — `BOGGS 152` lost |
| `BOGGS 152 - Prof. Nguyen` | `[]` | NULL | NULL |
| `HIST 2111 - Untitled Class` | `[]`→n/a | NULL | NULL |

Three distinct defects:
- **Course titles are dropped** — `General Chemistry I` becomes `Untitled Class`, though it sits right after the dash on the same line the code already splits.
- **The location line becomes a class.** `BOGGS 152` + `Prof. Nguyen` were emitted as a phantom course named `BOGGS 152 - Prof. Nguyen`.
- **`building` / `room` are never populated** — the location is lost from the real classes entirely, even though the columns exist.

## 4. Per-card Edit/Delete vanish after the first delete

In the Review Your Schedule step, each parsed class has Edit and Delete. After deleting **one** card, Edit/Delete disappear from **all** remaining cards — only Cancel / Confirm remain. With #3 producing phantom rows, a user who deletes one phantom then can't remove the second without cancelling and re-parsing the whole schedule.

---

## Suggested order

1. **#2 first** (smallest, highest value) — inspect the `syncClassToCalendar` results and stop lying in the toast. That alone converts a silent failure into a visible one.
2. **#1** — use the already-imported `detectSemester` (or the confirm dialog's start date) instead of `'Spring 2026'`, and validate that the chosen term actually contains the start date.
3. **#3** — parser fixes, with the placeholder's own format as a test fixture.
4. **#4** — UI state bug in the review step.

<sub>Test data created during this run was deleted afterwards; `golf_player_classes` is back to the original 6 rows.</sub>
title: Class schedule import silently syncs nothing: hardcoded 'Spring 2026' fallback, discarded sync results, and parser producing phantom classes

body:
Found during in-browser testing of GolfHelm (coach role, `fix/deepsec-wave2-security`). All minor, grouped because they're all small polish items on otherwise-clean pages.

## 1. Calendar toolbar is rendered twice in the DOM

`/golf/dashboard/calendar` — the control set `Previous / Today / Next / New event` appears **twice** in the accessibility tree. Almost certainly a mobile variant and a desktop variant both mounted with the other hidden via CSS.

Effect: screen-reader users hear every calendar control twice, and keyboard users tab through a set of controls that appear to do nothing. If one copy is CSS-hidden it should be unmounted, or marked `aria-hidden="true"` + `inert`.

## 2. Inconsistent salutation inside one flow

Sign in as a coach → the `/golf/welcome` interstitial says **"Welcome back, Coach Edwards."** → the dashboard `<h1>` immediately after says **"Welcome back, Pat"**.

Same user, same flow, two different name formats one screen apart. Pick one (last-name-with-title, or first name) and use it in both.

## 3. Tap targets below 32px

`/golf/dashboard`:

| control | size |
|---|---|
| "Collapse navigation" | 24 × 24 |
| "View as table" | 116 × 28 |
| "Skip to main content" | 32 × 16 |

WCAG 2.2 AA target-size (minimum) is 24×24 so these aren't violations, but they're below the 44×44 comfortable-touch guideline and this app ships as a Capacitor iOS build where that matters more than on desktop.

## 4. Minor text clipping

`/golf/dashboard` — `scrollWidth` exceeds `clientWidth` on: "View as table" (by 8px) and "Improving" (by 3px). Small enough to be invisible at default zoom, but they'll truncate at larger text sizes or narrower breakpoints.

---

<sub>Positive findings from the same pass, for context: no horizontal overflow anywhere, no broken images, **0 unlabelled interactive controls**, and 0 console errors on the dashboard and calendar once #1223's 500 was fixed.</sub>
title: [UI/UX] Calendar toolbar duplicated in DOM, inconsistent salutation, sub-32px tap targets, minor clipping

body:
## What happened

`/golf/dashboard/calendar` and `/golf/dashboard/tasks` returned **HTTP 500** on `fix/deepsec-wave2-security`.

Cause: `41ed50607` added `import 'server-only'` to `src/lib/server-error-logger.ts`, but that module is reached from **client** components:

```
FairwayCalendar.tsx (client)
  -> use-calendar-range-events.ts
    -> supabase/fetch-all-rows.ts
      -> admin/rls-denial.ts
        -> server-error-logger.ts   <-- 'server-only'
```

`use-task-realtime.ts` sits on the same chain, hence tasks. A second error rode along: `admin/request-context.ts` pulls `node:async_hooks`, which cannot be bundled for the client.

Fixed in `4ad0ccc5f`.

## Why this matters more than the bug

**Every gate passed while two primary pages were dead:**

| gate | result at the broken commit |
|---|---|
| `npm run typecheck` | exit 0 |
| `npm run lint` | clean |
| `npm test -- --run` | **8,755 passing**, 927/927 files |

Vitest never crosses the Next.js RSC/client boundary. Only `next build` (or loading the page) catches this class of error. The wave-1 and wave-2 remediation workflows explicitly instructed agents **not** to run `npm run build` to save time, and the gate stage ran only typecheck/lint/test — so ~90 security fixes shipped without the app ever being compiled for production.

## Proposed fix

Add `npm run build` to the gate set — CI (`ci.yml`) and any agent-driven remediation workflow.

Evidence it works: run against the fixed tree it gives `BUILD_EXIT=0`, 284 routes, 178/178 static pages, and finds **no other** `server-only`/`async_hooks` collisions in the tree — so it both catches the regression and confirms there are no siblings.

Cost is a few minutes per run, against a failure mode that ships a completely broken page behind three green checks.

## Follow-up (separate, smaller)

`src/lib/supabase/fetch-all-rows.ts` is a shared util that drags the admin logger — and therefore `createAdminClient` and `node:async_hooks` — into every client bundle that imports it. Breaking that dependency would let `server-only` be reinstated on `server-error-logger.ts` legitimately, and would shrink the client bundle.
title: Add `next build` to the gate set — typecheck+lint+8755 tests all passed while the calendar and tasks pages were 500ing

body:
**Table:** `public.golf_announcement_recipients`
**Affected policies:** `golf_ann_recipients_select_coaches`, `golf_ann_recipients_insert_coaches`, `golf_ann_recipients_delete_coaches` — **read, write, and delete**
**Status:** live in production · pre-existing (not introduced by #1220 or #1221)

> **Exposure today is zero — `golf_announcement_recipients` currently has 0 rows.** This is a latent
> misconfiguration, not an active leak. It becomes exploitable the moment targeted announcements are used.
> Filing at P1 because it is a live cross-tenant **write** path across 12 organizations, and the failure
> mode is silent: nothing surfaces until data exists.

## The defect

All three coach policies share one predicate. The inner subquery's `FROM` is `golf_coaches`, but it
**selects a column of `golf_announcements`** — the outer table:

```sql
announcement_id IN (
  SELECT golf_announcements.id
  FROM golf_announcements
  WHERE golf_announcements.team_id IN (
      SELECT golf_announcements.team_id   -- ← correlated ref to the OUTER row
      FROM golf_coaches                   -- ← FROM is golf_coaches
      WHERE golf_coaches.user_id = (SELECT auth.uid())
  )
)
```

Postgres resolves `golf_announcements.team_id` against the outer query, so the subquery returns the outer
row's **own** `team_id`, once per `golf_coaches` row belonging to the caller. The test collapses to
`team_id IN (team_id)` — trivially true — whenever the caller holds at least one coach row, and false
otherwise.

**Net effect: the policy's only real gate is "does the caller have a `golf_coaches` row at all."** Coach
signup is self-service, so that is not an authorization boundary. Any coach account can read, insert, and
delete recipient rows for any announcement in any team in any organization.

## Reproduction

The obvious check is vacuous — with 0 rows in the table, both the broken and correct predicates return 0.
So the predicate shape was tested directly, with a control:

```sql
WITH ann(id, team_id) AS (VALUES (1,'team-MINE'::text), (2,'team-RIVAL-ORG'::text)),
     my_coach_rows(user_id) AS (VALUES ('me'::text)),
     no_coach_rows(user_id) AS (SELECT 'x'::text WHERE false)
SELECT a.team_id,
       a.team_id IN (SELECT a.team_id FROM my_coach_rows WHERE user_id='me') AS broken_grants_access,
       a.team_id IN (SELECT a.team_id FROM no_coach_rows WHERE user_id='me') AS control_no_coach_row
FROM ann a;
```

```
 team_id        | broken_grants_access | control_no_coach_row
----------------+----------------------+----------------------
 team-MINE      | t                    | f
 team-RIVAL-ORG | t                    | f     ← access to an unrelated org's row
```

## Fix

Scope to teams the coach actually staffs, matching the `coach_id_for_team` RPC used elsewhere:

```sql
-- Repeat for all three: select / insert (WITH CHECK) / delete.
DROP POLICY IF EXISTS golf_ann_recipients_select_coaches ON public.golf_announcement_recipients;
CREATE POLICY golf_ann_recipients_select_coaches
  ON public.golf_announcement_recipients FOR SELECT TO authenticated
  USING (
    announcement_id IN (
      SELECT a.id
      FROM public.golf_announcements a
      WHERE a.team_id IN (
        SELECT gtcs.team_id
        FROM public.golf_team_coach_staff gtcs
        JOIN public.golf_coaches gc ON gc.id = gtcs.coach_id
        WHERE gc.user_id = (SELECT auth.uid())
      )
    )
  );
```

Aliasing the outer table (`golf_announcements a`) is what makes the bug impossible to reintroduce — the
inner query can no longer name an outer column by accident.

Note `golf_ann_recipients_select_own` (players reading their own rows) is **correct** and should be left
alone: `player_id IN (SELECT id FROM golf_players WHERE user_id = auth.uid())`.

## Worth checking alongside

This predicate shape looks copy-pasted. Other policies in the schema may carry the same
outer-column-in-inner-subquery mistake, and it is invisible to review because the SQL reads plausibly. A
sweep for inner subqueries whose selected column's table does not appear in their own `FROM` would find any
siblings.

---

<sub>Found during deepsec wave-1 review (#1220); verified directly against the production `pg_policies`
catalog. Requires a migration and db-migration-reviewer sign-off, which is why it was not bundled into
#1220 or #1221.</sub>
title: [RLS] golf_announcement_recipients coach policies grant cross-tenant read/insert/delete to any coach (correlated-subquery bug)

body:
**File:** `src/lib/server-error-logger.ts:1,528,539,559,317,338`
**Severity:** MEDIUM · **Class:** `server-action-no-auth` · **Scanner confidence:** medium

> **Not independently verified.** This is a scanner finding that has not been through an adversarial verification pass — confirm it against the code before acting. In wave 1, 25 of 77 findings were refuted on inspection.

## Finding
The file begins with a file-level `'use server'` directive (L1), so every export becomes a publicly-dispatchable POST endpoint (Server Action). `logServerError` (L528), `logServerException` (L539), and `logServerEvent` (L559) perform NO authentication, authorization, rate-limiting, or size-capping of their `context` argument, yet they write to the service-role-backed `error_logs` and `admin_events` tables via `createAdminClient()` (RLS-bypassing) and emit Sentry events.

An attacker who can dispatch these actions controls the entire `context` object, which flows straight into the write sinks: `user_id` (L317, L338), `user_email` (L339), `fingerprint` (L322–323 via `context.dbFingerprint`), `severity`, `source` (L346), `sport`/`team_id` (L343–344), and unbounded `metadata`/`extra`/`tags` (normalizedContext, L337 — message is capped to 2k/10k but the JSON context is not). Concrete impact: (1) INCIDENT-FEED FORGERY & FLOODING — inject unlimited fake `critical` error rows that surface on `/admin/errors` and get emailed to the founder by the admin-digest cron, drowning real incidents; (2) USER-ATTRIBUTION SPOOFING — set `userId`/`userEmail` to a victim so fabricated errors appear on that user's `/admin/users/[id]` detail page (which filters `admin_events.user_id`); (3) SENTRY ABUSE — `captureSentryTrace` runs before the persistence gate (so it fires in ALL environments) and honors the attacker's `fingerprint`, letting them burn Sentry quota and defeat/forge issue grouping; (4) STORAGE BLOAT — the uncapped `metadata` jsonb.

That this capability is meant to be gated is proven by the team's OWN client bridge, `src/app/api/internal/log-server-error/route.ts`, which wraps the very same `logServerException` behind a shared-secret header (`INTERNAL_LOG_KEY`, fail-closed), a 30/min per-IP rate limit, and strict per-field length caps. The Server Action surface exposes a strictly more powerful, completely unguarded path to the same sink. No client component imports these functions (only comments reference them), so their action IDs are not in the client bundle — exploitation requires deriving the Next.js action ID — but per this framework's model every `'use server'` export is a dispatchable endpoint, and any future client import would expose the ID immediately. Note: React auto-escaping + absence of `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` in the admin surface rules out a stored-XSS escalation.

## Recommendation

These are server-only utilities called by ~300 server modules and never by a client component, so they should not be Server Actions at all. Remove the file-level `'use server'` directive and rely on normal server imports (add `import 'server-only'` to enforce the boundary). Client/edge callers already have the guarded `/api/internal/log-server-error` route. If any export must remain an action, gate it exactly like that route: shared-secret/auth check, per-IP rate limit, and reject/override caller-supplied `userId`/`userEmail`/`source`/`fingerprint` plus cap `metadata` size.

## Recent committers (`git log`)

- njrini99-code <njrini99@gmail.com> (2026-08-01)
- Fable Integrator <fable@helm.local> (2026-07-20)

---

<sub>Filed from a deepsec wave-2 scan of the 129 files that use `createAdminClient` outside `src/app/golf/actions`. Wave-1 findings were fixed separately in `fix/deepsec-wave1-security`.</sub>
<!-- deepsec-wave2 server-action-no-auth src/lib/server-error-logger.ts -->
title: [MEDIUM] Unauthenticated Server Actions allow forging incident/error records and poisoning Sentry

body:
**File:** `src/lib/coachhelm/v2/orchestrator.ts:659,666,689,697,1919`
**Severity:** MEDIUM · **Class:** `cross-tenant-id` · **Scanner confidence:** medium

> **Not independently verified.** This is a scanner finding that has not been through an adversarial verification pass — confirm it against the code before acting. In wave 1, 25 of 77 findings were refuted on inspection.

## Finding
generateRoundReview(roundId, playerId) (L659-770) takes two independent identifiers and never verifies that the round belongs to the player. Every player-level layer — extractAllFeatures(playerId), getPlayerSignalSettings(playerId), PatternMiner/CausalEngine/PerformancePredictor/ShotPatternMiner(playerId), fetchPlayerStats(playerId) (the admin-scoped, RLS-bypassing fetch documented at L1913-1922), and generateInsights(playerId,...) — is keyed solely on the caller-supplied playerId, while roundId feeds only buildRoundSpecificInsights(roundId). Because the class deliberately performs zero authorization and relies on the caller (L1919: 'the caller of analyzePlayer ... authorized the player by other means'), any caller that authorizes only ONE of the two ids turns this into a cross-tenant leak. This is not theoretical: the reachable 'use server' caller src/app/golf/actions/insights.ts › generateRoundReviewImpl authorizes roundId via verifyRoundAccess but forwards an independent, attacker-controlled playerId, causing this method to compute and return a different player's full analysis (see the paired insights.ts finding). PerformancePredictor.predictPerformance() additionally UPSERTs a golf_predictions row for that playerId, so the contract also enables cross-tenant writes.

## Recommendation

Make the engine self-defending rather than fully trusting callers: have generateRoundReview derive playerId from roundId internally (look up golf_rounds.player_id for roundId) and ignore/assert the passed playerId, or require callers to pass a single authorized identity. At minimum, assert the round's owner == playerId before running any player-level analysis. Broadly, treat the admin-client entry points (analyzePlayer/generateRoundReview/fetchPlayerStats) as a trust boundary and document/enforce that the exact id used for the read must be the id the caller authorized.

- njrini99-code <njrini99@gmail.com> (2026-07-28)
- Fable Integrator <fable@helm.local> (2026-07-09)

**File:** `src/lib/calendar/rsvp.ts:156,173,189,209`
**Severity:** MEDIUM · **Class:** `cross-tenant-id` · **Scanner confidence:** high

> **Not independently verified.** This is a scanner finding that has not been through an adversarial verification pass — confirm it against the code before acting. In wave 1, 25 of 77 findings were refuted on inspection.

## Finding
sendEventInvitations(eventId, playerIds, supabase) trusts caller-supplied playerIds with no verification that each player belongs to the event's team, and its callers (createGolfEvent at golf.ts:2238-2245 and updateGolfEvent at golf.ts:2555-2578) pass client-supplied attendeeIds/addAttendeeIds through unvalidated.

The apparent mitigation — reading golf_players with the RLS client at L173-178 — does NOT bind players to the event's team. The golf_players_select policy authorizes coach reads via public.user_is_coach_of_golf_player(id), whose body is ORG-scoped (JOIN golf_teams gt ON gt.organization_id = gc.organization_id), so a coach can read EVERY active player in their organization, including other teams (e.g. men's coach reading women's-team players). Those players therefore survive the .in('id', playerIds) filter into `players`.

The attendance upsert (L189-193) then goes through the RLS client, but the golf_event_attendance_insert_coach policy WITH CHECK only verifies is_golf_team_coach(event.team_id) — it never constrains player_id to the event's team — so cross-team rows insert successfully. Finally, the notification insert (L209-213) uses createAdminClient(), bypassing RLS on golf_calendar_notifications entirely, delivering an attacker-controlled title (`You're invited: ${event.title}`), message (location string), and action_url to each victim player's user_id.

Impact: any coach (self-service signup) can (1) pollute another team's players' attendance data and (2) push forged/spam/phishing in-app notifications to players on other teams in the same organization. Cross-org is blocked because the golf_players read is org-scoped, but cross-team-within-org is fully reachable, which is a real tenant-boundary violation for rival-program tenancy. The victim UUIDs are obtainable by the same org-scoped read, so targeting is trivial.

## Recommendation

Before writing attendance or notifications, filter playerIds to active members of the event's team: fetch golf_team_members for event.team_id and intersect, or add a WHERE gtm.team_id = event.team_id / status='active' guard. Defense in depth: tighten golf_event_attendance_insert_coach to also require player_id IN (SELECT player_id FROM golf_team_members WHERE team_id = e.team_id AND status='active'), and have createGolfEvent/updateGolfEvent validate attendeeIds against the roster.
