body:
**File:** `src/lib/baseball/timeline-writer.ts:176,177,178,179,200`
**Severity:** MEDIUM · **Class:** `other-service-role-gate` · **Scanner confidence:** low

> **Not independently verified.** This is a scanner finding that has not been through an adversarial verification pass — confirm it against the code before acting. In wave 1, 25 of 77 findings were refuted on inspection.

## Finding
appendTimelineEvent selects the RLS-bypassing admin client via `useSystemClient = opts.system === true && (sourceKind === 'system' || sourceKind === 'ai')` (L178-179). The header comment (L176-177) claims 'A caller cannot smuggle a coach note through service-role.' But the gate constrains only the PROVENANCE (sourceKind, which is itself derived from the caller-supplied input.source via normalizeSourceKind, L169-171) — it does NOT constrain event_type (kind) or visibility. So a call of the form appendTimelineEvent({ kind: 'note', source: 'ai', visibility: 'staff_only', teamId, playerId, ... }, { system: true }) writes a staff_only event_type='note' row through the service-role client, bypassing the coach-only INSERT RLS policy (is_baseball_team_coach_v2(team_id)) entirely, with team_id/player_id taken verbatim from input and NO ownership check in this module. The guard checks the wrong field: it verifies the row is *labeled* system/ai, not that the row is actually a system/ai *kind* of event. NOT CURRENTLY WIRE-EXPLOITABLE: opts.system is the 2nd positional arg (never settable from request input), and I verified every current system-path caller is safe — appendSystemTimelineEvent constrains kind to 'ai'|'system'|'stat_milestone', appendLiftTimelineEvent forces kind:'lift', player-actions.ts:277 uses kind:'system'/source:'system', and the only kind:'note' writer (postgame.ts:326) deliberately omits {system:true} so it routes through the RLS coach client. Reported as a latent hardening gap because this is a shared, reusable writer whose safety comment actively misleads a future caller into believing notes are structurally protected.

## Recommendation

Bind the gate to the event kind, not just the provenance: define the set of kinds legitimately allowed on the service-role path (e.g. 'ai' | 'system' | 'stat_milestone' | 'lift') and require `kind ∈ SYSTEM_ALLOWED_KINDS` in useSystemClient, so a coach-authored kind ('note','recruiting', etc.) can never select the admin client regardless of the source override. Optionally also validate that player_id belongs to team_id before the system-path insert.

## Recent committers (`git log`)

- njrini99-code <njrini99@gmail.com> (2026-07-28)

---

body:
**File:** `src/app/baseball/actions/roster.ts:206,223,263`
**Severity:** MEDIUM · **Class:** `cross-tenant-id` · **Scanner confidence:** low

> **Not independently verified.** This is a scanner finding that has not been through an adversarial verification pass — confirm it against the code before acting. In wave 1, 25 of 77 findings were refuted on inspection.

## Finding
`assignPlayerToTeam` (line 206) is correctly gated by `withBaseballAction` + `can_manage_roster` against the coach's own active team (the WRITE target is properly authorized). However the SUBJECT — `args.playerId` — is never validated to belong to, or be discoverable within, the coach's tenant. The player row is fetched via the RLS-scoped client at line 223, then a `baseball_team_members` row with `status:'active'` is inserted for `(ctx.targetTeamId, playerId)` at lines 263-270. The sibling player-initiated path (`teams.ts joinTeam`) deliberately enforces an IDOR/ownership check (`player.user_id !== user.id`) and the team's join policy; the coach-side add bypasses both. This file's own `searchAssignablePlayers` documents (lines 708-714) that `baseball_players_select` is currently `USING(true)` until migration `20260729000200` is applied — meaning a coach can presently read and reference players from *other programs*. Combined, a coach can unilaterally attach a rival program's player (by id) to their roster, misrepresenting membership and potentially exposing that player to any RLS policy that grants team-staff access based on a membership row. Impact magnitude depends on the (currently-in-flux) tenant-isolation RLS state acknowledged in-file, hence low confidence, but the missing subject/tenant check is real and asymmetric with the consent-checked join path.

## Recommendation

Before inserting the membership, verify the target player is within the acting coach's tenant boundary (e.g. via the same SECURITY DEFINER, team-scoped resolver used by `findAssignablePlayerByExactEmail`, or an explicit organization/discoverability check) rather than relying solely on `baseball_players` RLS. Ensure migration `20260729000200` (own-roster + recruiting-discoverable SELECT policy) is applied so cross-tenant player rows are not referenceable in the first place.

**File:** `src/app/baseball/actions/demo-access.ts:519,520,521,529`
**Severity:** MEDIUM · **Class:** `rate-limit-bypass` · **Scanner confidence:** low

> **Not independently verified.** This is a scanner finding that has not been through an adversarial verification pass — confirm it against the code before acting. In wave 1, 25 of 77 findings were refuted on inspection.

## Finding
The public, unauthenticated `enterBaseballDemo` gate rests its entire abuse model on a per-IP rate limit — the JSDoc states 'abuse is bounded by the per-IP rate limit (RATE_LIMITS.DEMO_GATE)' and the code hammers `signInWithPasswordResilient` against a SHARED demo account plus writes unauthenticated CRM lead rows. The rate-limit identity is built at lines 519-522 as `headersList.get('x-forwarded-for')?.split(',')[0]?.trim() ?? x-real-ip ?? 'unknown'`, i.e. the LEFTMOST X-Forwarded-For token, which is the most client-controllable hop. If any deployment/proxy in front of this handler appends (rather than overwrites) a client-supplied `X-Forwarded-For`, an attacker can rotate the leftmost token per request (`X-Forwarded-For: <random>`) to mint unlimited distinct rate-limit keys, defeating the only abuse bound and enabling shared-account sign-in flooding and CRM lead-spam (`createLeadFromGate` inserts attacker-controlled name/email/school). Confidence is low because whether the leftmost token is attacker-controlled depends on the exact edge XFF-handling in production (if the platform strictly overwrites XFF with the real client IP, this token is trustworthy and the issue does not exploit).

## Recommendation

Derive the client IP from the platform's trusted signal rather than the leftmost XFF token — on Vercel use the framework-provided request IP or the rightmost/trusted-proxy hop of X-Forwarded-For (the value the edge itself set), not `split(',')[0]`. Document the trusted-hop assumption next to the rate-limit call so it can't silently regress.

**File:** `src/app/api/webhooks/resend-inbound/route.ts:86,130,179`
**Severity:** MEDIUM · **Class:** `other-webhook-content-trust` · **Scanner confidence:** low

> **Not independently verified.** This is a scanner finding that has not been through an adversarial verification pass — confirm it against the code before acting. In wave 1, 25 of 77 findings were refuted on inspection.

## Finding
The svix signature (L106-114) correctly proves the request was relayed by Resend, but it does NOT prove the email came from a real coach — Resend's Inbound Email Receiving forwards ANY message sent to the configured inbound domain (mx.helmsportslabs.com). So the from/subject/body/to fields are fully attacker-controlled: anyone on the internet can email that address and cause a row to be written to crm_replies via the service-role admin client (RLS bypassed), which then surfaces in the admin CRM inbox (InboxView/ReplyThread). There is no SPF/DKIM/allowlist check and no rate limiting, so an attacker can flood the admin inbox and bloat the table with forged 'replies' (spoofed From addresses, arbitrary subject/body). Impact is bounded and this is not a cross-tenant or RCE issue: body_html is never rendered (ReplyThread shows a placeholder and escapes body_text), from/subject/to render as React-escaped text, and the stop_sequences_on_reply trigger only fires when coach_id IS NOT NULL — which requires matching an opaque, unguessable resend_message_id, so a spoofed message lands with coach_id=null and cannot stop a real coach's sequence. The residual risk is admin-surface integrity/DoS (inbox spam, misleading reply rows, unbounded inserts), which an operator should weigh; some of this may be intended to be handled upstream at Resend.

## Recommendation

Treat inbound content as untrusted even after signature verification: validate the recipient (data.to) is an expected mailbox, optionally require the From domain to correspond to a known crm_coaches address before creating a row (or mark unknown-sender rows as quarantined/unlinked), and add basic rate limiting / volume caps on inbound inserts. Keep the current text-only rendering (never introduce dangerouslySetInnerHTML for body_html).

**File:** `src/app/api/log-error/route.ts:30`
**Severity:** MEDIUM · **Class:** `rate-limit-bypass` · **Scanner confidence:** medium

> **Not independently verified.** This is a scanner finding that has not been through an adversarial verification pass — confirm it against the code before acting. In wave 1, 25 of 77 findings were refuted on inspection.

## Finding
POST is protected only by withRateLimit(request, RATE_LIMITS.API_WRITE) (L30). That resolves the client key via getClientIdentifier() in `src/lib/rate-limit.ts` (L89-105), which returns `x-forwarded-for.split(',')[0].trim()` — the LEFTMOST X-Forwarded-For value. That leftmost entry is the least-trusted, caller-appendable part of the header: an attacker can send `X-Forwarded-For: <random>` on each request and the proxy appends the real IP after it, so every request is keyed to an attacker-chosen bucket and the 30-req/min limit never trips. The store is also a process-local in-memory Map (L11) that is not shared across serverless/Fluid instances, further diluting the limit. Because this endpoint accepts ANONYMOUS writes into admin tables (error_logs + admin_events via the service-role client, L177-205), an unauthenticated attacker can flood the incident/triage pipeline: unbounded row growth, cost, and — since the incident fingerprint (L118-123) is derived from attacker-controlled message/route — poisoning or drowning of the operator triage queue. The same limiter primitive also gates AUTH/EMAIL (login, signup, password reset), so the bypass enables credential brute-force and reset-spam beyond this route. Note: the stored message/stack/context fields are attacker-controlled but are rendered by React (auto-escaped) with no dangerouslySetInnerHTML sink in the admin surface, so this is not stored XSS.

## Recommendation

Key rate limiting on a trusted source: on Vercel use the platform-provided client IP (e.g. the rightmost XFF hop your proxy controls, or `x-real-ip`/`request.ip`), never the leftmost XFF value. Move the counter to a shared store (Upstash/Redis — already used elsewhere in this codebase) so limits hold across instances. Consider tightening the limit for this unauthenticated write path.

**File:** `src/app/api/cron/log-retention/route.ts:157`
**Severity:** MEDIUM · **Class:** `insecure-crypto` · **Scanner confidence:** low

> **Not independently verified.** This is a scanner finding that has not been through an adversarial verification pass — confirm it against the code before acting. In wave 1, 25 of 77 findings were refuted on inspection.

## Finding
L157 authorizes the cron with a plain string comparison: `req.headers.get('authorization') !== \`Bearer ${expected}\``, which is not constant-time. Same class as the admin-digest route. The check is correctly fail-closed (`!expected` → 401), so this is a best-practice hardening item, not an auth bypass; practical remote timing exploitation is very limited, hence low confidence.

## Recommendation

Use a constant-time comparison (`crypto.timingSafeEqual` with a length guard) via a shared cron-auth helper rather than `!==` on the raw secret.

body:
**File:** `src/app/api/cron/admin-digest/route.ts:56`
**Severity:** MEDIUM · **Class:** `insecure-crypto` · **Scanner confidence:** low

> **Not independently verified.** This is a scanner finding that has not been through an adversarial verification pass — confirm it against the code before acting. In wave 1, 25 of 77 findings were refuted on inspection.

## Finding
The cron authorization at L56 compares the caller-supplied bearer token to the secret with a plain string `!==`: `req.headers.get('authorization') !== \`Bearer ${expected}\``. JavaScript `!==` short-circuits on the first differing byte, so it is not constant-time. In principle this leaks timing information about `CRON_SECRET`. The check itself is correctly fail-closed (`!expected` → 401), so this is a hardening/best-practice issue rather than an auth bypass, and remote exploitation over HTTP is impractical given network jitter and the secret's high entropy — hence low confidence. Flagged because it is the standard finding for secret comparison and the scanner explicitly surfaced it.

## Recommendation

Compare secrets with a constant-time primitive (e.g. `crypto.timingSafeEqual` over equal-length buffers, after a length guard) or hash both sides before comparing. Centralize this in the shared cron-auth helper so all cron routes benefit.

body:
**File:** `src/app/api/crm/unsubscribe/route.ts:16,97,110`
**Severity:** MEDIUM · **Class:** `secret-in-fallback` · **Scanner confidence:** medium

> **Not independently verified.** This is a scanner finding that has not been through an adversarial verification pass — confirm it against the code before acting. In wave 1, 25 of 77 findings were refuted on inspection.

## Finding
This endpoint has no session auth by design (RFC 8058 one-click). The ONLY gate is verifyUnsubToken(c, t), whose key comes from `src/lib/crm/unsubscribe-token.ts` L20: `const SECRET = process.env.CRM_UNSUB_SECRET || 'helm-sports-unsub-v1'`. The token is `HMAC-SHA256(coachId, SECRET)` truncated to 16 hex chars (signUnsubToken, L33-35). If `CRM_UNSUB_SECRET` is not set in the environment, the HMAC is keyed by the hardcoded default that is committed to source (and the file's own comment says to set the env var 'to harden', implying the default is expected to be live out-of-the-box). An attacker who reads the source can compute a valid `t` for ANY coach id and POST/GET `/api/crm/unsubscribe?c=<id>&t=<forged>` to force-suppress arbitrary coaches (insert into crm_email_suppressions + flip crm_coaches.email_status='unsubscribed'). The endpoint's own header comment states the token exists 'so a stranger can't suppress arbitrary coaches by guessing ids' — that control is void when the default key is used. Impact is bounded by needing to know coach UUIDs (not enumerable), so this is a business-integrity/outreach-suppression issue rather than data exposure. Exploitability depends on whether CRM_UNSUB_SECRET is actually set in production (could not verify env from static review).

## Recommendation

Remove the hardcoded fallback. Require CRM_UNSUB_SECRET to be set and throw at startup if missing (fail-closed), matching how createAdminClient() throws when its env is absent. Rotate the secret if the default was ever deployed. Consider widening the token beyond 16 hex chars.

**File:** `src/app/api/crm/book-call/route.ts:136,208,263`
**Severity:** MEDIUM · **Class:** `rate-limit-bypass` · **Scanner confidence:** low

> **Not independently verified.** This is a scanner finding that has not been through an adversarial verification pass — confirm it against the code before acting. In wave 1, 25 of 77 findings were refuted on inspection.

## Finding
This is an intentionally-public GET beacon that, on every non-HEAD hit in production, does a service-role read of golf_demo_sessions (resolveVisitorHint, L158) and a service-role INSERT into admin_events (L263) via createAdminClient(). The only abuse control is checkRateLimit(`crm:book-call:${ip}`) at L208, where `ip` comes from readClientIp() → the first hop of the client-supplied x-forwarded-for header (L136–141). An attacker who rotates x-forwarded-for gets a fresh rate-limit bucket per value, defeating the 30/5min limit the file's own comment says exists 'to stop a script flooding the prod event feed.' The result is unbounded, unauthenticated service-role write amplification into a production incident/telemetry table plus per-hit admin reads — a DoS/cost/feed-integrity abuse. Impact is bounded to telemetry pollution (no attacker-readable data is returned; the redirect target is a constant and the visitor hint is only written to admin_events, never echoed), which caps severity. Note the scanner's other flags on this file are false positives: L316 redirects to the constant DEMO_PRICING_CALL_URL (no open redirect), L200 `new URL(request.url)` only parses (no SSRF/outbound fetch), and the L143–147/L206 'secret-in-log' hits log only error.message/error.code (no secrets).

## Recommendation

Rate-limit on a value the client cannot forge for evasion (e.g. combine the trusted platform-provided connecting IP with a coarse global ceiling), and/or add a small global cap on admin_events writes from this route. Consider dropping the golf_demo_sessions lookup + insert entirely for requests classified as automated scanners to bound write volume.

**File:** `src/app/api/coachhelm/v3/chat/stream/route.ts:223,281,458`
**Severity:** MEDIUM · **Class:** `expensive-api-abuse` · **Scanner confidence:** medium

> **Not independently verified.** This is a scanner finding that has not been through an adversarial verification pass — confirm it against the code before acting. In wave 1, 25 of 77 findings were refuted on inspection.

## Finding
The only abuse control on this paid LLM streaming endpoint is the per-coach daily budget. checkBudget() reads spent_usd at request start (L223) but the matching recordSpend() runs only in the stream's onFinish callback (recordTurnCost, L458) — after a stream that may run up to maxDuration=120s. There is no per-IP/per-request rate limit here (proxy.ts does session auth only, no throttling), so N concurrent POSTs all read the same low spent_usd, all pass `allowed = budget_usd > 0 && remaining >= estimated_cost_usd`, and all invoke streamText() (real Anthropic cost) before any spend is recorded. The daily cap ($3 default per budget.ts) is therefore exceeded by roughly (concurrency × ~$0.045) in a single burst. Because resolveCoachChatContext only requires a signed-in coach and the shared demo account is effectively public (per repo threat model), an unauthenticated-in-practice attacker can drive this. The window (full stream duration) is unusually large for a TOCTOU quota race, making it trivially exploitable by firing concurrent requests.

## Recommendation

Close the race before the expensive call: atomically reserve the estimated cost at gate time (e.g. an UPSERT that increments spent_usd/a reserved counter and checks the cap in one DB statement, or a SELECT ... FOR UPDATE / RPC), then reconcile to actual usage in onFinish. Additionally add a per-coach (and per-IP) request-rate limit via the existing checkRateLimit() so a burst of concurrent turns is bounded independently of the dollar budget.

**File:** `src/app/api/calendar/feeds/[token]/route.ts:296,330`
**Severity:** MEDIUM · **Class:** `secret-in-log` · **Scanner confidence:** high

> **Not independently verified.** This is a scanner finding that has not been through an adversarial verification pass — confirm it against the code before acting. In wave 1, 25 of 77 findings were refuted on inspection.

## Finding
The feed's secret bearer token is part of the request URL path (/api/calendar/feeds/<token>). On error paths the handler logs `url: request.url`, and server-error-logger.ts writes that url verbatim into three durable sinks: error_logs.url (server-error-logger.ts L319), admin_events.url (L340), and the Sentry 'server_trace' scope context (L434). ATTACK/EXPOSURE SCENARIO: a calendar app polls the feed (~hourly webcal refresh); a transient golf_events query error triggers logServerError({url: request.url}) at L293/L296, or any unexpected throw triggers logServerException(error, {url: request.url}) at L327/L330. The full URL — including the 256-bit feed_token that the file header explicitly calls 'the auth' (encode(gen_random_bytes(32),'hex')) — is now stored durably. Anyone with read access to those logs or the Sentry project (ops staff, extra Sentry seats, or a downstream log-exposure bug) obtains a working, non-expiring credential that grants read access to that team's entire calendar (event titles, locations, travel, opponents). Tokens do not expire; they are only invalidated by explicit regeneration. The existing feed-token-security.test.ts covers only the 401/404/200 authorization split, so this leak is untested.

## Recommendation

Never log the raw request.url for token-in-path routes. Log the static route pattern ('/api/calendar/feeds/[token]') plus a redacted/hashed token (e.g. first 6 chars + SHA-256 prefix) for correlation. Add a Sentry beforeSend scrubber that strips /calendar/(feeds|coach)/<token> path segments and confirm error_logs/admin_events writers never receive the raw token. Longer term, consider moving the token out of the URL path (e.g. an opaque short id in the path + token in a query the logger drops, or signed short-lived URLs) since path tokens also land in CDN/proxy access logs.

body:
**File:** `src/lib/coachhelm/v3/ingest/providers/arccos.ts:117,144`
**Severity:** HIGH_BUG · **Class:** `other-permanent-connection-stranding` · **Scanner confidence:** medium

> **Not independently verified.** This is a scanner finding that has not been through an adversarial verification pass — confirm it against the code before acting. In wave 1, 25 of 77 findings were refuted on inspection.

## Finding
sync() calls refreshAccessToken() (L117) and fetchRounds() (L144) without a surrounding try/catch. Both throw on ANY non-OK provider response other than 401 and on any network error (arccos-client.ts L94-96 and L137-139 `throw new Error(...)`). The adapter contract (types.ts L29-31) says adapters should instead RETURN `next_state:'error'` for provider downtime, but arccos.ts lets the exception escape. The ingest-sync cron catches it (route.ts L119-137) and hard-sets `state='error'`. Critically, the cron only ever selects connections with `.eq('state','active')` (route.ts L66), and NO code path anywhere resets an 'error' row back to 'active' (verified: the only writers of golf_ingest_connections.state are this adapter — tokens only — and the cron). The self-heal in nextConnectionState (`prev === 'error' ? 'active'`, types.ts L55) is therefore dead code: its `prev` is always 'active' because those are the only rows fetched. Net effect: a single transient Arccos 5xx or network blip during a sync silently and permanently disables that player's auto-ingest until they manually re-link the device. Latent today because the adapter is dormant in prod (isConfigured() false).

## Recommendation

Wrap the refresh + fetch calls in try/catch inside sync() and return `{ errors_count: 1, next_state: 'error', error_detail }` instead of throwing, AND fix the root cause in the cron: have the sync query also re-select connections in a recoverable 'error' state (or add a retry/backoff counter) so nextConnectionState's self-heal can actually fire. Distinguish terminal states ('revoked') from transient ones ('error').

**File:** `src/lib/coachhelm/v2/mining/shot-pattern-miner.ts:830,861`
**Severity:** HIGH_BUG · **Class:** `other-cross-writer-supersede-overreach` · **Scanner confidence:** medium

> **Not independently verified.** This is a scanner finding that has not been through an adversarial verification pass — confirm it against the code before acting. In wave 1, 25 of 77 findings were refuted on inspection.

## Finding
Same single issue as the pattern-miner.ts finding, seen from this file. savePatterns() (L830-943) writes pattern_type='contextual' shot-dispersion rows to the SHARED golf_patterns_v2 table with is_active=true and no lifecycle_state, and — unlike pattern-miner and causal-engine — performs NO supersede of its own. It implicitly relies on nothing else retiring its rows. That assumption is violated by PatternMiner.savePatterns()'s player-scoped, pattern_type-agnostic supersede, which runs concurrently in orchestrator.analyzePlayer() (Promise.all, L513-533) and flips these rows to is_active=false because their ids are absent from the round-level fresh-id list. Reported here as well so a reviewer scoped to this file is aware; the fix belongs in pattern-miner.ts's supersede filter (add a pattern_type constraint). No security impact — the effect is confined to the player's own patterns.

## Recommendation

Fix in pattern-miner.ts (constrain the supersede to round-level pattern_types). Optionally, defensively, have ShotPatternMiner tag its rows with a distinguishing column the round-level supersede excludes, and add a cross-miner integration test covering the concurrent analyzePlayer path.

> **Not independently verified.** This is a scanner finding that has not been through an adversarial verification pass — confirm it against the code before acting. In wave 1, 25 of 77 findings were refuted on inspection.

## Finding
PatternMiner.savePatterns() ends with a soft-supersede that flips is_active=false on every active auto-detected row for the player that is NOT in this run's fresh id set:

  fromUntyped(supabase,'golf_patterns_v2')
    .update({ is_active:false, ... })
    .in('player_id', playerIds)
    .eq('is_active', true)
    .not('id','in', idList)   // idList = ONLY round-level (conditional/compound/anomaly) ids
    .or('lifecycle_state.is.null,lifecycle_state.not.in.(confirmed,addressed,resolved,dismissed)')

There is NO pattern_type constraint. But golf_patterns_v2 is a shared table: ShotPatternMiner.savePatterns() (shot-pattern-miner.ts L830-943) writes pattern_type='contextual' shot-dispersion rows for the same player with is_active=true and no lifecycle_state (so they match the .or() branch). Their deterministic ids (shotPatternSignature namespace) are never in the round-level idList, so the round-level supersede classifies them as stale and retires them.

In orchestrator.analyzePlayer() (L513-533) PatternMiner.minePatterns() and ShotPatternMiner.analyzeShotPatterns({persistPatterns}) run CONCURRENTLY via Promise.all. The round-level supersede is the final DB op of a long sequential chain (extractAllFeatures -> load rounds -> 3-way mine -> batch-fetch lifecycle -> N sequential upserts -> supersede), while the shot miner's single batch upsert typically lands earlier; the common interleaving is therefore: shot rows written is_active=true, then round supersede flips them to is_active=false. Aggravating variant: any caller invoking analyzePlayer with includePatterns=true and persistPatterns=false (read-only) runs the round supersede (retiring shot rows) while the shot miner is skipped entirely and never re-adds them — deterministic loss, no race. Net effect: shot-dispersion patterns ('From 130-160y you miss long-right 67%') intermittently or systematically disappear from any surface that filters is_active=true.

Why it slipped through: the round-review path (orchestrator L676-694) runs the two miners sequentially (round first, then shot), masking the interaction there; and pattern-miner.supersede.test.ts pins the exact PostgREST filter (explicitly to prevent 'widen[ing] its blast radius') but only ever feeds round-level patterns, so the shared-table over-reach is untested.

## Recommendation

Scope the supersede to the pattern types this miner actually owns, e.g. add `.in('pattern_type', ['conditional','compound','anomaly'])` (or `.neq('pattern_type','contextual')`) to the update chain so it can never retire shot-dispersion rows written by ShotPatternMiner. Add a regression test that seeds an active contextual row and asserts it survives a round-level savePatterns() supersede. (Alternatively, give each miner a dedicated is_active namespace or a source-column filter.)

**File:** `src/app/api/account/delete/route.ts:170,177,196,208,228`
**Severity:** HIGH_BUG · **Class:** `other-non-atomic-delete` · **Scanner confidence:** medium

> **Not independently verified.** This is a scanner finding that has not been through an adversarial verification pass — confirm it against the code before acting. In wave 1, 25 of 77 findings were refuted on inspection.

## Finding
The handler performs a sequence of independent, auto-committing service-role statements with no surrounding transaction: it NULLs out attribution columns (L128-167), then DELETEs baseball_messages / golf_messages / engagement events (L170-194), and only then DELETEs from `users` (L196-199). The header comment documents that a residual set of NOT NULL attribution columns (player stats, box scores, travel expenses, goals, qualifier selections) can still make that final delete fail with Postgres 23503, in which case the route returns a 409 telling the user 'Please contact support' (L208-219). But by that point the user's messages have ALREADY been permanently deleted and their content attribution stripped — the failure path reports the account was NOT deleted while irreversible data loss has already occurred. The user reasonably believes nothing happened. Separately, admin.auth.admin.deleteUser (L228) runs AFTER the public.users row is deleted; if it fails (L230-235 → 500) the auth user is orphaned (can still authenticate, no profile row) with no rollback. Because there is no transaction, any mid-sequence failure leaves a corrupted, partially-deleted account.

## Recommendation

Perform the whole deletion in a single DB transaction (e.g. a SECURITY DEFINER RPC that does the null-outs, dependent deletes, and users delete atomically) so a blocking FK rolls everything back and no data is lost on the 409 path. Delete the auth user first (or last within the same atomic unit) and reconcile on failure. At minimum, do not delete messages until after the users-delete has been proven to succeed.

body:
**File:** `src/lib/notifications/push.ts:1,160,345`
**Severity:** HIGH · **Class:** `missing-auth` · **Scanner confidence:** medium

> **Verified by hand.** I read the code and confirmed this finding is real.

## Finding
The file starts with `'use server';` (L1), so its two exports — `sendPushNotification` (L160) and `sendBulkPushNotification` (L345) — are Server Actions, i.e. publicly callable POST endpoints. Neither performs any authentication (`auth.getUser()`) or authorization (ownership) check; they accept a fully caller-controlled `userId`/`userIds` and `data` and act on them. The module's own SECURITY CONTRACT comment (L154-159, mirrored in email.ts L40-45) states that `userId` MUST be server-sourced and NEVER raw user input, precisely because the device-token read uses the service-role admin client (RLS bypass, L180-188) and then invokes the paid APNs/FCM edge functions (L207). The `'use server'` directive contradicts that contract by exposing `userId`+`data` directly to the wire.

Attack scenarios: (1) Push spoofing / phishing — an attacker calls `sendPushNotification('new_message', <victimUserId>, { senderName: 'Coach Smith', preview: '<attacker text>', conversationId: '<attacker>' })`; `generatePushPayload` (L70-81) builds `title: 'Message from Coach Smith'` and `body: <attacker text>`, delivering a convincing spoofed push to the victim's real devices. (2) Expensive-API abuse — every call fans out to the paid Apple/Google push edge functions with no rate limiting; `sendBulkPushNotification` (L345-363) loops over an unbounded `userIds[]`, amplifying cost/volume. 

Reachability: server actions dispatch by POSTing the action ID to ANY route; public routes such as `/` (middleware.ts L547-554 returns `NextResponse.next()` with no auth) and the `(auth)` pages pass through middleware without a session, so the action is reachable without logging in. Next.js Origin-header CSRF protection does not authenticate a direct (non-browser) attacker who sets matching Origin/Host. 

Proof this is unintended: all 8 real callers are server-side (cron `event-reminders/route.ts` L482, `coachhelm/v3/notifications/dispatch.ts`, `coachhelm/v3/qualifying/player-notify.ts`, and server actions `announcements.ts`/`golf.ts`/`insights.ts`/`recurring-events.ts` via dynamic `import()`), plus the internal `golf-message-fanout.ts` helper; NO client component imports `push.ts`. The sibling helper `email.ts` — identical shape, same service-role reads — is deliberately a plain module with no `'use server'`, and `golf-message-fanout.ts` documents keeping helpers out of `'use server'` files specifically to avoid being client-callable. Mitigating factor (hence medium confidence): because no client component references these exports, their action IDs are not emitted in a client bundle, so exploitation requires deriving the deterministic action ID — but per this repo's threat model, action-ID secrecy is not an auth boundary and every `'use server'` export must carry its own auth+ownership check.

## Recommendation

Remove the `'use server';` directive from push.ts so `sendPushNotification`/`sendBulkPushNotification` stop being client-callable POST endpoints — it is only ever imported by server code (exactly like email.ts). If any export must remain a Server Action, add an explicit auth+authorization check at the top (verify `auth.getUser()` and that the caller is permitted to notify the target `userId`, e.g. shares a team/conversation), and add rate limiting before the edge-function fan-out. Bound `userIds.length` in `sendBulkPushNotification`.

body:
**File:** `src/app/baseball/actions/onboarding.ts:272,279,280,91,142`
**Severity:** HIGH · **Class:** `use-server-export` · **Scanner confidence:** high

> **Verified by hand.** I read the code and confirmed this finding is real.

## Finding
`completeCoachOnboarding` is exported from a file-level `'use server'` module (line 272), so it is a publicly callable POST endpoint. Its second parameter `_preVerifiedUser?: User` is intended only for internal server-to-server reuse (called with an already-verified user from `signupAndCompleteCoachOnboardingImpl` at lines 408/444). But because the function is exported, an attacker can invoke it directly and supply an arbitrary `_preVerifiedUser`. When `_preVerifiedUser` is truthy the function calls `runCompleteCoachOnboardingCore(_preVerifiedUser, data)` at line 280 with NO `supabase.auth.getUser()` check at all — the wrapper-guarded path (`completeCoachOnboardingAction` via `withBaseballAction`) is skipped entirely. `runCompleteCoachOnboardingCore` (line 138) then performs privileged writes through `createAdminClient()` (service role, bypasses RLS) keyed on the forged `user.id`/`user.email`: it creates an `organizations` row (attacker-named), a `baseball_coaches` row bound to the forged user_id, a `baseball_teams` row, and a `baseball_team_coach_staff` row. Critically, `ensureUserRowPreservingAdmin` (lines 70-93) reads `public.users` for that id and, if a row exists with role 'player', executes `UPDATE users SET role='coach' WHERE id=<forged>` (line 91) — a role flip on a victim account. Attack scenario: an unauthenticated attacker who knows a victim's user UUID crafts a POST with args `[{coachType,schoolName,...}, {id:'<victimUuid>', email:'x'}]`, flipping the victim's global role from player→coach and attaching an attacker-controlled 'program' to their account. Even absent a specific victim, this is an unauthenticated service-role write path. I confirmed the only legitimate client caller (coach-onboarding/page.tsx:288) passes a single argument, so no production code depends on a client supplying the identity param. The `withAdminObserved`/`withBaseballAction` distinction matters here: `withAdminObserved` is observability-only and this exported function isn't even wrapped in it.

## Recommendation

Do not accept caller-supplied identity in an exported Server Action. Remove the `_preVerifiedUser` parameter from the exported `completeCoachOnboarding` and always resolve the user server-side via `supabase.auth.getUser()` (or route exclusively through the `withBaseballAction` wrapper). If an internal fast-path is needed to avoid a redundant getUser during signup, extract `runCompleteCoachOnboardingCore` into a non-exported (`import 'server-only'`) helper and call that internally, leaving no exported surface that trusts a client-provided user.

**File:** `src/app/api/push-subscriptions/route.ts:46,90`
**Severity:** HIGH · **Class:** `ssrf` · **Scanner confidence:** medium

> **Not independently verified.** This is a scanner finding that has not been through an adversarial verification pass — confirm it against the code before acting. In wave 1, 25 of 77 findings were refuted on inspection.

## Finding
The POST handler persists the client-supplied `endpoint` string into `push_subscriptions.endpoint` with no validation beyond `isValidPayload`, which only checks `typeof endpoint === 'string' && length > 0` (L43-52). `endpoint` is stored verbatim (L90) under the authenticated user's `user_id`. This value is later consumed as an outbound-request target: `sendWebPush` (src/lib/coachhelm/v3/foundation/push.ts L97-109) passes it straight into `webpush.sendNotification`, and `task-reminders.ts` (L940-960) invokes that for a user's subscriptions when a reminder fires. The `web-push` library performs NO host validation — `web-push-lib.js` does `url.parse(endpoint)` then `https.request({hostname, port, path})` (L348-369), so the hostname and port are fully attacker-controlled with no allowlist, no scheme restriction to real push providers, and no RFC1918/loopback/link-local blocking. Attack: any authenticated user — including the shared demo account, which the repo treats as effectively public — POSTs `{endpoint:"https://internal-host:port/path", keys:{p256dh,auth}}` (a valid P-256 public key + 16-byte auth are trivially generated locally so the encryption step succeeds), then triggers a push to their own user_id (e.g. a self-assigned task reminder). The server then issues an HTTPS request to the attacker's chosen internal host/port. It is a BLIND SSRF (only statusCode is used server-side, never returned to the caller) and HTTPS-only (web-push forces https.request, so plain-HTTP targets like the AWS/GCP metadata IP won't complete a TLS handshake), but it still lets an unprivileged user make the server reach arbitrary internal TLS services/ports and leak the app's VAPID-signed Authorization JWT to an attacker-controlled external host.

## Recommendation

Validate `endpoint` at the trust boundary before storing: parse it with `new URL()`, require `protocol === 'https:'`, and enforce an allowlist of known push-service hosts (e.g. `*.push.services.mozilla.com`, `fcm.googleapis.com`, `*.notify.windows.com`, `*.push.apple.com`) OR at minimum reject hostnames that resolve to private/loopback/link-local/metadata ranges. Reject non-conforming endpoints with 400. Optionally also guard the sink in `sendWebPush` as defense-in-depth.

body:
This has been tracked as an error-count problem ("41 `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET is not configured` events"). It is bigger than that.

## What is actually happening

Stripe holds **live-mode invoices to real universities** for the 2026–27 GolfHelm annual (`helm_batch_id: 2026-07-golfhelm-annual`, written by `scripts/stripe-golfhelm-invoices.mjs`). Lynchburg, Shenandoah, UNCW, Hampden-Sydney, Piedmont, and more — the list returns `has_more: true`.

**One of them has been paid.** Shenandoah University, **$1,200.00**, `status: "paid"`.

`billing_invoices` in production holds **0 rows**.

So the only real revenue event to date never reached the product. Anything that reads billing state — admin, entitlements, reporting — cannot see that a customer has paid.

## Why

The webhook endpoint is healthy and delivering. Verified directly:

```
we_1TyO94PvzDMlWDMKjp3JiGyW
  url:    https://helmsportslabs.com/api/webhooks/stripe
  status: enabled
  events: invoice.paid, invoice.payment_failed, invoice.finalized,
          invoice.sent, invoice.marked_uncollectible, invoice.voided
```

It is `enabled`, so Stripe's ~3-day auto-disable for a continuously-failing endpoint **has not fired** — which is lucky, and is a clock worth respecting.

The handler 500s because `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is absent from the production environment, so signature verification fails before any business logic runs. `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` is absent too. Both re-confirmed missing against production env.

## The fix

Set both in Vercel production. That is the whole fix — no code change, no re-enable, no backfill mechanism to build.

This is dashboard-only and cannot be automated: **Stripe has no API to create an API key at all, and never re-reveals an endpoint's signing secret after creation.** So it needs a human in the Stripe dashboard.

## After setting them

Worth checking rather than assuming:

1. Stripe → Developers → Webhooks → this endpoint → **Resend** the failed `invoice.paid` delivery for Shenandoah, so the existing payment mirrors without waiting for a new event.
2. Re-query `select count(*) from billing_invoices` and confirm it is no longer 0.
3. Confirm the `[Stripe Webhook] STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET is not configured` events stop.

## Note on ordering

Setting these vars does **not** require the pending production deploy — they are read at runtime by the webhook route, not inlined at build time like `NEXT_PUBLIC_*`. So this can be fixed independently of, and before, the promote.
title: A paid live invoice is not mirrored into billing_invoices — Stripe webhook 500s for want of two env vars

body:
`vitest.config.ts` already records the headline:

> the other 46 files in `scripts/__tests__/` are written for `node --test` … and are **NOT wired into any CI job or npm script today** — a separate, larger dead-test finding

This issue puts numbers on it, because the shape of the problem turns out to matter more than the count.

## Measured

I ran every unwired `.test.mjs` in `scripts/__tests__/` by hand (excluding the seed-related ones, which touch seeding logic):

| | |
|---|---|
| **pass today** | 20 |
| **fail today** | 20 |

47 files live there; 3 are wired into vitest, plus 2 more from `scripts/lib/__tests__/`.

**Read that second row carefully.** A failing unwired guard is not noise — it is either a rotted pointer, or a guard that has been correct and unheard. Both have now been confirmed, one each:

- **rotted** — `drawers-mobile.test.mjs` (#1189). The 44pt touch-target suite had drifted in **four** places: it asserted against `ShotTrackingComprehensive.tsx` (which nothing renders), plus `RoundStripGrid.tsx`, `ChatDrawer.tsx` and `ChatComposer.tsx`, none of which exist. It guarded dead code while the surface users actually touch went unguarded.
- **correct and unheard** — `icon-only-button-aria-label.test.mjs` (#1193). It had been sitting on a real accessibility defect: an icon-only dismiss button in `lifting/dashboard/import/import-client.tsx` with no accessible name. A screen-reader user heard "button". Fixed, and the guard promoted.

## Suggested triage

For each of the 20 failing files, decide which of three it is:

1. **rotted pointer** → repoint at what renders, or delete the rule if what it guarded no longer exists in any form (both happened in #1189 — the hole-strip scroll-snap rule and the launcher-FAB safe-area rule were removed, because round review now reflows with a grid and the FAB is `hidden md:flex`, desktop-only).
2. **real defect** → fix it, then promote the guard, as in #1193.
3. **obsolete rule** → delete the file.

The 20 that already pass are close to free: convert `node:test` → `vitest` (a one-line import swap; see the note at the top of `scripts-no-committed-secrets.test.mjs`) and add a line to the `unit` include list.

## Two traps for whoever picks this up

**Do not trust my numbers without re-deriving them.** My first sweep reported **40/40 failing**. That was entirely an artifact of `timeout` not existing on macOS — every invocation died on a missing command rather than a failing assertion. The real split is 20/20.

**Some of these files are invisible to `rg`.** `icon-only-button-aria-label.test.mjs` contained three raw NUL bytes (a `sr-only` sentinel), which made ripgrep classify it as binary and skip it entirely:

```
$ rg -n "^import" scripts/__tests__/icon-only-button-aria-label.test.mjs
binary file matches (found "\0" byte around offset 7570)
```

So a source-text audit of these guards can silently miss some of them. Fixed in that one file; worth checking whether any others do the same before concluding a sweep is complete.

## Why this is worth doing rather than deleting

A stale test that passes is worse than no test, because it reads as coverage — but two out of two examined so far produced real value once run. The base rate here looks good enough to justify the triage rather than a bulk delete.

Related: #1186 (the mobile-viewport gate covers zero golf routes, for a different reason — no golf CI fixture).
title: 44 guards in scripts/__tests__/ run under nothing — 20 pass, 20 fail, and at least one was hiding a real defect

body:
`e2e/mobile-viewports.spec.ts` is a genuinely good gate. It renders at real device widths (390px among them) and asserts two things that matter:

```
`${route}: page pans horizontally (scrollWidth ${scrollWidth} > viewport ${innerWidth})`
`${route}: header/nav controls clipped at viewport edge`
```

It is wired as a **blocking** regression project in `.github/workflows/playwright.yml`.

**It covers zero GolfHelm dashboard routes.**

```ts
const PUBLIC_ROUTES = ['/', '/products', '/golf/login', '/baseball/login'];
const COACH_ROUTES  = ['/baseball/dashboard/command-center', '…/calendar', '…/roster', '…/stats-center', '…/settings'];
const PLAYER_ROUTES = ['/baseball/player/today', '/baseball/dashboard/calendar', '…/roster', '…/my-stats'];
```

The only golf route in the whole suite is `/golf/login`. Roster, calendar, stats, messages, rounds, CoachHelm, intelligence — none are checked at any mobile width, by anything, ever.

## Why — one root cause, two symptoms

There is **no golf CI fixture**. `scripts/` contains `seed-baseball-e2e.ts` and nothing equivalent for golf, and `playwright.config.ts` only ever hands out baseball storage state:

```ts
storageState: 'playwright/.auth/baseball-coach.json'   // mobile-coach
storageState: 'playwright/.auth/baseball-player.json'  // mobile-player
```

`playwright/auth.setup.ts` already knows how to log a golf coach and player in and persist their state — it just needs `GOLFHELM_COACH_EMAIL` / `GOLFHELM_PLAYER_EMAIL` credentials that only exist against real data, never in a local stack.

That same missing fixture explains a second symptom: `golf-dashboard.spec.ts`, `golf-round.spec.ts` and `golf-qualifier.spec.ts` all `test.skip` unless `E2E_GOLF_EMAIL`/`E2E_GOLF_PASSWORD` are set, so **in CI they skip rather than run**. Golf E2E is not failing; it is absent.

The playwright workflow already names this, in the comment explaining why that job still writes to production:

> …it runs the full chromium suite, including the golf specs that authenticate as `E2E_GOLF_EMAIL` against real golf data. A job has one `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`… **Rehoming this job means seeding golf locally first — a separate piece of work.**

This issue is that separate piece of work.

## Why it matters now

"Mobile and desktop cohesion" is a stated goal for GolfHelm specifically, and the regression gate that would defend it runs entirely against the other sport. The `#806` class it was built to catch — a control visible but cut off at the viewport edge — is unguarded on every golf surface.

## Shape of the fix

1. `scripts/seed-golf-e2e.ts`, mirroring `seed-baseball-e2e.ts` — including its target guard, which refuses a non-local target unless explicitly named. That guard was added because the baseball seeder had none and was silently writing to production; do not reintroduce that.
2. A `golf-coach` / `golf-player` setup project persisting `playwright/.auth/golf-*.json`.
3. `mobile-golf-coach` / `mobile-golf-player` projects, plus golf route lists in `mobile-viewports.spec.ts`.
4. Once golf is seeded locally, the `Playwright E2E` job can stop pointing at production entirely — which is the prize, not a side effect.

## Cheap partial, if the above is too big right now

Add unauthenticated golf routes to `PUBLIC_ROUTES`. It needs no fixture and would at least pin golf's auth surfaces at 390px. It is a small fraction of the value — the dashboard is where the layout risk lives — but it is non-zero and lands today.
title: GolfHelm has no mobile-viewport regression coverage — the gate is baseball-only

body:
`capacitor.config.ts` appends `HelmSportsLabsApp` to the iOS user agent specifically so the server can keep marketing and membership surfaces out of the native app:

> Marker appended to UA so the server-side proxy can detect native iOS requests and block marketing/membership pages (App Store Guideline 3.1.1).

That guard **is** implemented, and implemented the right way round — as an allowlist in `src/proxy.ts`:

```ts
const APP_ROUTE_PREFIXES = ['/golf','/baseball','/admin','/api','/auth','/support','/privacy','/terms','/dev'];

function isMarketingRoute(pathname: string): boolean {
  if (pathname === '/') return true;
  return !APP_ROUTE_PREFIXES.some(p => pathname === p || pathname.startsWith(`${p}/`));
}
```

Anything outside those prefixes is treated as marketing and redirected away, so `/products` and `/pricing` are blocked by default rather than by enumeration. That is the safe direction, and it is good.

## The gap

**Nothing tests it.** The only test in the repo mentioning `HelmSportsLabsApp` is `src/test/lib/error-logging.test.ts`, and that is about the bot-detection regex, not this guard.

So the failure mode is silent and expensive: someone adds a prefix to `APP_ROUTE_PREFIXES`, or refactors `isMarketingRoute`, or changes the UA marker on one side only — and marketing/pricing surfaces become reachable inside the iOS app. Nothing goes red. The next signal is an App Store review rejection, which costs a submission cycle.

Note the marker is duplicated: `src/proxy.ts:17` and `src/lib/supabase/middleware.ts:130` each define `NATIVE_UA_MARKER` independently, and `capacitor.config.ts` defines the string a third time. Three copies, no test tying them together.

## Why I did not just add the test

`isMarketingRoute` and `isNativeUserAgent` are module-private. Reaching them means either exporting them from `src/proxy.ts` — which is Next's proxy entrypoint, where I would rather not add exports casually — or extracting them into a helper module.

The extraction is the better shape, but `proxy.ts` runs on **every request** and owns session refresh and role-based redirects. That is not a file to refactor unattended at 3am for a test. Doing it wrong breaks auth for everyone, which is far worse than the gap it closes.

## Suggested shape

1. Move `NATIVE_UA_MARKER`, `APP_ROUTE_PREFIXES`, `isNativeUserAgent`, and `isMarketingRoute` into something like `src/lib/native/app-routes.ts`, and import from all three current definition sites so the marker exists once.
2. Unit-test `isMarketingRoute` over a table: every entry in `APP_ROUTE_PREFIXES` and a nested child of each → not marketing; `/`, `/products`, `/pricing`, `/about` → marketing.
3. Assert the config's `appendUserAgent` and the server's marker are the same string, so the two halves cannot drift.

All pure functions, no mocking of `NextRequest` or Supabase needed once extracted.

body:
**Framing correction first: this is not a new discovery.** `src/test/schema/rpc-functions-tracked.test.ts` has carried both names in `KNOWN_MISSING_RPCS` since 2026-07-29 (#1134), with a stale-entry test so the lines cannot outlive the defect. I re-found them independently by the same method and initially filed this as new. The gate was already working; what was missing is a tracked decision, which is what this issue is now for.

Two RPCs are called from live code and do not exist:

| RPC | called from |
|---|---|
| `calculate_grad_year_percentiles` | `baseball/actions/recruiting-philosophy.ts:344`, inside exported `recalculatePercentiles` |
| `calculate_player_match_score` | `baseball/actions/recruiting-philosophy.ts:398`, inside `calculateMatchScoresForPlayers` |

Verified: absent from **every schema**, no similarly-named function (`%grad_year%`, `%match_score%`), and **no migration mentions either name under any casing**. They were never authored — this is not the "recorded but never ran" trap.

## Impact

Both fail gracefully. `recalculatePercentiles` returns `{ success: false, error: sanitizeDbError(...) }` and logs, so it surfaces as a generic error rather than an outage. The features simply do not work:

- recalculating grad-year percentiles from baseball recruiting preferences
- server-side match scoring used to enrich player data in discover

`recruiting-philosophy.ts` is imported by live surfaces — `baseball/(dashboard)/dashboard/settings/page.tsx` and `recruiting-preferences/recruiting-preferences-client.tsx` — so this is reachable, not dead code behind the recruiting sunset.

## The decision

Whether these belong to the sunset recruiting surface or are still wanted.

- **Wanted** → they need authoring plus a migration, and the allowlist lines come out.
- **Not wanted** → the call sites and their UI should go, because those pages currently present a control that cannot succeed. The allowlist lines come out then too.

Either way the exit condition is the same: `KNOWN_MISSING_RPCS` ends up empty. What is not acceptable is leaving it as-is indefinitely, which is precisely what the stale-entry test cannot detect — it catches entries that became *false*, not entries that stayed true too long.

## Footnote worth keeping

While checking this I ran a case-**sensitive** sweep and wrongly concluded `ingest_external_round_atomic` was untracked too. It is not — it is declared in `20260621130000`, in lowercase, and correctly revoked from `public` and `anon`. Hand-run greps over this migrations directory are unreliable in two specific ways: the 2026-05-27 baseline quotes every identifier (`"public"."foo"`) and hand-written migrations vary in case. The committed test handles both; ad-hoc greps should not be trusted over it.
title: calculate_grad_year_percentiles / calculate_player_match_score were never written — decide sunset vs build

body:
The `Supabase Preview` check cannot validate migrations, and has not been able to for about a month.

## Evidence

`main`'s own Supabase branch:

```
name: main   status: MIGRATIONS_FAILED   updated_at: 2026-07-03T21:11:11Z
```

Preview branches are built by replaying migrations from that parent. With the parent in `MIGRATIONS_FAILED`, a PR that adds a migration gets **no branch created at all** — the check just goes red.

Observed on three PRs open at the same time tonight:

| PR | has a migration | preview branch |
|---|---|---|
| #1176 | no | created, `FUNCTIONS_DEPLOYED` |
| #1177 | no | created, `FUNCTIONS_DEPLOYED` |
| #1181 | **yes** | **none created; check failed** |

So the check passes precisely when it has nothing to verify, and fails whenever it would have mattered. On PRs without migrations it reports `skipping`, which reads like healthy noise.

## Why it matters

`Supabase Preview` is the only thing in CI that *executes* SQL. `sqlfluff` lints style and the RLS tests run against a local stack, but nothing else replays a migration end to end. So for roughly a month, every migration has merged with no execution check — including tonight's, and including any that were recorded but never ran.

That compounds a hazard this repo already has documented: `schema_migrations` has been wrong here before, with migrations marked applied that never ran. The preview branch was the mechanism that would have caught the class.

It is also not a required context on `main` (only `CodeQL`, `all`, `Smoke checks` are), so its red never blocks anything — which is why it could sit broken this long without forcing the issue.

## What to do

1. Find out why `main`'s branch entered `MIGRATIONS_FAILED` on 2026-07-03 — most likely one migration in the sequence does not replay cleanly from the baseline. The active baseline `20260527000000_prod_public_baseline.sql` is a **public-schema-only** dump, so anything a migration assumes about `auth`, `storage`, `cron`, or `realtime` will not exist on a rebuilt branch. That is the same structural gap that explains the untracked `avatars` bucket (`20260730030000`) and the `auth.users` trigger (`20260730020000`).
2. Once replay is green, consider making the check required for PRs that touch `supabase/migrations/**`. A check that only runs when it has nothing to do is worse than no check, because it reads as coverage.

## Related

Same shape as the rest of the 2026-08-01 sweep — a safety net that is present in the UI and dead in practice:

- the realtime publication: 13 subscriptions silently dead (fixed, `20260801040000`, plus a coverage test)
- #1173 / #1181: storage buckets the code writes to that do not exist
- #1175: edge functions deployed with no source in the repo
- this issue
title: Supabase preview branches have been unable to validate migrations since 2026-07-03

body:
## What I checked

All 17 crons declared in `vercel.json` are genuinely running: **933 runs in the last 48h, all `completed`, zero failures**. Nothing scheduled is broken.

(First pass of this query said every job was failing. That was my predicate — the status value is `completed`, not `success`. Noting it so the number below is read as verified rather than assumed.)

## What is not running

There are **22 cron routes on disk and 17 scheduled**. Three of the five gaps are deliberate and correct:

- `v3/genome-backfill`, `v3/standing-backfill` — one-shot backfills, manual by design (the label is literally `v3-genome-backfill-oneshot`).
- `v3/weekly-coach-email` — unscheduled on purpose by #1139, *"so no automated mail can reach a coach"*. Last ran 2026-07-26. **Correct as-is.**

The other two were dropped by **#93**, which was explicitly a temporary experiment:

> ops: reduce cron load to test Vercel deploy block
> Drop 3 unused baseball-side crons (process-sequences, refresh-engagement, v3/ingest-sync)…
> Goal: isolate whether cron volume/config is what's tripping the "Resource provisioning failed" abuse flag on this project.

`refresh-engagement` was put back — it runs every 5 minutes today. `process-sequences` and `v3/ingest-sync` never were. Neither has any entry in `background_job_logs`.

## The decision

### `process-sequences`

The route is intact and it **sends real outbound email through Resend to `crm_coaches`** (`route.ts:407`), walking `crm_sequence_enrollments` → `crm_sequence_steps` → `crm_email_templates`, and it does check `crm_email_suppressions` first.

So CRM email sequences have not been processing for as long as this has been unscheduled. Whether that is a bug depends on intent, and there is real evidence pointing both ways:

- it was unscheduled **by accident of a load test**, not by choice
- but #1139 later unscheduled the coach email deliberately so that no automated mail could reach a coach, and the repo's standing posture is that outbound sending is approval-gated

I have deliberately **not** rescheduled it. Turning automated email to real college coaches back on unattended is not a call to make from a cron audit. If sequences are meant to run, restoring it is one entry in `vercel.json` — but the dry-run/approval path should be confirmed first.

### `v3/ingest-sync`

Labeled `v3-ingest-sync`, never scheduled, no job-log history. Worth confirming whether it is meant to run at all — the Arccos/Garmin/TrackMan adapters it would drive are still stubs, so "not scheduled" may well be correct.

## Also worth a line

`coach-morning-digest` still has rows in `background_job_logs` (last 2026-07-25) but no route — deleted by #1052. That is fine; it just means the job-log table outlives its jobs, so "appears in the log" is not evidence a job exists.
title: Two crons dropped by a temporary diagnostic (#93) were never restored — decide whether they should be

body:
Found by comparing deployed Supabase edge functions against `supabase/functions/`. Two ACTIVE functions have no committed source.

**Correction to my first framing:** these are not new findings. A prior audit already recorded both in `docs/qa/helm-database-map.md`, verbatim as `orphan P0` and `orphan P0/P1`. They were documented and then nothing happened. That makes this more urgent, not less — and it means the gap is not detection, it is that a finding in a QA doc has no mechanism to become work.

| slug | in repo | `verify_jwt` | note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `send-apns-push` | yes | true | **deployed source differs from the committed source** — see 3 |
| `personalize-email` | yes | true | fine |
| `process-task-reminders` | was | — | not deployed, not invoked; deleted as dead code |
| `create-admin-user` | **no** | **false** | see 1 |
| `verify-emails` | **no** | true | see 2 |

Nothing in `src/` invokes either untracked function.

### 1. `create-admin-user` — prior audit: "orphan P0"

A one-shot bootstrap that provisioned the current super-admin account in February. Still needs closing out:

- `verify_jwt: false` — it takes no Authorization header at all.
- It authenticates a fixed account using a credential written directly into the function body, so that credential's strength is whatever was typed in February, and it lives in a deployed artifact.

It cannot re-provision or alter the existing account today (the underlying admin call rejects a duplicate address), so this is latent rather than open.

1. Rotate the credential for that account from the dashboard — the only piece with real exposure, since the app has a public sign-in page.
2. Delete the function; it has served its purpose:
   `supabase functions delete create-admin-user --project-ref qmnssrrolpinvwjjnufo`
3. Consider MFA on that account.

### 2. `verify-emails` — prior audit: "orphan P0/P1"

`verify_jwt: true` is weaker than it appears. Supabase checks only that the presented JWT is signed by this project, and the anon publishable key satisfies that — and it ships in the client bundle. There is no role check inside the handler.

The handler reads `crm_coaches`, opens outbound SMTP connections to arbitrary MX hosts to test whether addresses accept mail, and writes `email_status = 'bounced'` for ones it judges invalid. Both the outbound traffic and the CRM writes should require more than a public key.

Fix: role check at the top of the handler, and commit the source under `supabase/functions/verify-emails/`.

### 3. `send-apns-push` — committed source is not what runs

The same audit notes "deployed/repo token-deactivation behavior differs". So even the function we *do* track has drifted: reviewing the file in this repo does not tell you what production does. Worth diffing deployed against committed and reconciling.

### The general pattern

Third instance in one night of **production infrastructure that no repo artifact describes, so nothing notices when it is wrong**:

- the realtime publication: 13 subscriptions silently dead, fixed in `20260801040000` plus a coverage test that cross-checks code against migrations
- #1173: a storage bucket the code writes to that does not exist
- this issue

The publication got a test. Edge functions deserve the equivalent: source committed, plus a check that deployed matches committed — which would have caught 1, 2, and 3 at once.
title: Two edge functions run in production with no source in the repo; both need an authz review

body:
## The bug

`src/components/features/video-upload.tsx` uploads to a storage bucket named **`baseball_videos`**:

```
:131  supabase.storage.from('baseball_videos').upload(fileName, file, …)
:139  supabase.storage.from('baseball_videos').getPublicUrl(fileName)
:152  supabase.storage.from('baseball_videos').remove([fileName])
```

Plus `src/app/baseball/actions/video-classes.ts:463`.

**That bucket does not exist in production.** Buckets that do:

```
avatars, baseball-imports, course-images, documents,
helm-bridge-feedback, lifting-nutrition, logos, recruit-documents
```

The component is reachable — `VideoLibraryClient.tsx:47` imports `VideoUpload` — so any user attempting a video upload gets a "Bucket not found" failure.

## Strong hint about the cause

Every existing bucket uses **hyphens**. The code asks for an **underscore**:

| Convention in Supabase | What the code requests |
|---|---|
| `baseball-imports` | `baseball_videos` |
| `course-images` | |
| `recruit-documents` | |

So this may be a naming mismatch rather than a genuinely missing bucket — except that `baseball-videos` doesn't exist either. Both spellings are absent.

## No migration ever created it

Migrations create buckets for `recruit-documents`, `documents`, `avatars`, `course-images` and the lifting/nutrition set. **None creates a videos bucket.** `20260624002000_baseball_videos_coach_rls_and_recruiting_check.sql` only adds RLS policies to the `baseball_videos` **table**, which is a different object that does exist.

## State

`baseball_videos` table has **5 rows**, newest `2026-07-01` — so rows were registered by some path, but there's no bucket behind the upload flow.

## Why this wasn't just fixed

Creating the bucket requires decisions I shouldn't make unilaterally: public vs private, size limit, allowed MIME types, and the RLS policies on `storage.objects`. Getting those wrong on a bucket holding player video is an exposure risk. It also sits outside the GolfHelm production push this was found during.

## Same class as #1162

Code expects infrastructure that was never provisioned, and nothing fails loudly at deploy time — it fails at the moment a user tries to use the feature. That's the second instance found tonight (the first: 13 realtime subscriptions against an unpublished table).
title: bug(baseball): video upload targets a storage bucket that does not exist

body:
## Symptom

`fetchShotDriversByCategory failed (continuing without shot drivers): AbortError` — **40 occurrences, 2026-07-26 → 07-29**, the single largest warning-severity fingerprint in the feed. It trips the 5s `BEST_EFFORT_QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS` budget, so players silently lose shot-driver enrichment on their CoachHelm themes.

`insight-delivery.ts` already documents the cause and explicitly defers the fix to a reviewed migration. This issue records the measurements so that review has data.

## Measured

`golf_shots` has **four permissive SELECT policies**. Postgres ORs all permissive policies, so every read evaluates all four:

| Policy | Shape |
|---|---|
| `admin_read_all` | `is_admin()` |
| `golf_shots_select` | `EXISTS` correlated on `golf_rounds`, covering own / team-coach / team-player |
| `golf_shots_select_own` | `hole_id IN (SELECT …)` **OR** `round_id IN (SELECT …)` |
| `golf_shots_select_team` | `hole_id IN (SELECT …)` **OR** `round_id IN (SELECT …)` |

The two `IN (SELECT …)` policies materialise id sets rather than correlating per row — the "materialize an org-wide set" the code comment names.

`golf_shots_select` alone appears to already cover all three non-admin cases:
- own → `EXISTS golf_players WHERE user_id = auth.uid()`
- team coach → `is_golf_team_coach(gr.team_id)`
- team player → `is_golf_team_player(gr.team_id)`

## Indexing is NOT the fix

Checked every join column used by these policies — `golf_holes.round_id`, `golf_rounds.player_id`, `golf_rounds.team_id`, `golf_players.user_id`, `golf_shots.round_id`, `golf_shots.hole_id`, `golf_team_members.player_id/team_id`, `golf_coaches.user_id/organization_id`, `golf_teams.organization_id`.

**All 11 already have a leading index.** So there is no additive, zero-risk speedup available. The cost is the redundant policy evaluation itself.

## Why this wasn't just done

Consolidating requires proving the dropped policies are strictly redundant, and one asymmetry blocks a confident call: `_own` and `_team` also match via **`hole_id`**, whereas `golf_shots_select` matches only via `round_id`. Equivalence therefore depends on every shot's `hole_id` resolving to the same round as its `round_id` — including rows with a null `round_id`, and any orphaned holes.

Getting that wrong is either a data leak (too permissive) or players unable to see their own shots (too strict). That is not a change to make unreviewed.

## Suggested approach

1. Prove the `hole_id` vs `round_id` reachability sets are identical, with a query over live data (rows where one path grants and the other does not — expect zero).
2. If zero, drop `golf_shots_select_own` and `golf_shots_select_team`, keeping `golf_shots_select` + `admin_read_all`.
3. Re-measure the abort rate for `insight-delivery.fetchShotDriversByCategory`.
4. Same pattern likely applies elsewhere — Supabase advisors report **137 `multiple_permissive_policies`** findings.

## Context

Related: #1161 fixed a *separate* bug in the same function (a 25,000-row `.limit()` silently truncated to 1,000, so 6 of 33 players had shot drivers computed from an arbitrary subset). That one is merged; this is the remaining performance half.
title: perf(rls): golf_shots has 4 overlapping permissive SELECT policies; 2 materialise id sets

Importing a class schedule from a photo fails in **production** because the Vercel AI Gateway refuses the requested model on the current plan.

Filed by the Helm Mission Control sweep (2026-07-30 ~02:35Z). Read-only triage — no fix attempted.

## What

Creating a golf conversation fails against RLS in **production**.

- Sentry: [JAVASCRIPT-NEXTJS-H6](https://helm-xs.sentry.io/issues/JAVASCRIPT-NEXTJS-H6)
- `Error: Failed to create conversation: new row violates row-level security policy for table "golf_conversations"`
- `POST /golf/dashboard/messages`, action `createGolfConversation`
- **1 event, 1 real user affected**, `2026-07-26T00:49:07Z`
- `environment: production`, `feature_area: messaging`

## Where

Sentry resolves this to first-party code:

`src/app/actions/messages.ts:324` — in `createConversation`

```ts
321       sport,
322       userId: user.id,
323     });
324     throw new Error(`Failed to create conversation: ${convError?.message || 'Unknown error'}`);
325   }
```

i.e. the INSERT into `golf_conversations` is refused by policy, and line 324 is only the rethrow.

## Why it is worth a look despite being 1 event

Low volume, but it is a **write policy refusing a legitimate first-party action in production** — the same class of defect as the cross-tenant RLS work landed in #1102 / #1105. A single occurrence here most likely means the path is rarely exercised, not that it rarely fails: messaging is a core team feature (`golf_messages` / #7 Messaging), so a policy that rejects conversation creation would fail *every* time for whichever role hit it.

Worth determining which role/shape triggered it before assuming it is a one-off — the affected account was an admin-capable user, so a coach or player may fare worse rather than better.

## Suggested first checks (not done here)

1. Read the current INSERT/`WITH CHECK` policies on `golf_conversations` out of live `pg_policies`.
2. Reproduce by role impersonation (`SET LOCAL ROLE authenticated` + `request.jwt.claims` inside a rolled-back transaction) for coach, player, and admin — the house pattern for this.
3. Check whether `createConversation` sets every column the `WITH CHECK` predicate correlates on (a NULL `team_id`/`organization_id` at insert time is the usual cause of this exact error).

/cc labels: `agent:needs-triage`, `workflow:bug`

Filed by the Helm Mission Control sweep (2026-07-30 ~02:35Z). Read-only triage — no fix attempted.

## What

Submitting a golf round in **production** fails to enqueue its CoachHelm follow-up work because Inngest rejects the event key.

- Sentry: [JAVASCRIPT-NEXTJS-HS](https://helm-xs.sentry.io/issues/JAVASCRIPT-NEXTJS-HS)
- `[submitGolfRoundComprehensive.inngestSendFailed] server trace` on `POST /golf/dashboard/rounds/new`
- **3 events, 1 real user affected** (a college coach account, user id `604cadcc…`, Guilford)
- First seen `2026-07-27T19:00Z`, last seen `2026-07-29T19:40Z`
- `environment: production`, `feature_area: coachhelm`, level `warning`, `handled: true`

## Root cause is stated outright in the event

```
Error: Inngest API Error: 404 Event key not found
```

with:

```
trace_message: "Failed to send coachhelm/round.submitted to Inngest,
                falling back to direct postRoundTrigger:
                Inngest API Error: 404 Event key not found"
```

So `INNGEST_EVENT_KEY` in the production environment is **missing, wrong, or belongs to a different Inngest environment**. CLAUDE.md already records that production requires `INNGEST_EVENT_KEY` + `INNGEST_SIGNING_KEY` (see `.env.example`).

## Impact, stated honestly

This degrades rather than breaks: the code catches the failure and falls back to `postRoundTrigger` directly, which is why it is level `warning` and why round submission still appears to succeed to the player. The cost is that the durable-workflow path — the entire reason Inngest was adopted "to replace scattered cron + retry loops" — is silently not in use in production. Anything relying on Inngest retry/durability for `coachhelm/round.submitted` is running without it, with no user-visible signal.

Affected round/player ids are present in the Sentry event context (`roundId`, `playerId`) if a replay is wanted.

## Suggested first checks (not done here)

1. Compare the `INNGEST_EVENT_KEY` value in Vercel's **production** environment against the key in the Inngest dashboard for the production Inngest environment (`vercel env ls`; do not print the value).
2. Confirm `INNGEST_SIGNING_KEY` is set too — a 404 on the event key often accompanies a wholly unconfigured environment.
3. Check whether any other `inngest.send` call sites are failing the same way and simply have no fallback.

/cc labels: `agent:needs-triage`, `workflow:bug`
title: [Sentry] Inngest "404 Event key not found" in production — round submit silently loses the durable path (JAVASCRIPT-NEXTJS-HS)

Filed by the Helm Mission Control sweep (2026-07-30 ~02:35Z). Read-only triage — no fix attempted.

## What

`Error: Server trace error` thrown from `POST /api/webhooks/stripe` in **production** (`helmsportslabs.com`).

- Sentry: [JAVASCRIPT-NEXTJS-J4](https://helm-xs.sentry.io/issues/JAVASCRIPT-NEXTJS-J4)
- **29 events**, 0 users attributed (server-to-server, so users are expected to be 0)
- First seen `2026-07-29T10:02:09Z`, last seen `2026-07-30T01:45:29Z` — **still firing at time of filing**
- Sentry substatus: **escalating**
- `environment: production`, `handled: yes`, region `iad1`, node v24.18.0
- Caller geo is US/Ashburn — consistent with Stripe's own webhook senders

## Why this one is worth attention

This is the only *new, production, still-escalating* error in the sweep window. Everything else new in Sentry over the last 6 days was either dev-only (localhost/turbopack/HeadlessChrome) or fallout from the already-known 2026-07-29 Supabase 522 wedge.

Stripe retries failed webhooks, so a persistently 500-ing endpoint means **billing events are not being durably recorded** even though Stripe considers them delivered-with-failure. Per #1116's description there are six live invoices totalling ~$6,450 in Stripe.

## Stack (top first-party frames)

```
app:///_next/server/app/api/webhooks/stripe/route.js:2:202097 (d2)
app:///_next/server/app/api/webhooks/stripe/route.js:3:5603  (v)
app:///_next/server/app/api/webhooks/stripe/route.js:3:4167  (u)
app:///_next/server/app/api/webhooks/stripe/route.js:3:4063  (t)
```

`server_trace.trace_message` is `"[Filtered]"`, so the underlying message is scrubbed by our own Sentry config — the actual cause is not visible from Sentry alone.

## Suggested first checks (not done here)

1. **Timeline vs. #1116.** #1116 ("persist Stripe invoices — the webhook had nowhere to write") merged `2026-07-29T23:45Z`, and the first J4 event predates it (`10:02Z`). Errors continue *after* that merge — but `main` no longer auto-deploys to production (`git.deploymentEnabled {"*":false}`, since #789), so production may still be running pre-#1116 code. Confirm which release production is actually serving before concluding the fix didn't work.
2. **Un-filter the message.** `trace_message: "[Filtered]"` is hiding the cause. Check the Sentry `beforeSend`/denylist so webhook errors surface their reason.
3. **Signature vs. persistence.** Distinguish `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` signature-verification failure from a write failure against the new `billing_invoices` / `billing_customers` tables.

## Do not

- Do not replay or re-send Stripe events as part of triage.

/cc labels: `agent:needs-triage`, `workflow:bug`
title: [Sentry] Stripe webhook 500s in production — escalating, 29 events, still firing (JAVASCRIPT-NEXTJS-J4)
