Filed by the Mission Control sweep (2026-07-24 ~22:05 UTC).

## Signal

Sentry groups **JAVASCRIPT-NEXTJS-GA** (server, culprit `/golf/dashboard`) and **JAVASCRIPT-NEXTJS-GB** (browser) — 2 events each, first seen 2026-07-24T16:48Z, 0 users impacted.

> Encountered a script tag while rendering React component. Scripts inside React components are never executed when rendering on the client. Consider using template tag instead.

- https://helm-xs.sentry.io/issues/JAVASCRIPT-NEXTJS-GA
- https://helm-xs.sentry.io/issues/JAVASCRIPT-NEXTJS-GB

**Environment caveat:** both events are tagged `environment: development` (localhost, Turbopack, HeadlessChrome). The *code path* is shipped to production, so the underlying behaviour is real — but this has not yet been observed firing in prod.

## Root cause

`ThemeScript` renders a raw inline `<script>`:

`src/components/golf/theme/ThemeScript.tsx:20`

```tsx
export function ThemeScript() {
  return <script dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: BOOT }} suppressHydrationWarning />;
}
```

It is mounted from the golf dashboard **route-group** layout, not the root `<html>` document layout:

`src/app/golf/(dashboard)/layout.tsx:202`

Because it lives in a nested layout, there are two different render paths:

| Entry path | What happens |
|---|---|
| Full document load (hard nav / refresh) | `<script>` is in the streamed SSR HTML -> executes before first paint -> no-FOUC works as designed |
| Client-side (soft) navigation into the dashboard — e.g. login -> dashboard, marketing -> dashboard | React renders the `<script>` on the client, where **it never executes**. React logs the error above. |

So the "theme is correct on the very first painted frame" guarantee documented in the component header silently does not hold on the soft-nav path.

## Impact

Low-to-moderate, cosmetic. `ThemeApplier` (`src/components/golf/theme/ThemeApplier.tsx`, mounted at `layout.tsx:205`) is a client component that re-applies the theme after hydration, so dark mode is not *broken* — it just lands after paint instead of before it. Expected symptom is a brief light-theme flash for dark-mode users entering the dashboard via soft navigation, plus recurring console/Sentry error noise on every such entry.

## Origin

Introduced by #1014 (`feat(golf): premium dark mode + Light/Dark/System control`, commit `773bde38f`, merged 2026-07-23).

## Suggested direction (not applied)

Options, roughly in order of preference:

1. Hoist the boot script into the **root** layout's `<head>` (the document-level layout that owns `<html>`), so it is only ever part of the initial HTML document and never re-rendered by React on a soft nav.
2. Use `next/script` with `strategy="beforeInteractive"`, which Next.js is allowed to hoist into the document.
3. If it must stay in the route-group layout, drop the raw `<script>` and rely solely on `ThemeApplier`, accepting post-hydration application and removing the misleading no-FOUC comment.

Option 1 preserves the actual no-FOUC intent. Note the storage key must stay in sync with `THEME_STORAGE_KEY` in `src/lib/golf/theme.ts`, per the component header.

---
Filed automatically by the Helm Mission Control sweep. Read-only investigation — no code changed.
title: [Sentry] No-FOUC ThemeScript renders client-side on soft nav — script never executes (JAVASCRIPT-NEXTJS-GA/GB)

> **DRAFT — not sent.** Prepared by Helm Mission Control for internal review. Nothing in this update has been shared with any partner. **Do not forward or send externally until a human has reviewed and approved it.**

**Notion copy:** https://app.notion.com/p/3a78daf2b331819a80f6c47c00808910

*Reporting window: 2026-07-17 → 2026-07-24*

---

## State of Helm

This was the largest shipping week of the quarter. **GolfHelm** completed a full visual and structural redesign of its three most important surfaces — the CoachHelm AI dashboard, Stats, and Round Review — and Helm now has a real public marketing presence for the first time (landing page, About, Products, Pricing).

The week had two distinct halves. The first half closed out the production-readiness audit that has been running for two weeks: five remediation waves fixing several hundred verified findings across correctness, accessibility, mobile layout, and AI content quality. The second half was net-new build — the premium dashboard rebuild, dark mode, a redesigned account and password-reset experience, and the new marketing site.

**Production is live and serving.** The live site and its health endpoint both respond normally, twenty-five production releases shipped cleanly, and no build failed. The one honest caveat is telemetry: our production error volume rose sharply this week, and roughly 60% of it traces to two backend clusters that affect zero users but do need attention. Details in Telemetry below.

The headline: **60 substantive pull requests in seven days**, touching roughly 1,750 files — the redesign landed, and the audit backlog closed.

---

## What shipped

**72 pull requests merged (60 substantive, 12 automated dependency and documentation updates).** The work clustered into seven themes:

- **The Spine & Stage redesign — shipped.** CoachHelm, Stats, and Round Review were rebuilt onto one coherent structural language, followed by a premium pass on the CoachHelm dashboard and a ground-up rebuild of the Round Review shot visuals. Stats gained a purpose-built visual kit (shot-dispersion fields, distance-band histograms, putting make-curves) so each drill-down has one signature, readable hero chart instead of a generic graph. This is the surface coaches and players spend the most time in, and it now looks and behaves like a finished product.

- **A real public marketing site.** Built and shipped a new landing page plus About, Products, and Pricing — replacing what was previously a thin placeholder. Two follow-up polish passes fixed mobile fit, scroll behavior, and copy, and a consolidation pass removed a duplicate competing landing implementation (~5,000 lines of dead code).

- **Production-readiness audit — closed out.** Five remediation waves shipped: critical trust bugs, mobile recomposition and overflow, the AI content contract, dead controls and accessibility, plus a final batch of 20 verified fix packages covering more than 150 findings. Separately, a 23-fix accuracy pass corrected stats depth, CoachHelm wiring, and goal tracking.

- **New capability for coaches and players.** Class schedules can now be imported directly from a screenshot or photo instead of typed in by hand. The player dashboard's top slot became a swipeable day-by-day calendar. Coaches gained a triage desk that surfaces previously discarded team shot-weaknesses, and CoachHelm gained category-level insights.

- **Account experience and dark mode.** A premium password-reset flow (pages plus branded email), branded signup-confirmation and email-change messages, a full Light/Dark/System theme control with a properly designed dark mode, and a settings cleanup that removed dead controls and clarified confusing copy.

- **Stability and load hardening.** Fixed a session bug that was signing users out after roughly two minutes, prevented authenticated-route timeouts, eliminated a slow multi-stage cold start on the player dashboard, and hardened the demo environment to survive a mass email send without logouts or crashes. Also fixed a caching bug that had been serving stale builds to mobile users.

- **Sales and CRM instrumentation.** A ten-lens audit of the CRM produced four critical fixes and thirty smaller ones; the demo funnel gained visitor tracking, a pricing nudge, a step preview, and a daily send cap; and the outbound template designer now lints messages for spam-compliance as they are written.

On the engineering-process side, the two paid third-party AI code reviewers were retired in favor of our own deterministic review gate — same coverage on the rules that matter, without the queue time that had become the slowest step in shipping.

---

## Open PRs

**Four pull requests are open — all automated dependency bumps. No human feature work is blocked or waiting on review.**

- **#1039, #1040, #1041** — routine dependency updates in a developer tooling directory (not shipped to users).
- **#1031** — a minor build-tool patch update.

Each is awaiting standard CI, not human decision.

---

## Blockers

**No launch-blocking issues in the live product.** Every user-facing surface shipped this week is deployed and serving. Three items are worth flagging as active engineering follow-ups rather than blockers:

1. **Two backend error clusters need triage.** A recurring timeout on our internal health probe and a failing telemetry write inside a background refresh job together account for most of this week's error volume. Neither affects a user session — but both are noisy enough to obscure real signal, so they are first in the queue next week.

2. **Two redesigned dashboard routes showed rendering mismatches** after the premium pass. These produce a brief re-render rather than a visible failure, and no user reports have come in, but they are a correctness debt from a fast-moving redesign week and will be closed out.

3. **Three production deployments were blocked before building** (out of 28 attempted). These are pipeline-hygiene events, not build failures — no deploy in the window failed to compile — but the pattern is worth cleaning up so release status stays unambiguous.

Production deploys remain intentionally **on-demand** — promoted deliberately rather than auto-shipped on every merge. That is a stability choice, and it held up under an unusually heavy merge week.

---

## Telemetry

**Production health — green.** 28 production releases were attempted in the window; **25 shipped successfully and none failed to build.** The live site and its health endpoint both respond normally, with sub-second response times. The current production build is serving the latest merged work.

**Errors — volume up, user impact minimal.** We recorded **792 production error events over the last 7 days**, against 113 in the prior week. That is a real increase and we are not going to soften it — but the composition matters:

- **~60% of the volume is two zero-user backend clusters** — an internal health-probe timeout (245 events) and a failing telemetry write in a background refresh job (233 events). Neither is a user-facing failure; both are infrastructure noise that needs a fix.
- **Most of the remainder is internal server-trace instrumentation** captured during the redesign, plus rendering mismatches on two dashboard routes — all recording zero affected users.
- **Confirmed user impact across the entire week: 2 users**, on two isolated clusters (a calendar action and a round-review save).

The honest read is that this was a very heavy build week — 60 substantive merges, roughly 1,750 files touched — and the error count reflects both a genuinely busier system and much broader instrumentation, not a degradation in what coaches and players experience. The two-user figure is the number that best describes real-world impact, and the two noisy backend clusters are already scoped for next week.

---

## Next week

- **Quiet the telemetry.** Fix the health-probe timeout and the background-job telemetry write, so error volume reflects real problems again.
- **Close the redesign's correctness debt** — resolve the rendering mismatches on the two affected dashboard routes.
- **Continue the mobile and accessibility sweep** across the surfaces the redesign has not yet reached.
- **Finish the marketing site** — remaining polish on Products and Pricing, plus performance work on the new landing page.
- **Advance billing infrastructure** — wire durable persistence for the school-invoicing scaffold.
- **Harden CRM and outbound instrumentation**, continuing the work the ten-lens audit started.

---

Detected by the **Helm Mission Control sweep** — Supabase postgres logs (project `qmnssrrolpinvwjjnufo`), recurring `ERROR` in bursts across the last 2h window (sampled occurrences span ~11:34–13:03Z on 2026-07-23; latest ~13:03Z).

- **Error**: `permission denied for function heartbeat`
- **Level**: Error · recurring · **Users affected**: 0

### Root cause (verified this sweep)
`public.heartbeat()` is owned by `postgres` and grants `EXECUTE` only to `authenticated` and `service_role`:

```
acl: postgres=X/postgres, authenticated=X/postgres, service_role=X/postgres
```

The app calls it via `supabase.rpc('heartbeat')` in `src/hooks/use-presence.ts:20`. The recurring denial is the **`anon` role** — presence heartbeats fired by unauthenticated visitors, or sessions whose JWT expired / logged out while the hook is still mounted. `anon` has no `EXECUTE` grant, so Postgres logs `permission denied for function heartbeat` on every such tick.

### Fix options
- **Preferred:** gate the presence heartbeat behind a confirmed authenticated session in `use-presence.ts` (don't fire `rpc('heartbeat')` when there is no user) — also removes the wasted round-trips.
- Or `GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.heartbeat() TO anon;` if anonymous presence is intended (unlikely).

### Impact
No user-facing impact — log noise + wasted RPCs. Low severity but persistent.

_Filed by `helm-mission-control-sweep`. Read-only diagnosis; no DB/schema changes made._
title: [Supabase] Postgres: permission denied for function heartbeat — anon presence RPC (use-presence.ts)

These six items surfaced during the parallel audit-fix fleet. Each fix agent stayed inside its package's file-ownership allowlist (to keep the packages conflict-free for parallel work), so items whose root cause lives in a **shared primitive, server action, SQL function, or the nav registry** could not be closed in that pass. None is a regression — each is an existing gap, now with an exact diagnosis. Filed here so nothing is lost. See PR #975 for the fixes that did land.

---

### 1. `documents #151` — coach-only doc metadata via event/announcement surfaces (defense-in-depth, LOW)
`getEventDocuments()` (`src/app/golf/actions/event-documents.ts`) and the `docDetails` lookup in `src/app/golf/actions/announcements.ts` embed/select `golf_documents` with no `is_public` filter.
**Already gated at the RLS layer** — migration `20260621041833_golf_documents_select_is_public.sql` (Wave A·A2): `is_golf_team_player(team_id) AND is_public = true`, so a player's read returns null for coach-only docs and the impl filters nulls. Not a live leak; add the explicit `.eq('is_public', true)` player-branch as belt-and-suspenders + a parity trace.

### 2. `ask-coachhelm #76` — chat narrates wrong roster count (MEDIUM)
`get_team_overview` in `src/lib/coachhelm/v3/chat/tools.ts` filters roster members to those with a well-formed joined `golf_players` record, silently dropping any row whose FK join is null/malformed — producing "all 6 players" against a true 7-player roster. Fix: surface a distinct `total_roster_size` (or fail loud) + a test asserting the tool's count matches a direct DB roster-count query.

### 3. `tasks #49` — coaches have no working "mark complete" (MEDIUM)
`completeTask` (`src/app/golf/actions/tasks.ts`) requires the caller to have a `golf_players` row, which coaches never have, so any coach-facing button wired to it always fails. Needs a **new auth-checked server action** (verify coach owns the task's team via `org_id`, verify the target player's assignment, then complete on their behalf) + a coach-context regression test. Deliberately NOT wired to the failing action (would violate the file's "no dishonest control" rule).

### 4. `coachhelm-signals` — shared-primitive polish (#62/#70/#71/#73) (MEDIUM, visual)
- **#62** `MetricCard.tsx` (NumberFlow) — overlapping digits mid-transition. Needs a transition-disable/plain-format prop.
- **#70** `Toolbar.tsx` — sticky Signals filter toolbar not opaque when stuck (`--fw-glass-bg-strong` 88% mechanism exists; confirm it's engaging or forward a className override from `SignalsToolbar`).
- **#71** `FairwayAspectDrillDown.tsx` — weakness drill-in rows need min height/gap breathing room.
- **#73** `Ribbon.tsx` — yardage strokes-vs-par chart needs labeled visible axes (has aria-label only).

### 5. `qualifiers #89/#90/#147` (MEDIUM)
- **#89/#90** `FairwayQualifyingWorkspace.tsx` (orphaned — owned by no package) — its `STATE_META`/`StateBar` renders only `selection_state`, never cross-checking the play `status`; SlotLeaderboard "Locked" badge has no tie-break guard at 0-rounds/E ties. Reconcile the two state machines from one source + a tie-break rule. (Detail page now shows a scoped InlineNotice warning as mitigation.)
- **#147** `src/lib/golf/nav-registry.ts` — `PLAYER_TEAM_TABS` groups `my-qualifiers` into the same "Team" hub as Roster/Team Info/Team Hub, so `FairwayHubSubNav` shows all four as one strip on the My Qualifiers route. Move `my-qualifiers` to its own single-destination rail item.

### 6. `team-hub #152` — announcements count parity (LOW-MEDIUM)
`get_player_hub_announcements()` RPC (`20260527000000_prod_public_baseline.sql`) hard-filters to `published_at >= now()-30d LIMIT 10`, capped to 5 in its `visible` CTE, and `AnnouncementsList` (`hub-parts.tsx`) further `.slice(0,3)` — while the dedicated page's `getAnnouncementsWithMeta()` has no window, so the Team Hub tab under-counts. Fix in the RPC/`page.tsx`/`hub-parts.tsx` (all out of the package's scope). Team Hub empty state was made honest ("No recent announcements" + 30-day copy + link) as mitigation.

## Where
Focus Areas on the player CoachHelm page — the underlying focus-area / insight generator (data), surfaced by `FocusAreasGrid.tsx`. NOTE: the card **layout** overlap is already fixed (#967, live) — this is a CONTENT/data issue, not layout.

## Evidence
IMG_4976: "Short (50-100) Shots" and "Long (190-220) Shots" BOTH show `0 yd from target` and the identical recommendation "You tend to leave shots short. Consider taking one more club or committing to a fuller swing."

## The problems
1. **Duplicate generic recommendation** across two distinct shot bands (50-100 yd and 190-220 yd) — the same canned sentence for very different clubs/situations reads as templated, not intelligent.
2. **"0 yd from target"** is a nonsensical headline value for a flagged focus area — if the distance-from-target is 0, why is it a focus area, and why show 0? Either the value is wrong/unpopulated or the framing is off.

## How it should behave
- Each focus area's recommendation should be specific to its band (a 50-100 yd wedge miss ≠ a 190-220 yd long-iron/hybrid miss). If the generator can't say something band-specific, it should say less, not repeat a generic line.
- The headline metric ("0 yd from target") must be a real, meaningful number or be replaced by the actual signal that made this a focus area.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] No two focus areas show the identical recommendation sentence when they represent different shot bands.
- [ ] The headline value is meaningful (no "0 yd from target" on a flagged area).
- [ ] Verified against prod (rinin376).

`src/components/golf/coachhelm/player/CompositeRatingCard.tsx` — GAME STRENGTH composite + sub-scores.

## Evidence
IMG_4977: composite 50/100; sub-scores Tee Game **50**, Approach **57**, Short Game **53**, Putting **42**, Scoring **51** — all clustered tightly around 50.

## The problem
A near-uniform ~50 across every category is the classic signature of **default / placeholder values** (a 0-100 rating that falls back to the midpoint when it lacks real inputs). For a player who elsewhere has real, differentiated data (see the shot-analysis deep dive), flat ~50s either (a) are genuinely uninformative and shouldn't be shown as authoritative scores, or (b) indicate the composite isn't actually computing from the player's data.

Per the CoachHelm honesty rule (never surface a hollow/authoritative-looking number), this needs to be either a real, differentiated computation or an honest "not enough to rate this yet" state — not a wall of 50s presented as a verdict.

## What to check / how it should behave
- Confirm whether these sub-scores are computed from the player's data or defaulting to ~50. If defaulting, gate them behind the honest insufficient-data state instead of rendering midpoint numbers.
- If computed, verify the scale/normalization — real per-category strength should spread, not cluster at the midpoint.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] GAME STRENGTH either shows real, differentiated sub-scores or an honest insufficient-data state — never placeholder ~50s presented as a rating.
- [ ] Documented which case applied (default vs computed) and the fix.
- [ ] Verified against prod (rinin376).
title: [player-coachhelm][honesty] GAME STRENGTH sub-scores look like placeholder ~50 defaults

## Where
`src/components/fairway/pages/coachhelm/FairwayPlayerCoachHelm.tsx` (the cockpit collapse logic) vs `ShotAnalysisCard.tsx` (Deep dive). Data sources: `initialShotAnalytics` (getPlayerShotAnalytics) vs `shotData`.

## Evidence
- Cockpit (IMG earlier / seg-01): "Your shot cockpit — Warming up … as more tracked rounds come through" AND the micro-readouts read "NO PUTTS — 0 OF 1".
- Deep dive (IMG_4979): the SAME player clearly HAS rich shot data — **172 tee shots**, Dead Zones (275-300y, 50-75y), Key Weaknesses with real SG deficits, Resilience 1.1, Scramble Rate 31%.

## The problem
The redesign (#967) collapses the cockpit's forecast/radar/readouts to a single "Warming up" panel when `shot.roundsAnalyzed === 0`. But this player is NOT data-less — the deep-dive `shotData` is fully populated. So **`initialShotAnalytics` is returning empty/0 while `shotData` returns real data for the same player**. The cockpit is honest about the source it reads, but that source is wrong/empty, so the page tells the player "warming up / no putts" while simultaneously showing them 172 analyzed tee shots below. That's incoherent and hides real data.

## Root-cause directions
- Why does `getPlayerShotAnalytics` (the cockpit's `initialShotAnalytics`) return `roundsAnalyzed: 0` when shot-level data clearly exists and `shotData` sees it? Different query, different table, a filter (date window? tracked-only?), or a loader that silently failed. Trace both loaders on rinin376.
- If the two are meant to be the same underlying data, they should agree; if they're genuinely different scopes, the cockpit's "Warming up" copy must not claim "no tracked rounds" when tracked-shot analysis exists.

## Also (same card, honesty)
Key Weaknesses surfaces bands with **6 shots** and **5 shots** as top weaknesses (IMG_4979) — tiny samples ranked as "key". Add a minimum-sample guard or a "small sample" flag so 5-6-shot bands don't outrank a 172-shot signal.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The cockpit does NOT show "Warming up / no putts" for a player who has populated shot analytics; the readouts + radar reflect the same data the deep dive uses (or the copy is corrected to match the true scope).
- [ ] Root cause of the `initialShotAnalytics` empty result documented + fixed.
- [ ] Key Weaknesses applies a minimum-sample threshold (or clearly flags small-sample bands).
- [ ] Verified against prod (rinin376).
title: [player-coachhelm][data] Cockpit shows "Warming up" but the player HAS shot data — initialShotAnalytics vs shotData source mismatch

body:
## Where
`src/components/golf/coachhelm/player/FairwayTrendBrain.tsx` — the "FORM · SCORE TO PAR" card.

## Evidence
IMG_4978.

## The problems
1. **Self-contradiction in one card.** The headline reads **"Your scoring is sliding"** (red) with all three windows (Long range / Medium / Recent) marked **↓ declining** — but the footer reads **"4-round hot streak · 23.5 strokes below your average"** (green, positive). A card cannot credibly say the player is both sliding and on a hot streak in the same viewport. The two signals need reconciling or clearly reframing (e.g. "declining trend, but the last 4 rounds buck it").
2. **Implausible magnitude.** "**23.5 strokes below your average**" is not a real per-round figure — no golfer averages 23.5 strokes better than their own average for 4 rounds. This looks like a calculation bug (summing a delta across rounds, a unit error, or comparing against the wrong baseline). Needs root-causing in the hot-streak/trend math, not just the copy.
3. **Cramped 3-column rows on mobile.** The middle annotations ("· the real signal", "· small sample — noisy") wrap awkwardly between the "declining" label and the % column. The row layout needs to breathe or restructure at 390px.
4. **Em dashes in copy** ("raw scoring — not course-adjusted", "small sample — noisy") — house style avoids em dashes in UI copy.

## How it should behave (architecture)
- One honest verdict per card. If the long/medium windows decline but the recent 4 buck it, SAY that as a single coherent read, don't stack a red headline over a green footer.
- The hot-streak metric must be a sane per-round figure with a correct baseline; add a guard/clamp and a unit assertion so an impossible magnitude can never render.
- Restructure the window rows for 390px (label + trend on one line, annotation below, % right-aligned and never colliding).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The card never shows contradictory verdicts simultaneously.
- [ ] The hot-streak / delta figure is a plausible per-round number with the correct baseline (add a test around the calc).
- [ ] Window rows read cleanly at 390px; no awkward mid-row wraps.
- [ ] No em dashes in the copy.
title: [player-coachhelm] FORM/trend self-contradicts: "scoring is sliding" vs "4-round hot streak, 23.5 strokes below average" (+ implausible number)

## Where
`src/components/golf/coachhelm/player/CompositeRatingCard.tsx` (GAME STRENGTH, "50 / 100") and the Resilience ring in `src/components/golf/coachhelm/player/ShotAnalysisCard.tsx` ("1.1 · Good recovery"). Both use the same hand-rolled SVG progress ring pattern.

## Evidence
IMG_4977 (GAME STRENGTH gauge), IMG_4979 (Resilience gauge).

## Root cause (confirmed in source)
`CompositeRatingCard.tsx` ~line 143-165 draws a full-circle SVG ring:
- **Track circle**: `className="stroke-warm-100"` — warm-100 is near-cream, essentially invisible on the cream card background.
- **Value arc**: an animated `m.circle` with `strokeDasharray/strokeDashoffset` filling to the value %.

At value = 50/100 the orange arc fills ~half the circle; because the grey track is invisible, the eye sees only a floating half-arc, which reads as a **broken / incomplete C-shape open on the left** rather than an intentional gauge. (Same pattern → same effect for the Resilience ring.)

## How it should fill (architecture)
- The **track must be visible** at a proper contrast (a real neutral ring, e.g. a warm/inset token with enough delta from the card), so a partial fill reads as "half of a full gauge," not a broken arc.
- Decide the gauge intent explicitly: a full 360° ring (track always a full circle) vs a 270° speedometer arc. Whichever, make the unfilled portion legibly present.
- Cap-and-rotation should place the "start" of the arc at a natural anchor (top or bottom), not leave an ambiguous left gap.
- Fold this into the Fairway-native gauge used by the cockpit (#969) rather than keeping bespoke SVG rings, so every gauge on the page looks like one family.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] At any value (including 50/100 and 1.1), the gauge reads as an intentional, complete gauge — visible track + fill — never a floating broken arc.
- [ ] GAME STRENGTH and Resilience use the same gauge treatment.
- [ ] reduced-motion safe; verified on mobile against prod (rinin376).
title: [player-coachhelm][mobile] Ring gauge renders as a broken C-shape — track stroke is invisible (GAME STRENGTH + Resilience)

body:
## The core problem (Nick: "like the old shell or something")
The player CoachHelm page is currently **two different products stacked on top of each other**:

- **Top half (redesigned, Fairway):** the insight hero, the "Themes to work on" cards, Focus Areas, the shot-cockpit — flat matte instrument panels, the Fairway type scale, calm hierarchy. This got the recent redesign (#967).
- **Bottom half (legacy V3 "old shell"):** everything under `PERFORMANCE OVERVIEW` — the **GAME STRENGTH** card (`CompositeRatingCard.tsx`), the **FORM · SCORE TO PAR** card (`FairwayTrendBrain.tsx`), and the **Deep dive** shot-analysis (`ShotAnalysisCard.tsx`). These were deliberately kept "mounted UNCHANGED" during #967 and are visibly a different, older design language — different card treatment, different gauges, different label style, heavier chrome.

The seam between the two is jarring on mobile: you scroll from a premium cockpit into a stack of legacy cards.

## Evidence
IMG_4977 (GAME STRENGTH), IMG_4978 (FORM · SCORE TO PAR), IMG_4979 (Deep dive / shot analysis).

## Components in scope
- `src/components/golf/coachhelm/player/CompositeRatingCard.tsx` (GAME STRENGTH ring + sub-score bars)
- `src/components/golf/coachhelm/player/FairwayTrendBrain.tsx` (FORM · SCORE TO PAR trend rows)
- `src/components/golf/coachhelm/player/ShotAnalysisCard.tsx` (Deep dive: Dead Zones, Key Weaknesses, Resilience, Scramble Rate)
- Host: `src/components/fairway/pages/coachhelm/FairwayPlayerCoachHelm.tsx` (the "Performance overview" + "Deep dive" sections)

## How it should look (architecture / desired state)
The page should read as **one coherent Fairway cockpit top to bottom** — a single design language, one card system, one type scale, one gauge/chart vocabulary.
- Rebuild (or re-skin) the three legacy cards in the Fairway kit: matte `InstrumentPanel`/`Surface` treatment, the 9-step type scale, `font-fw-*`, cream/warm/primary/accent tokens only, rounded-2xl, the same "honest awaiting" states as the cockpit.
- Reuse the cockpit's existing primitives (Readout, InstrumentPanel, the Fairway chart components) instead of the bespoke SVG rings and ad-hoc bar rows in these cards.
- Keep every real datum and every honest empty state; this is a presentation/design-system unification, not a data change.
- Decide the section's information architecture deliberately: GAME STRENGTH (composite + sub-scores), FORM/trend, and shot-analysis deep-dive are three distinct reads — rank and space them like the top of the page does, don't just restyle in place.

## Sub-issues (tracked separately, all surfaced by these same screenshots)
- #970 ring gauge reads as a broken C-shape (invisible track)
- #971 FORM/trend contradiction + implausible "23.5 strokes below average"
- #973 GAME STRENGTH sub-scores look like placeholder ~50 defaults
(and the cockpit/shot-data mismatch in #972)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Scrolling the full player CoachHelm page on mobile shows ONE consistent design language end to end — no visible "old shell" seam.
- [ ] The three legacy cards use Fairway tokens/primitives (no bespoke SVG ring, no legacy card chrome, no off-scale type).
- [ ] All existing data + honest empty states preserved.
- [ ] Verified against prod (rinin376) via the headless capture harness.
title: [player-coachhelm][architecture] Lower half of the page is the un-redesigned "old shell" — unify into the Fairway cockpit language

body:
## Where
Player-facing golf surface, mobile (390px). The putting **make-rate by distance** line chart (green solid = you, grey dashed = PGA/reference; distance bands 0-3 / 3-5 / 5-10 / 10-15 / 15-25 / 25+ ft). Likely component: a putting make-rate line chart rendered in `src/components/fairway/pages/coachhelm/FairwayStatsCockpit.tsx` or the CoachHelm shot-analysis deep dive — **confirm the exact chart at fix time** (grep the "0-3 ft" band labels).

## Evidence
IMG_4975. This is the "text isn't rendering for the chart" report.

## The problem
1. **X-axis category labels overlap/collide.** They render as `0-3 ft  3-5 ft  5-10 f10-15 ft15-25 f25+ ft` — adjacent labels run into each other because six ~6-char labels do not fit the 390px plot width at the current font size and there is no rotation / abbreviation / wrapping / interval strategy.
2. **Y-axis tick labels are clipped at the left edge.** Only a partial "0" is visible; the numbers are cut off by the chart's left margin / the page gutter. The plot has no left margin reserved for the axis, or the chart overflows its container to the left.
3. **The plot overflows its container** — the green line runs off the left edge, confirming the chart is wider than its box and is being clipped rather than fit-to-width.

## How it should look (architecture)
- The chart must fit **within** its card on a 390px viewport: reserve an explicit left margin for y-axis labels, and never let the plot area exceed the card's content box (the card, not the chart, owns horizontal bounds; if anything scrolls, it's an inner `overflow-x:auto` container, never the page body).
- Six dense x labels on mobile need a real strategy: rotate ~-35°, OR abbreviate (`0-3`, `3-5`, … dropping the repeated "ft" into the axis title), OR thin to every other tick with the rest on tap. Pick one and apply it responsively (full labels on desktop, condensed on mobile).
- Value callouts (61%, 35%, …) must not sit on top of gridlines/other labels.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] At 390px, every x-axis label is fully readable with no character overlap between adjacent labels.
- [ ] Y-axis tick labels are fully visible (not clipped by the left edge).
- [ ] The chart's drawn area stays inside its card; page body does not scroll horizontally.
- [ ] Verified against prod with a real player (rinin376) via the headless capture harness at `audit/product-audit/`.
title: [player-coachhelm][mobile] Putting make-rate chart: x-axis labels collide and y-axis labels clip off-screen

1. **Uneven cards**: DetailGrid — the most-reused card (25+ instances) — wraps its bordered Surface in `flex flex-col` with NO h-full/flex-1, so it never stretches to match grid siblings (worst: Approach tab's 2-row vs 8-row pair). ONE className fix evens every tab.
2. **"Not a lot of color"**: all neutral tokens are near-zero-chroma cream/graphite and DetailGrid renders values colorless. Add a `tone` prop that colors values green/amber when crossing thresholds vs PGA/team baseline — instantly turns walls of graphite numbers into readable signal. body:
Deep code trace of the full insight pipeline (round-submit after() → postRoundTrigger → 18 Tier-1 generators + composite synthesis → upsertInsight; nightly roster-sweep re-runs the same engine; lifecycle cron ONLY ages rows out). The engine design is sound — staleness comes from five specific gaps:

1. **coachhelm-safety-net and coachhelm-validation run WEEKLY** (vercel.json `0 4 * * 0`) while their own file headers say every-30-min/hourly. Any round whose after() trigger dies (cold start, timeout — silent) waits **up to 7 days** for recovery instead of 30 minutes. Meanwhile the lifecycle cron keeps archiving old insights nightly, so the visible effect is exactly "everything is stale and nothing replaces it." → src/app/api/cron/coachhelm-safety-net/route.ts vs vercel.json.
2. **alert_posture='silent' sets the player's confidence threshold to +Infinity** — permanently and invisibly blocks ALL new insights for that one player while teammates update fine. Matches "SOME insights don't update" verbatim. Needs a visible "Insights muted for this player" banner. → insights.ts posture→threshold mapping.
3. **Legacy insight path dedups on (player_id, insight_type) while any active row exists** (+3-day cooldown) — same card text survives new rounds. Native Tier-1 path already does value-aware 5%-movement refresh; port legacy paths onto it. → convertV2ToInsightRecord path.
4. **Race on round submit**: TWO independent after() callbacks — stats-cache refresh and insight engine — with no ordering; several v3 generators read golf_player_stats_cache. Insight run can compute on pre-round numbers. Chain them.
5. **Roster-sweep skips any player analyzed within 12h** (per-player, not per-round) — a failed second-round-of-the-day stays unanalyzed until the (weekly) safety net. Skip should check the LATEST round's coachhelm_analyzed_at.

Bonus mind-trick fixed: the Brief's "updated Jun 8, 8:00 PM" is **not a pipeline timestamp** — it's the last round's date-only round_date parsed as UTC midnight and localized (hence a fake 8:00 PM). Show the date only, or a real analysis timestamp.

Also: golf_coach_insights dismiss state lives in THREE columns kept in sync by convention (status + dismissed + dismissed_at) — one future writer away from readers disagreeing.
title: [QA] Why insights go stale — five concrete causes, ranked (safety-net cron weekly, silent posture, legacy dedup, cache race, sweep skip)

## State of Helm

Helm is in a strong, high-velocity build phase across both products — **BaseballHelm** (college baseball recruiting + team management) and **GolfHelm** (team management + the CoachHelm AI layer). Production is healthy and stable, shipping is fast and controlled, and the team spent the week converting "it works" into "it's trustworthy": reconciling data so every number a coach or player sees traces back to one source of truth, hardening the mobile experience end-to-end, and standing up an internal observability layer ("Helm Bridge") that now catches issues within minutes of a release.

The headline this week is **depth over flash** — roughly 95 substantive pull requests, most of them focused on correctness, data integrity, and polish rather than net-new surface area.

## What shipped

**~95 substantive pull requests merged this week (97 total, including 2 automated documentation refreshes).** The work clustered into six themes:

- **BaseballHelm data-integrity push.** A large, deliberate effort to make every baseball statistic consistent everywhere it appears. Player profiles, rosters, dashboards, and the CoachHelm engine were all migrated onto a single shared stats layer, with drift-detection tests so the numbers can't silently disagree again. This is foundational trust work ahead of wider rollout.
- **Full mobile overhaul.** A sweep across both products fixing phone layouts at real device widths — tap-target sizing, bottom-navigation clipping, responsive tables and cards, and loading states. The result is a product that feels native on a phone, not a desktop app squeezed down.
- **Helm Bridge (internal operations layer).** New visibility instruments for the team — feature-adoption views, per-team health signals, a release ledger that grades each deploy, and **release-aware auto-resolution** that automatically closes stale issues once a fix has been live and quiet. Error monitoring was significantly expanded across both products.
- **Public marketing pages.** Built out the public-facing BaseballHelm marketing page (previously a bare redirect) and fixed a rendering issue that affected public profile pages.
- **GolfHelm navigation + CoachHelm.** Unified the stats and CoachHelm areas onto one canonical navigation model, removing several conflicting menus and dead links, plus continued refinement of AI insight quality and empty-state handling.
- **Correctness, security, and honesty sweeps.** Fixed dozens of broken or stranded user flows, tightened a privacy boundary on a recruiting surface, hardened the demo-request intake path, and removed UI elements that displayed labels or columns not backed by real data — the product now shows only what it can actually stand behind.

Underneath all of this: expanded automated test coverage and CI gates (mobile-viewport regression checks, an authenticated route smoke test promoted to a required merge gate) and a "de-vibe" cleanup pass removing dead code and stray files.

## Open PRs

Only two pull requests are open, both **automated and low-stakes** — no human feature work is currently blocked:

- **#901 — automated documentation refresh** (bot-generated inventory update), awaiting routine CI checks.
- **#857 — dependency bump** (a minor `postcss` patch from Dependabot), needs a routine rebase.

## Blockers

**No external-facing blockers.** The live product has no known launch-blocking issues this week. Remaining open items are internal and routine:

- The two automated PRs above are pending standard CI, not human review.
- A small number of internal engineering follow-ups (a background-job tuning item and non-blocking CI advisory checks) are tracked in our ops board and do not affect the live product.

Production deploys are intentionally **on-demand** (promoted deliberately rather than auto-shipped on every merge), which keeps the live environment stable and predictable.

## Telemetry

**Production health — green.** Multiple production releases shipped this week and the current live build is healthy. There were **no failed production deployments** in the window; the current build is serving the latest merged work.

**Errors — low volume, well understood.** We tracked **113 error events over the last 7 days**, with single-digit users affected on the largest genuine cluster. The week-over-week count rose versus the prior week, but that increase is driven almost entirely by **newly expanded error instrumentation deployed mid-week** — we are now capturing far more signal into our own monitoring, which is a deliberate improvement, not a regression in the live product. The large majority of captured events are either zero-user internal/admin traces or **expected guard conditions** (for example, the read-only boundary on our sales-demo environment, expired-session redirects, and stale mobile push-notification tokens).

One genuine bug did reach production this week — a crash on two internal admin panels — and it demonstrates the new monitoring working as intended: **our own Bridge caught it within roughly two minutes of the deploy, and it was fixed and shipped the same day.**

## Next week

- **Wrap up the BaseballHelm data-integrity work** so all baseball stats sit on one verified source of truth, and prepare the associated historical-stats backfill (staged, pending final go-ahead).
- **Continue mobile polish** across the remaining surfaces.
- **Extend Helm Bridge coverage** and tune the new release-aware auto-resolution now that it is live.
- **Advance billing infrastructure** — wire persistence for the school-invoicing scaffold that was stood up recently.

| Sentry | Error | Culprit | Events | First/Last seen |
|--------|-------|---------|--------|-----------------|

## Action

Promote #902 to production (Vercel Redeploy/Promote or `vercel --prod`), then resolve `NEXTJS-CJ` / `NEXTJS-7` and close this issue. No new code change required.

## Summary
Sentry issue **JAVASCRIPT-NEXTJS-C8** — "Server trace error" — recurring on the CoachHelm roster-sweep cron.

- **Source:** Sentry (org `helm-xs`) — https://helm-xs.sentry.io/issues/JAVASCRIPT-NEXTJS-C8
- **Culprit:** `GET /api/cron/coachhelm-roster-sweep`
- **Occurrences:** 3 · **Users impacted:** 0
- **First seen:** 2026-07-13T03:45:56Z · **Last seen:** 2026-07-15T03:45:54Z
- **Level:** error · **handled:** yes · **environment:** production
- **Release:** `760b626c53e1e152629d51fe8d83b9a5c793a661`

## Root cause (from the captured `server_trace`)
> `synthesizeForPlayer: rule front_9_starter compose/upsert threw for cd822fe9-…: upsertInsight: evidence.sample_n=3 < 5; refusing to emit`

The v3 composite synthesis path (`src/lib/coachhelm/v3/composite/synthesis.ts:433` → `synthesizeForPlayer`) hits the **minimum-sample-size guard** (`sample_n=3 < 5`) for rule `front_9_starter` and **throws** to refuse emitting a low-confidence insight. That rejection propagates up through `Promise.all` in `src/app/api/cron/coachhelm-roster-sweep/route.ts:124` and is captured by `logServerException` → `captureServerTrace` (`src/lib/server-error-logger.ts:313`), landing in Sentry as an `error`-level "Server trace error".

The refusal itself is **correct** — the min-sample guard is intended insight-quality behavior. The defect is that an *expected* control-flow refusal is thrown and logged at `error` severity, producing recurring Sentry noise on the cron rather than a soft skip.

## Suggested fix direction
Make the min-sample refusal a soft-skip (return a `{ skipped: 'insufficient_sample' }`-style result the caller ignores) instead of a thrown error, **or** classify it as a benign control-flow marker in `captureServerTrace` so it does not log at `error` level. `server-error-logger.ts` already has a `controlFlowMarker` mechanism (~line 310) that this could hook into.

## Notes
- Automated triage only — do **not** auto-resolve in Sentry; this needs a human decision on skip-vs-log.
- Low user impact (handled, 0 users) but it is masking any *real* synthesis failures on the same cron under the same Sentry group.

---
_Filed by **Helm Mission Control — Sweep**. Mirrored in the Notion Incidents / Errors DB._

Production Postgres reported a `deadlock detected` (severity **ERROR**) during the CoachHelm refresh cron.

- **Source:** Supabase postgres logs — project `qmnssrrolpinvwjjnufo` (Helm-Production)
- **Detected by:** Mission Control sweep, 2026-07-08 ~04:32 UTC
- **When:** 2026-07-08 ~03:45:09 UTC (single occurrence in the last 24h)

## Log evidence
```
LOG    process 1858834 detected deadlock while waiting for ShareLock on transaction 603025 after 1000.113 ms
ERROR  deadlock detected
```

## Context
The deadlock coincides with the CoachHelm standing/insight refresh cron, which around 03:45 UTC was issuing many concurrent `PATCH`/`UPSERT` operations against `golf_goals`, `golf_causal_relationships`, `golf_coach_insights`, and `golf_patterns_v2` (visible in the REST/api logs at ~03:45:32 UTC). Two concurrent transactions acquired `ShareLock`s in opposite order, so Postgres aborted one to break the cycle.

## Impact
One aborted transaction in the refresh path → a likely partial/failed standing or insight refresh for a single player on that cron tick. Not user-facing; self-heals on the next refresh. Low severity but a real concurrency defect worth hardening.

## Suggested next step
Serialize the concurrent refresh writes in the CoachHelm refresh cron — e.g. consistent row-ordering on the batched updates, a per-player advisory lock (`pg_advisory_xact_lock`), or lower refresh concurrency — so repeated ticks can't interleave into a cycle.

## Summary

Package the current HelmV3 cleanup work into one fix-ready tracking issue. This combines findings from the repo freshness audit, the follow-up agent handoff, and the latest Codex session work.

The repo is buildable/testable, but not yet a clean maintenance baseline. Work should proceed as small PRs, not one mega cleanup.

## Hard guardrails

- Do not mutate linked Supabase during discovery/planning.
- Do not close GitHub issues/PRs automatically from this issue.
- Do not delete source files from the first Knip pass.
- Do not run `npm audit fix` or `npm audit fix --force`.
- Do not run broad destructive cleanup like `git clean -Xdf`.
- Do not treat `npm run db:types:check` as read-only; it runs `npm run db:types` first and can rewrite `src/lib/types/database.ts`.
- Keep generated-file/audit-output cleanup separate from app behavior changes.

## Repomix status

Generated packs, all gitignored under `.repomix/`:

## Finding

While fixing #380 (env-scoped seed tooling for `seed-baseball-stats.mjs`), the same production Supabase `service_role` JWT for project `qmnssrrolpinvwjjnufo` was found hardcoded today, in **currently tracked source**, in 9 other files:

- `scripts/check-policies.ts`
- `scripts/check-rls.ts`
- `scripts/db-health-check.ts`
- `scripts/debug-player-insert.mjs`
- `scripts/diagnose-rls.ts`
- `scripts/fix-auth.mjs`
- `scripts/import-via-api.mjs`
- `scripts/list-orphan-players.ts`
- `scripts/run-sql.mjs`

This is **not** old git history that needs scrubbing — the key is live in the current working tree of `main` today. Anyone with read access to this repo has full `service_role` (bypasses RLS) access to the production database referenced by this key.

## Why this is more urgent than a typical secret-scan finding

- `service_role` bypasses Row Level Security entirely.
- The key is in 9 files, not 1 — broad blast radius, easy to miss in a single-file review.
- The project ref (`qmnssrrolpinvwjjnufo`) and key format match the key that was already flagged as compromised in `scripts/seed-baseball-stats.mjs` (see `docs/operations/2026-06-30-baseball-stats-seed-key-rotation.md`) — i.e. this is the *same* key, already known to need rotation, just not yet scrubbed from these 9 additional files.

## Required actions

1. **Rotate** the Supabase `service_role` key for project `qmnssrrolpinvwjjnufo` in the Supabase dashboard (Settings → API).
2. **Update** the new key in: local `.env.local` files (all developers), Vercel (production + preview env vars), and any CI secret stores (GitHub Actions secrets, CircleCI).
3. **Refactor all 9 files** above to read `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` from `process.env` instead of a literal, following the pattern already applied to `scripts/seed-baseball-stats.mjs` in #380 (dry-run-by-default where the script is destructive, fail loudly with a clear message when the env var is missing).
4. **Verify** via `gitleaks detect --no-git -c .gitleaks.toml --source scripts/` once refactored — the new `supabase-hs256-jwt" / `supabase-key-env-assignment` gitleaks rules added in #380 should catch any remaining literal key.

## Context

- See `docs/operations/2026-06-30-baseball-stats-seed-key-rotation.md` for the rotation runbook (already covers the `seed-baseball-stats.mjs` instance of this same key).
- `.gitleaks.toml` already has rules that will catch this pattern going forward, once they're not ignoring these 9 already-tracked files.

## Problem
Several academics server actions are plain exported functions without `withBaseballAction` or `requireBaseballCapability`, while the page guard only protects the route render. `getTeamAcademics`, class CRUD, and `getPlayerClasses` can be invoked directly with arbitrary IDs.

## Evidence
- `src/app/baseball/actions/academics.ts` (lines 113-201): define `getTeamAcademics(teamId)` with no auth/capability check
- `src/app/baseball/actions/academics.ts` (lines 207-329): define `getPlayerClasses`, `addPlayerClass`, `updatePlayerClass`, `deletePlayerClass` similarly unguarded
- Contrast `upsertPlayerAcademics` (lines 518-524) wrapped with `requiredCapability: 'can_view_academics'`

## Why it matters
Defense-in-depth fails if RLS is misconfigured: academics roster and class mutations are not uniformly server-gated like other baseball actions.

## Acceptance criteria
- All academics reads/mutations run inside `withBaseballAction` with `requiredCapability: 'can_view_academics'` (or stricter where appropriate).
- Cross-team `teamId` / `playerId` / `classId` calls return authorization errors without leaking data.
- Existing academics page flow continues to work for authorized JUCO/college staff after gate alignment.
title: BaseballHelm: Enforce auth/capability checks on unwrapped academics server actions

## Problem
Players can acknowledge timeline events on `/baseball/player/timeline`, but the coach player-profile Timeline tab renders `ProfileTimeline` without acknowledgement data or toggles. Coaches cannot see whether a player acknowledged a shared coach note.

## Evidence
- `src/app/baseball/(player-dashboard)/player/timeline/page.tsx` (lines 68-69): load `getTimelineAcksForViewer` and pass `initialAcks` to `PlayerTimelineClient`
- `src/app/baseball/(dashboard)/dashboard/players/[id]/page.tsx` (lines 126-129): fetch timeline events but never fetch acks
- `src/components/baseball/player-profile/PlayerProfileClient.tsx` (lines 1332-1336): render `<ProfileTimeline events={timelineEvents} ... />` with no `acknowledged` / `onToggleAck` props

## Why it matters
The "source → signal → action → timeline → outcome" loop stops at the coach view; acknowledgement tracking is write-only from the player side.

## Acceptance criteria
- Coach player-profile Timeline shows per-event acknowledgement status for events the coach can see.
- After a player acknowledges a `player_only` note event, the coach profile reflects it without a full reload beyond normal revalidation.
title: BaseballHelm: Surface timeline acknowledgement state on the coach player profile

## Problem
The only baseball UI that creates coach notes hardcodes `scope: 'staff_public'`. There is no scope picker, and no UI calls `updateCoachNote` / `deleteCoachNote`. Coaches cannot share notes with players from the profile surface; player-visible Today/Timeline flows never receive those notes.

## Evidence
- `src/components/baseball/player-profile/PlayerProfileClient.tsx` (line 403): calls `createCoachNote({ ..., scope: 'staff_public' })`
- `src/app/baseball/actions/coach-notes.ts` (lines 160-168): only emit `player_only` timeline events when `scope === 'player_visible'`
- `src/lib/baseball/read-models/player-today.ts` (lines 602-610): only reads `scope = 'player_visible'`

## Why it matters
The staff-notes privacy model exists server-side, but the coach authoring UI cannot produce the player-facing notes the player surfaces are built to show.

## Acceptance criteria
- Coach note composer exposes the permitted scopes (at least `staff_public` and `player_visible`).
- Creating a `player_visible` note appears on Player Today and the player timeline as `player_only`.
- Notes created as `staff_public` remain absent from player surfaces.
title: BaseballHelm: Add player-visible scope control when coaches author notes

## Problem
The AI Settings UI only offers Approve for audits with `withheld_reason === 'awaiting_approval'`, but the server action approves any `disposition === 'pending'` row and promotes the paired signal to `desired_visibility`. A pending row withheld for `player_visible_disabled` can still be promoted to player-facing visibility via the action, bypassing the `ai_player_visible_enabled` toggle.

## Evidence
- `src/components/baseball/settings/AiAuditLog.tsx` (line 99, lines 233-235): gate UI on `withheld_reason === 'awaiting_approval'`
- `src/app/baseball/actions/ai-governance.ts` (lines 115-120): approve whenever `disposition === 'pending'`; (lines 125-151): set `visibility: targetVisibility` from `audit.desired_visibility`
- `src/lib/baseball/ai-policy.ts` (lines 292-301): create `disposition: 'pending'` with `reason: 'player_visible_disabled'`

## Why it matters
A coach (or crafted client call) can expose AI output to players while "Player-visible AI enabled" is off.

## Acceptance criteria
- `approveAiOutput` rejects pending audits unless `withheld_reason === 'awaiting_approval'` (and re-checks current AI policy).
- Attempting to approve a `player_visible_disabled` audit returns a clear error and leaves the signal `staff_only`.
- Add a unit/integration test covering this rejection path.
title: BaseballHelm: Block approveAiOutput from bypassing player-visible AI policy

The player Today read model queries `baseball_coach_notes` with columns and filters that do not exist on the typed row shape (`deleted_at` is the soft-delete column; there is no `title`, `pinned`, or `archived_at`). ## Problem
The permissions reference page lists `can_manage_documents` under the Documents group, and document mutations require it server-side, but `StaffSettingsClient`'s `CAPABILITY_DEFS` omits it — coaches cannot assign document-library access through the staff UI.

Settings-capable associate coaches get a broken Staff & Permissions experience — toggles appear editable but every action errors.

## Problem
Program Settings lets coaches disable "Academics & class conflicts" and "Travel & team operations"; values are saved to `baseball_program_settings`, but nothing outside `program-settings.ts` / variant defaults reads `academics_module_enabled` or `travel_module_enabled` to gate routes or actions.

- Academics and travel server actions/pages check `academics_module_enabled` / `travel_module_enabled` and deny when off.

body:
## Problem
Season Settings exposes seven "What this season runs" toggles (`roster_enabled`, `schedule_enabled`, etc.) and persists them via `updateSeason`, but no other application code reads `baseball_seasons` or those columns — toggles are write-only configuration.

## Evidence

Coaches disable stats or roster for an archived/off-season record expecting modules to stop; routes and mutations keep working unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria
- Mutations/routes for roster, schedule, stats, practice templates, lift groups, baselines, and player status check the current season's corresponding `*_enabled` flag server-side.
- Disabling a module returns a clear 403 and hides the nav entry.
- Test: flip `stats_enabled` off → stat write action denied.

body:
## Problem
Team Settings persist `invite_policy`, `allow_player_self_join`, and `require_coach_approval` on `baseball_teams`, but `joinTeam` and `joinTeamByCode` never read those columns. Setting "Closed" or "Require coach approval" does not block or pend membership creation.

## Evidence
- `updateTeamJoinSettings` writes `invite_policy` / `require_coach_approval` (`team-season-settings.ts` lines ~126-156)
- `TeamSettingsClient` copy claims closed rosters block joins (`TeamSettingsClient.tsx` lines ~188-192)
- `joinTeam` inserts directly into `baseball_team_members` after player-type validation only (`teams.ts` lines ~305-312)
- `joinTeamByCode` resolves team by code and calls `joinTeam` with no policy read (`teams.ts` lines ~761-775)

## Why it matters
Coaches believe roster lock and approval gates are active; players can still self-join whenever any valid code path succeeds.

## Acceptance criteria
- `invite_policy === 'closed'` denies all player joins for that team.
- `require_coach_approval === true` creates `pending` membership (or equivalent) instead of `active`.
- `code_self_join` vs `invite_only` is honored on direct code redemption.

## Note
Distinct from the existing "Route direct join_code confirmations through joinTeamByCode" finding (which covers the broken join-code lookup path itself) — this finding covers policy enforcement once redemption is wired up correctly.
title: BaseballHelm: Enforce team join policy (closed/approval-required) on join code redemption

body:
## Problem
Any coach with `can_invite_staff` can grant arbitrary assignable capabilities (including `can_manage_settings` and `can_invite_staff`) to another staff member or to themselves. `updateStaffCapabilities` only blocks edits to primary/head coaches; it never compares the requested capability map to the caller's resolved capabilities or blocks self-escalation.

## Evidence
- `src/app/baseball/actions/staff.ts` — `inviteStaff`/`updateStaffCapabilities` sanitize client input but do not intersect with the caller's caps; `resolveInviteCapabilities` merges presets with explicit grants; target guard is only `is_primary`/`is_head_coach` (lines 422-451, 98-109, 142)

## Why it matters
A limited staffer can promote themselves or a confederate to full program control without head-coach involvement — a direct privilege-escalation path in the roles/permissions system.

## Acceptance criteria
- Server rejects any invite or capability update that grants a capability the actor does not hold (head/primary excepted).
- Self-edits cannot increase the actor's own capabilities.
- Regression test: assistant with only `can_invite_staff` cannot grant `can_manage_settings`.
title: BaseballHelm: Cap staff capability grants to the inviter's own permissions

The UI treats missing `kind` as an open signal, so real meeting items get the wrong badges and wrong actions ("Raise to agenda" instead of "Mark discussed" / "Resolve").

## Problem
Selecting an agenda item can throw at render time because the detail pane calls `.length` on `sourceRefs` without a null guard. The agenda read model sets `sourceRefs` to `null` when the DB column is absent.

## Evidence
- `src/lib/baseball/read-models/decision-room/agenda-ledger.ts` (lines 162, 179): `sourceRefs: row.source_refs ?? null`
- `src/components/baseball/staff-decision-room/StaffDecisionRoomClient.tsx` (lines 1097-1103): `{item.sourceRefs.length === 0 ? (`

## Why it matters
Meeting mode is unusable for any item without structured sources — the right-hand detail pane hard-crashes instead of showing the action bar.

## Acceptance criteria
- Agenda detail renders safely when `sourceRefs` is `null`, `[]`, or populated.
- Evidence section shows the "no structured sources" empty state for `null`/`[]`.
- Regression test covers selecting an agenda row with `source_refs = null`.
title: BaseballHelm: Fix Decision Room agenda detail crash when sourceRefs is null

body:
## Problem
Each `publishLiftDay` call always `insert`s a new `baseball_lift_program_assignments` row and materializes new sessions keyed to that assignment. Re-publishing the same program day (e.g., after editing prescriptions) creates duplicate assignments and duplicate player sessions for the same date instead of updating the existing materialization.

## Evidence
- `src/app/baseball/actions/lifting-v11.ts` (lines 1449-1464): unconditional `.insert` into `baseball_lift_program_assignments`
- `src/app/baseball/actions/lifting-v11.ts` (lines 1507-1523): skip exercise inserts only when a session already has rows, but never update exercises on existing sessions

## Why it matters
Athletes can see multiple "Lift" sessions for one day; coaches editing and re-publishing amplify stale and duplicate workouts.

## Acceptance criteria
- Re-publishing the same `programId` + `liftDayId` + `scheduledDate` updates the existing assignment/sessions (stage-and-swap exercises).
- Player sees exactly one session per published day; edited prescriptions appear after re-publish.
- Optional: prevent duplicate calendar lift events on re-publish when `createCalendarEvent` is true.
title: BaseballHelm: Deduplicate publishLiftDay assignments for the same program day and date

body:
## Problem
If a coach deselects every player in `GroupAvailabilityGrid`, `handleSave` passes `playerIds: undefined` when `selectedPlayerIds.size === 0`. `saveLiftSessionPlan` only intersects when `playerIds.length > 0`, so an empty selection assigns the session to the entire team/group.

## Evidence
- `src/components/baseball/performance/LiftBuilderClient.tsx` (line 262): `playerIds: selectedPlayerIds.size > 0 ? [...selectedPlayerIds] : undefined`
- `src/app/baseball/actions/lift-builder.ts` (lines 325-328): skips filtering when `playerIds` is absent/empty

## Why it matters
The UI implies per-player targeting, but deselecting everyone does the opposite of "nobody" — it blasts the plan to the full roster.

## Acceptance criteria
- Zero selected players → save blocked with a clear error, or `count: 0` with no DB writes.
- Selecting 2 of 10 players materializes exactly 2 sessions.
- UI copy matches behavior ("Save — N selected athletes").
title: BaseballHelm: Treat empty Lift Builder player selection as "assign to none," not whole team

body:
## Problem
In `LineupBuilder.handleDrop`, dropping a player onto a slot that already has a player overwrites the incumbent with no swap and no return to "Available Players." The displaced player is removed from the lineup entirely.

## Evidence
- `src/components/coach/lineup/LineupBuilder.tsx` (lines 60-87): when `draggedSlotIndex === null` (roster → slot), the code sets `newLineup[toSlotIndex] = { player: draggedPlayer }` without preserving the previous `slot.player`

## Why it matters
A common drag-and-drop action silently deletes a batter from the saved lineup; coaches can publish incomplete orders without noticing.

## Acceptance criteria
- Dropping onto an occupied slot swaps players, or moves the displaced player back to the roster pool.
- Repro test: place Player A in slot 3, drag Player B from roster onto slot 3 → both remain in the lineup (swapped or B in 3 / A in roster).
title: BaseballHelm: Swap or return displaced player when dropping into an occupied lineup slot

body:
## Problem
`RosterClient` always shows "Lineup saved successfully" after `await saveLineup(...)`, without inspecting `success`. `saveLineup` returns `{ success: false, error: '...' }` for validation failures (duplicate orders, more than 9 players, missing coach) without throwing.

## Evidence
- `src/app/baseball/(dashboard)/dashboard/roster/RosterClient.tsx` (lines 933-939): awaits `saveLineup` then unconditionally `showToast('Lineup saved successfully', 'success')`
- `src/app/baseball/actions/lineups.ts` (lines 80-81, 111): returns `{ success: false, error: validationError }`

## Why it matters
Coaches believe lineups were persisted when the server rejected them; debugging is painful because the UI contradicts the DB.

## Acceptance criteria
- Success toast only when `result.success === true`.
- Error toast surfaces `result.error` on failure.
- Failed saves do not clear the in-progress lineup builder state.
title: BaseballHelm: Check saveLineup result before showing roster success toast

body:
## Problem
After a player uploads, edits, deletes, or sets a primary video, `LibraryView` calls `onMutated`, but the root handler is explicitly a no-op. Server actions revalidate the path, but the client never refetches props, so the grid stays stale until a full page reload.

## Evidence
- `src/components/baseball/video/VideoLibraryClient.tsx` (lines 433, 451, 461): calls `startTransition(onMutated)` after mutations
- `src/components/baseball/video/VideoLibraryClient.tsx` (lines 1242-1245): `handleMutated` is `// Nothing`

## Why it matters
Users get false "success" feedback while the library still shows deleted videos, missing new uploads, or stale primary badges.

## Acceptance criteria
- After any successful mutation, the library re-renders with updated data (e.g. `router.refresh()` or optimistic local state).
- Upload → new card appears without manual reload; delete → card disappears immediately.
title: BaseballHelm: Refresh Video Library after upload/edit/delete mutations

body:
## Problem
The Video Library uses `VideoUpload`, which uploads to storage and inserts directly into `baseball_videos` from the browser. The server action `saveMyVideo` (gated on `can_upload_video`) exists but is never called, so the Settings-level upload toggle is bypassed and uploads lack centralized server-side enforcement/logging.

## Evidence
- `src/components/baseball/video/VideoLibraryClient.tsx` (lines 29, 509): imports `VideoUpload`
- `src/components/features/video-upload.tsx` (lines 139-147): `supabase.from('baseball_videos').insert(...)` client-side
- `saveMyVideo` is only defined in `src/app/baseball/actions/video-classes.ts` (lines 353-398) with no component callers

## Why it matters
Programs that disable player uploads can still be circumvented; failed RLS inserts can orphan storage objects after a successful upload.

## Acceptance criteria
- `VideoUpload` calls `saveMyVideo` after storage upload instead of client-side `insert`.
- When `players_can_upload_video` is off, upload fails server-side with a clear error before/at DB write.
- Existing `batchUploadStaffVideos` staff path remains unchanged.
title: BaseballHelm: Wire Video Library uploads through saveMyVideo server action

body:
## Problem
`publishLiftDay` materializes player sessions into `baseball_lift_sessions`, but the player-facing Lift Home (`/baseball/dashboard/lift`) and Player Today lift summary both read `helm_lifting_sessions`. A coach who publishes from Program Editor creates workouts staff can see in Live Weight Room (`baseball_lift_sessions`) that never appear on the player's Lift/Today surfaces.

## Evidence
- `src/app/baseball/actions/lifting-v11.ts` (lines 1478-1481): upserts into `baseball_lift_sessions`
- `src/lib/baseball/read-models/player-lift.ts` (lines 8-9, 153): reads `helm_lifting_sessions`
- `src/app/baseball/actions/player-today-lift.ts` (lines 114-133): queries `helm_lifting_sessions`

## Why it matters
The primary coach workflow (build program → publish) silently fails for athletes — they see an empty lift while coaches believe assignments went out.

## Acceptance criteria
- Publishing a program day creates a session visible on `/baseball/dashboard/lift` and Player Today for every targeted athlete.
- Live Weight Room and player surfaces show the same materialized session for a given publish.
- Add an integration test: publish → player lift home returns at least one session for that date.

## Note
This is a distinct table-split bug from the existing "Unify Today lift/readiness reads onto helm_lifting tables" finding (which covers the readiness check-in path) — this one is the program-publish path.
title: BaseballHelm: Route program publishes into the table player lift surfaces actually read

body:

Calendar uses viewport-based height math that does not subtract the shell's sticky notification bar and sits inside a `main` that already reserves bottom-nav padding, producing inconsistent vertical sizing versus other baseball pages.

body:
## Problem
Player Today renders up to three same-weight pill CTAs plus a separate "Next required event" hero card in the first viewport, violating the one-primary-action rule.

## Evidence
- `src/components/baseball/player-today/PlayerTodayClient.tsx` (lines 1497-1528): `PrimaryCtaRow` renders "Check In", "Acknowledge", and "View Today Plan/Schedule" as peer `rounded-full` buttons
- (lines 1609-1632): mount that row and `NextEventHero` back-to-back under a `text-3xl` title block

## Why it matters
Players opening Today on mobile face decision paralysis before seeing schedule content; the highest-priority action (e.g., pending acknowledgement) is not visually dominant.

## Acceptance criteria
- Mobile shows exactly one filled primary CTA chosen by priority (pending ack > due check-in > view plan).
- Secondary actions move to a single overflow/menu or inline text link.
- First meaningful schedule content appears above the fold on a 390×844 device after the single header row.
title: BaseballHelm: Reduce Player Today to one contextual primary CTA on mobile

body:
## Problem
The baseball shell's sticky top row does not account for the iOS notch/status bar, unlike the golf shell which sets a safe-area-aware header offset.

## Evidence
- `src/components/baseball/dashboard-shell.tsx` line 241: `sticky top-0 … px-4 py-2` with no `env(safe-area-inset-top)` / `safe-area-top`
- Contrast `src/app/golf/(dashboard)/FairwayDashboardShell.tsx` line 683: `style={{ '--golf-mobile-header-offset': 'env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px)' }}`
- `src/app/globals.css` (lines 1908-1909): define `.safe-area-top`

## Why it matters
Notification controls and any sticky content below the bar can sit under the status bar on notched iPhones, reducing tap targets and visual consistency with GolfHelm.

## Acceptance criteria
- Baseball shell top chrome includes `padding-top: max(0.5rem, env(safe-area-inset-top))` (or equivalent token).
- Sticky descendants (hub sub-nav, page headers) offset from a shared `--baseball-mobile-header-offset` CSS variable.
- Verified on iOS Safari/Capacitor: bell icon fully visible and tappable below the notch.

body:
## Problem
The public profile uses a tall decorative hero and absolute controls that are not safe-area aware; the back affordance is hard-wired to Discover and the hero exposes two competing coach actions.

## Evidence
- `src/app/baseball/(public)/player/[id]/PlayerProfileClient.tsx` (lines 231-265): `h-52` banner with `absolute top-4 left-4` back link to `/baseball/dashboard/discover`
- (lines 268-297): simultaneous "Add to Watchlist" and "Message" buttons in the hero overlay
- (lines 309-313): `w-32 h-32` avatar on mobile

## Why it matters
Shared recruiting links opened on a phone bury stats/videos below a ~200px+ hero, notch devices can clip controls, and non-Discover entry paths get a misleading back target.

## Acceptance criteria
- Mobile hero height is ≤ ~120px; primary player identity is visible without scrolling on a 390×844 viewport.
- Top controls respect `env(safe-area-inset-top)` (or `safe-area-top` utility).
- Back/history behavior uses browser history or context-aware fallback, not a fixed Discover URL.
- Coach actions collapse to one primary CTA with secondary actions in overflow on `<md`.
title: BaseballHelm: Compact the public player profile mobile hero and fix shared-link navigation

body:
## Problem
Message routes use hard-coded `100dvh` heights that ignore the shell's extra top bar and fixed bottom nav, and the loading state renders a `Header` the live Messages index does not.

## Evidence
- `src/app/baseball/(dashboard)/dashboard/messages/[id]/page.tsx` (lines 47-48): `<Header … />` plus `h-[calc(100dvh-4rem)]`
- `src/app/baseball/(dashboard)/dashboard/messages/page.tsx` line 143: `h-[calc(100dvh-64px)]` with no page header

body:
## Problem
Grouped-hub sibling routes (Roster, Calendar, Messages, Tasks, etc.) rely on `HubSubNav`, but the shell hides that strip below `md`, leaving mobile users without horizontal hub tabs.

## Evidence
- `src/components/baseball/dashboard-shell.tsx` (lines 246-252): `className="hidden md:block md:top-14"` on `HubSubNav`
- `src/app/baseball/(dashboard)/_components/hub-definitions.ts` (lines 50-57): define seven Team-hub destinations including Messages, Tasks, and Documents — none of which are bottom-nav primaries

## Why it matters
A coach on Roster cannot one-tap to Messages or Tasks on phone; they must open the drawer and hunt, while desktop users get a dedicated hub tab strip for the same routes.

## Acceptance criteria
- On mobile hub-owned routes (`/baseball/dashboard/roster`, `/calendar`, `/messages`, `/stats-center`, etc.), a horizontally scrollable sub-nav is visible and matches desktop tab order/labels.
- Sub-nav uses the same active-state styling as desktop and does not add a second utility row above page content (integrate with the single mobile header).
