title: BaseballHelm: Show hub sub-navigation on mobile for Team/Stats routes

body:
## Problem
`BaseballDashboardShell` already renders a sticky top utility row, but many baseball pages mount the full legacy `Header` on top of it. On mobile this stacks two persistent header bands and duplicates notification entry points before page content begins.

## Evidence
- `src/components/baseball/dashboard-shell.tsx` (lines 241-243): render a sticky bar
- `src/app/baseball/(dashboard)/dashboard/roster/RosterClient.tsx` (lines 443-451): mount `<Header>` inside the same shell
- `src/components/layout/header.tsx` (lines 86-159): add menu, mobile search, `NotificationCenter`, and user menu while the shell already shows `NotificationBell`

## Why it matters
Mobile users lose ~120px+ of first-screen space on core flows (Roster, Settings, Discover, message threads) and see two different notification UIs, which breaks the mobile consistency contract's "one header type" and "at most one trailing action" rules.

## Acceptance criteria
- On `<lg`, authenticated baseball routes expose exactly one top chrome row (shell OR page header, not both).
- Notification access exists in one place on mobile; no duplicate bell/popover stacks.
- Roster/Settings/Discover/message-thread pages match Command Center / Player Today / Stats Center (shell-only chrome + in-page title).
title: BaseballHelm: Eliminate stacked mobile top chrome (shell bar + legacy Header)

body:
## Problem
Legacy `analyzePlayer` emits separate hit-milestone and HR-milestone insights but both use `insight_type: 'development_milestone'`. Reconciliation keys insights by `playerId::insight_type`, so when both fire in one run only one milestone survives; the other is dropped or blocks refresh of the first.

## Evidence
- `src/app/baseball/actions/insights.ts` (lines 142-143, 300-328): both branches use `insight_type: 'development_milestone'`

## Why it matters
When a player crosses both thresholds (e.g., 50 hits and 10 HR), coaches see at most one milestone and may miss the other achievement entirely.

## Acceptance criteria
- Use distinct `insight_type` values (e.g., `milestone_hits`, `milestone_hr`) or include the milestone kind in the reconcile key.
- Player with both milestones at once generates two persistable insights.
- Re-running generation updates each milestone independently without overwriting the other.
title: BaseballHelm: Collapse competing development_milestone insights to one per player

body:
## Problem
`generatePostgameReview` upserts all emitted items with `disposition: 'new'` via `mapItem`, despite comments claiming conversions are not clobbered. Regenerating a review (the UI's "Regenerate" button) resets previously converted or dismissed items to actionable "new" state.

## Evidence
```476:498:src/app/baseball/actions/postgame.ts
// Only overwrite content + re-open NEW items; never clobber a coach conversion.
...
disposition: 'new',
dedupe_key: c.dedupeKey,
```
`PostgameReviewClient` exposes Regenerate — `src/components/baseball/postgame/PostgameReviewClient.tsx` (lines 202-211).

## Why it matters
Coaches can duplicate practice blocks / timeline entries by regenerating after conversion, and dismissed recommendations reappear as unresolved work.

## Acceptance criteria
- On upsert conflict, update title/detail/confidence but preserve non-`new` dispositions (`converted_to_task`, `converted_to_timeline`, `dismissed`, `resolved`).
- Regenerating a review does not re-show items already converted to practice or timeline.
- Idempotent regenerate: converted items stay converted even when the same `dedupe_key` is re-emitted.
title: BaseballHelm: Preserve postgame item disposition on regenerate upsert

body:
## Problem
`measureForTeam` upserts effectiveness reviews with `disposition: 'new'` on every run. `savePracticeRecap` auto-invokes this after save (`autoMeasure` defaults on). A coach who dismissed or resolved a review will see it return as "new" after the next recap save or manual re-measure.

## Evidence
- `src/app/baseball/actions/practice-effectiveness.ts` (lines 298-305): auto-measure after recap; (lines 575-608): upsert payload includes `disposition: 'new'`

## Why it matters
Practice recap is the mandated human completion loop; coaches lose triage state immediately after saving recap, so the Decision Room and effectiveness surfaces cannot be trusted.

## Acceptance criteria
- Upsert updates measurement fields but does not reset `disposition` when an existing row is `dismissed`, `resolved`, or `converted`.
- Saving a recap after dismissing a review leaves disposition unchanged.
- Only genuinely new `dedupe_key` rows insert with `disposition: 'new'`.
title: BaseballHelm: Preserve practice-effectiveness review disposition on re-measure upsert

body:
## Problem
`getPracticeIntelligence` derives visibility only from `metadata.visibility`, but the engine stores visibility in the `player_visible` boolean column and does not set `metadata.visibility`. The query also omits `player_visible` from the SELECT. Every signal is normalized to `staff_only`, so player-safe signals are mislabeled and their bodies are stripped from suggested blocks.

## Evidence
```145:178:src/app/baseball/actions/practice-intelligence.ts
function normalizeVisibility(raw: unknown): BaseballBlockVisibility {
  ...
  return 'staff_only';
}
const visibility = normalizeVisibility(meta.visibility);
```
Lines 215-216, 247-249: `description: visibility === 'staff_only' ? null : (signal.summary ?? null)`. Engine metadata has no visibility field — `src/lib/baseball/coachhelm/engine-run.ts` (lines 831-837): `player_visible: c.playerVisible` on row, not in metadata.

## Why it matters
Coaches see false "Staff only" badges and lose player-safe block descriptions when converting signals to practice — violating the board's stated visibility contract.

## Acceptance criteria
- Select `player_visible` (or `visibility` column if present) and map `player_visible === true` → `player_visible` block visibility.
- Player-visible CoachHelm signals show "Player-safe" badge and non-null descriptions in suggestions when appropriate.
- Staff-only signals still hide bodies from player-visible block text.
title: BaseballHelm: Honor player_visible in Practice Intelligence Board visibility

body:
## Problem
CoachHelm engine persists insight text in the `body` column (`buildInsightRow` sets `body: c.body`), and the player page selects `*` from `baseball_coach_insights`. UI components read `insight.description`, which is not populated on engine rows — so titles render but detail/recommended-action copy is blank.

## Evidence
- Engine write: `src/lib/baseball/coachhelm/engine-run.ts` line 816: `body: c.body`
- UI read: `src/components/baseball/player-profile/PlayerInsightsPanel.tsx` (lines 119-121, 146-148): `insight.description`
- Same mismatch in `src/components/baseball/command-center/TeamPlayerPeekPanel.tsx` line 263

## Why it matters
Player profile and command-center peek are primary places coaches review per-player CoachHelm signals; empty bodies make insights look broken or low-confidence.

## Acceptance criteria
- Player insights UI displays `insight.body ?? insight.description` (or read model normalizes to one field).
- Engine-generated insights show full description and recommended action on the player profile.
- Command Center peek panel shows the same text shown in the daily brief (`item.body`).
title: BaseballHelm: Render CoachHelm insight body on player profile (body vs description)

body:
## Problem
`runBaseballEngineCore` upserts every emitted candidate with `status: 'active'` in `buildInsightRow`, and only loads prior state for rows already `status = 'active'`. A coach-dismissed row (`status: 'dismissed'`) is invisible to prior-state lookup, so the next engine run upserts the same `dedupe_key` and overwrites dismissal back to active.

## Evidence
- Prior fetch filters active only: `src/lib/baseball/coachhelm/engine-run.ts` (lines 451-456)
- Upsert always writes active: `src/lib/baseball/coachhelm/engine-run.ts` (lines 810-818): `status: 'active'`

## Why it matters
Even after the dismiss-auth bug is fixed, regenerating the brief (manual run, post-import, or nightly cron) would resurrect signals the coach explicitly removed — breaking the V2 "dismissible AI output" contract.

## Acceptance criteria
- Before upsert, load prior rows for emitted `dedupe_key` values regardless of `status`.
- If prior `status` is `dismissed`, `addressed`, or `resolved`, skip the upsert (or preserve coach status and only update non-triage fields).
- Re-run engine after dismiss leaves the insight out of Command Center / Practice Intelligence feeds.
title: BaseballHelm: Stop CoachHelm engine upsert from reactivating coach-dismissed insights

body:
## Problem
`dismissInsight`, `markInsightAddressed`, and `submitInsightFeedback` compare `baseball_coach_insights.coach_id` (a `baseball_coaches.id`) against `supabase.auth.getUser().id` (auth UID). Those IDs are different domains everywhere else in BaseballHelm (player profile fetch uses `coach.id`; engine writes use `ctx.activeCoachId`). Dismiss/address/feedback therefore return Forbidden for every real coach.

## Evidence
```537:538:src/app/baseball/actions/insights.ts
if (!insight || insight.coach_id !== user.id) {
  return { success: false, error: 'Forbidden: You can only dismiss your own insights' };
}
```
Same pattern at lines 574-575 and 615-616. Player profile correctly scopes insights with `coach.id` at `src/app/baseball/(dashboard)/dashboard/players/[id]/page.tsx` line 121.

## Why it matters
`PlayerInsightsPanel` calls these actions on every Dismiss / Mark Addressed click; the UI refreshes but the insight stays active, so coaches cannot triage CoachHelm output.

## Acceptance criteria
- Ownership check resolves `baseball_coaches.id` from `user.id` (or compares against `ctx.activeCoachId` inside a `withBaseballAction` wrapper) before updating.
- Dismissing an active insight from the player profile removes it after refresh and sets `status = 'dismissed'`.
- Same fix applied consistently to `markInsightAddressed` and `submitInsightFeedback`.
title: BaseballHelm: Fix insight dismiss/feedback auth comparing coach_id to auth user.id

body:
## Problem
Coach onboarding collects a Free vs Elite plan choice and highlights selection in UI, but neither `completeCoachOnboarding` nor `signupAndCompleteCoachOnboarding` accepts a `plan` argument — selection is discarded at submit.

## Evidence
- `coach-onboarding/page.tsx` (lines 199, 355-363): set `plan` then call `handleSubmit()`; (lines 315-336): call onboarding actions with coach/program fields only — no `plan`
- `onboarding.ts` `CoachOnboardingInput` (lines 63-71) has no plan field

title: BaseballHelm: Persist or remove cosmetic coach plan selection during onboarding

body:
## Problem
The privacy settings page documents only four real DB columns, hardcodes defaults for many others, and the form saves the entire UI object — including field names that are not loaded from or mapped to the database.

## Evidence
- `privacy/page.tsx` (lines 29-31) comment: "Database columns: show_contact_info, show_academics, show_dream_schools, profile_visibility"; (lines 40-51): hardcode `show_full_name: true`, `show_school: true`, etc.
- `PrivacySettingsForm.tsx` (lines 229-237): `.update(settings)` / `.insert({ ...settings, player_id })` with keys like `show_full_name`, `show_location`, `show_in_discover` that are never read from the DB in the page loader

## Why it matters
Players toggle privacy controls that may not persist, may fail on save, or may not affect the public profile — undermining recruiting privacy trust.

## Acceptance criteria
- Loader and saver use the same canonical field list as `baseball_player_settings` (map UI labels to DB columns explicitly).
- Toggling a control → Save → reload shows the same state.
- Public profile rendering respects saved values for fields exposed in the form.
title: BaseballHelm: Fix privacy settings field mapping so saves match baseball_player_settings schema

body:
## Problem
The coach onboarding Account step enables Continue at 8+ characters, but `signupAndCompleteCoachOnboarding` rejects passwords that don't meet full complexity rules — so users pass the wizard then fail on plan submit with a server error.

## Evidence
- `coach-onboarding/page.tsx` line 688: `disabled={... || password.length < 8}`; line 681 hints at uppercase/lowercase/number/special
- `onboarding.ts` (lines 266-271): call `validatePassword(data.password)` and return `passwordValidation.feedback[0]` on failure

## Why it matters
Creates a dead-end at the plan step after users already entered program and account details — high abandonment and repeat attempts.

## Acceptance criteria
- Account-step Continue uses the same `validatePassword` rules (client-side mirror or server pre-check).
- Passwords like `password1` are blocked on Continue with the same message the server would return.
- Successful plan selection only occurs after password passes server rules.
title: BaseballHelm: Align coach onboarding password validation with server validatePassword

body:
## Problem
The lifting step's primary "Yes — invite them" card calls `handleLiftingAnswer('yes')` without an email, but `setLiftingMode` requires `inviteEmail` for `mode === 'yes'`. The onboarding handler ignores the failure and still completes onboarding.

## Evidence
- `coach-onboarding/page.tsx` line 828: `onClick={() => handleLiftingAnswer('yes')}`; (lines 392-398): pass `inviteEmail` only when truthy; (lines 402-409): catch all errors as "non-fatal" and always call `navigateAfterOnboarding`
- `src/app/lifting/actions/onboarding.ts` (lines 240-244): `if (!inviteEmail) return { success: false, error: "Enter the lifting coach's email address." }`

## Why it matters
Coaches who tap the prominent "Yes" card believe they opted into inviting an S&C coach, but no invite is sent and no error is shown.

## Acceptance criteria
- Top "Yes" card either requires email first or routes focus to the email field; do not call `setLiftingMode('yes')` without a validated email.
- Failed `setLiftingMode` surfaces an inline error; onboarding may still allow "Skip for now."
- "Send Invite & Continue" remains the only path that submits `mode: 'yes'` with an email.
title: BaseballHelm: Block coach onboarding "Yes — invite S&C coach" unless email is provided

## Problem
`handleToggle` and `handleShare` optimistically mutate local `today` state before calling the server, but `runAction` only sets an error string on failure — it never rolls back the optimistic state. A failed `toggleContractItem` or `setContractVisibility` leaves the UI showing honored/skipped/shared states that were not persisted.

## Evidence
- Optimistic update without revert: `src/components/baseball/daily-contract/DailyContract.tsx` (lines 606-623): `setToday(...)` then `runAction(() => toggleContractItem(...))`
- `runAction` on failure: (lines 557-571): `if (!res.success) { setError(...); return; }` — no state restore. Same pattern for share: (lines 645-658).

## Why it matters
Players think intentions are honored or shared with coaches when the server rejected the write; streak/completion decisions are made against stale UI.

## Acceptance criteria
- On `toggleContractItem` / `setContractVisibility` failure, item done/skipped flags and visibility control revert to pre-click state.
- Error banner shows the server message; a refresh shows the same state as before the failed action.
- Regression test simulates action rejection and asserts UI rollback.

body:
## Problem
The Today page resolves the team timezone and passes `todayIso` to the Daily Contract and performance check-ins, but calls `getPlayerToday(context.activeTeamId)` without `{ forDate: todayIso }`. Inside the read-model, `day` defaults to UTC (`new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10)`) and event windows use UTC midnight (`dayStart = ${day}T00:00:00.000Z`), so schedule, lifts, practice group, and "isToday" flags can disagree with the header date and daily contract for teams west of UTC after roughly 4-7pm local.

## Evidence
- Page passes TZ date only to contract: `src/app/baseball/(player-dashboard)/player/today/page.tsx` (lines 104-118) vs line 117: `getPlayerToday(context.activeTeamId)` — no `forDate`
- UTC default: `src/lib/baseball/read-models/player-today.ts` (lines 498-500)
- Team-TZ contract write: `src/app/baseball/actions/daily-contract.ts` (lines 136-139)

## Why it matters
A player can commit a daily contract for "today" while Today shows yesterday's schedule (or misses tonight's practice) — reproducible any evening in US timezones.

## Acceptance criteria
- `getPlayerToday(teamId, { forDate: todayIso })` is called from the Today page with the same `todayIso` used for the contract.
- Event/lift/practice filters use team-local day boundaries, not `T00:00:00.000Z`.
- Test case: team TZ `America/Los_Angeles`, server time `...T04:00:00Z` → schedule and contract both treat the day as the local calendar date, not the UTC date.
title: BaseballHelm: Pass team-tz todayIso into getPlayerToday

## Problem
`getPlayerPractices()` maps `p.calendar_start_time`, `p.calendar_date`, `p.calendar_end_time`, and `p.location`, but `baseball_practices` has only `event_id` (no calendar columns). The select never joins `baseball_events`, so those fields are always `undefined`, class-conflict detection never runs, and wall-clock block times never render.

## Evidence
- Phantom field usage: `src/app/baseball/actions/practice.ts` (lines 718-719): `const startTime: string | null = p.calendar_start_time ?? null` and (lines 768-771)
- Schema: `src/lib/types/baseball-practice.ts` (lines 28-45): `event_id` only, no `calendar_*`
- Contrast with the working pattern in `src/lib/baseball/read-models/player-today.ts` (lines 624-629): `baseball_events!inner(start_time)` join

## Why it matters
Players on `/baseball/player/practice` never see class-conflict warnings or real start times, even when coaches attached a calendar event at publish time.

## Acceptance criteria
- Published practice with a linked `event_id` shows `calendarDate`, `calendarStartTime`, and `location` on the player practice page.
- A player with overlapping `baseball_player_classes` sees `hasClassConflict: true` on the conflicting block.
- Unit test fixtures a practice + event + class schedule and asserts conflict detection fires.
title: BaseballHelm: Join practice events in getPlayerPractices for calendar times

The server read-model still queries legacy `baseball_readiness_checkins` and `baseball_lift_sessions`, while the interactive Lift & Check-in card writes/reads `helm_lifting_readiness_checkins` and `helm_lifting_sessions` via the W2-G rewire. - Lift card read path: `src/app/baseball/actions/player-today-lift.ts` (lines 114-134): `helm_lifting_sessions`

The core daily loop is broken for any team on the unified lifting stack — the page's summary strip, readiness band, and execution card disagree on the same day's data.

- "Lifts Due" count matches sessions shown in the Lift & Check-in card for the same player/team/date.
- Contract test asserts `getPlayerToday` and `getPlayerLiftTodaySummary` query the same storage layer.

## Problem
The chat UI subscribes only to message `INSERT` events, not `UPDATE`, so a sender's single-check "sent" state never upgrades to "read" when the recipient opens the thread.

## Evidence
- `src/hooks/use-messages.ts` (lines 42-56): subscribe to `event: 'INSERT'` only
- `src/components/messages/ChatWindow.tsx` (lines 15-31): render `MessageStatus` from `message.read`
- `src/app/actions/messages.ts` (lines 347-351): set `read: true` on others' messages when the viewer opens the thread

## Why it matters
Read receipts are a core messaging UX signal; they appear stuck on "sent" until a full page reload.

## Acceptance criteria
- Realtime subscription (or refetch) handles `UPDATE` on `baseball_messages` for the open conversation.
- Sender sees double-check/read state within a few seconds of recipient opening the thread.
- No duplicate messages when combining INSERT + UPDATE handlers.
title: BaseballHelm: Update read receipts when the other party reads messages

The announcements page stores data in `useState` loaded once in `useEffect`, but create/delete flows call `router.refresh()`, which does not re-run that effect — so the list stays stale until a full reload.

## Problem
`sendMessage` in the hook always returns `true` because the server action returns `{ success: false }` instead of throwing; the UI clears input and skips error toasts on failed sends.

body:
## Problem
Camp list/detail format dates with `new Date(dateString)` on date-only strings (`YYYY-MM-DD`). In US timezones west of UTC, that parses as the prior local calendar day.

## Evidence
```44:49:src/app/baseball/(dashboard)/dashboard/camps/page.tsx
function formatDate(dateString: string): string {
  return new Date(dateString).toLocaleDateString('en-US', {
    month: 'short',
    day: 'numeric',
    year: 'numeric',
  });
```
Same pattern in `src/app/baseball/(dashboard)/dashboard/camps/[id]/page.tsx` (lines 69-75). Travel already avoids this with `T12:00:00`.

## Why it matters
Camp start/end dates shown to players and coaches can be one day early — confusing scheduling and registration decisions.

## Acceptance criteria
- All camp date displays parse date-only values with a consistent local anchor (e.g. `T12:00:00`) or `date-fns` `parseISO` + `format`.
- Jul 15 stored in DB renders as "Jul 15" in US timezones.
- Shared formatter reused across camps list and detail pages.
title: BaseballHelm: Fix camp date display off-by-one for date-only values

Coaches and players see trips under the wrong heading on the day of travel.

body:
## Problem
Baseball calendar hardcodes `requires_rsvp: false` on read, and `createBaseballEvent` never writes `requires_rsvp` even when the shared calendar UI sends `requiresRsvp`. Player RSVP controls in `EventDetailModal`/`MobileEventSheet` are gated on `event.requires_rsvp`, so RSVP is effectively dead for BaseballHelm.

## Evidence
- `src/app/baseball/(dashboard)/dashboard/calendar/page.tsx` line 107: `requires_rsvp: false`
- `src/app/baseball/actions/calendar.ts` insert (lines 132-147): omits `requires_rsvp`; RSVP attendance is only created when `input.requiresRsvp` (line 153)
- `scripts/seed-baseball-demo.ts` / team-ops seeds show the column exists on `baseball_events`

## Why it matters
Coaches cannot run mandatory RSVPs for practices/games; players never see RSVP buttons despite coach intent.

## Acceptance criteria
- Create/update actions persist `requires_rsvp` (and existing deadline/max fields).

body:
## Problem
Camp cards count all `baseball_camp_registrations` rows, including cancelled ones, while unregister only flips `status` to `cancelled`. Cancelled players still consume capacity in the displayed count and `isFull` logic.

## Evidence
- `src/app/baseball/(dashboard)/dashboard/camps/page.tsx` (lines 224-225, 238): fetch `registrations:baseball_camp_registrations(count)` with no status filter; (lines 298-301): cancel via `update({ status: 'cancelled' })` rather than delete

## Why it matters
After cancellations, camps show as full and block new signups even with open spots.

## Acceptance criteria
- Capacity count includes only active statuses (`registered`, `confirmed`, `attended`, etc.), not `cancelled`.
- Card count, `isFull`, and coach roster totals stay consistent after cancel/re-register.
- Regression test: cancel one of N registrations and verify count drops.
title: BaseballHelm: Exclude cancelled camp registrations from capacity counts

body:
## Problem
Player camp registration is a client-side `insert` with a UI-only `isFull` check. The server action `registerForCamp` also never checks `capacity`. Concurrent registrations can exceed capacity ("Camp Full" is bypassable).

## Evidence
- `src/app/baseball/(dashboard)/dashboard/camps/page.tsx` (lines 71-72): gate UI on count; (lines 274-281): insert directly from the browser
- `src/app/baseball/actions/camps.ts` (lines 270-314): register without any capacity read or lock

## Why it matters
Camps can be overbooked under normal concurrent use; coaches see incorrect availability.

## Acceptance criteria
- Registration goes through a server action that checks active registration count vs `capacity` inside a transaction/RPC.
- UI disables "Register" only after server confirms availability; over-capacity returns a clear error.
- Test covers two simultaneous registrations when one spot remains.
title: BaseballHelm: Enforce camp capacity atomically on registration

## Problem
The join page correctly resolves teams from `baseball_teams.join_code`, but the confirm button always calls `processTeamInvitation`, which only looks up `baseball_team_invitations`. College/JUCO coaches generate persistent team join codes (`generateTeamInviteCode` → `/baseball/join/{code}`), so those players see a valid preview and then get "Invalid invitation code" on confirm.

body:
## Problem
`GamesList` computes losses as `completedGames.length - wins`, so tied games (equal scores) are counted as losses.

## Evidence
- `src/components/baseball/games/GamesList.tsx` (lines 76-80): `wins` requires `our_score > opponent_score`; `losses = completedGames.length - wins` with no tie branch (compare `BoxScoreView.tsx` lines 33-35, which labels ties 'T')

## Why it matters
The games list header ("X played · YW ZL") misstates team record whenever a game ends tied.

## Acceptance criteria
- W-L-T summary treats `our_score === opponent_score` as a tie.
- Header format shows ties when T > 0 (e.g. "12W-8L-1T").

body:
## Problem
When a CSV upload auto-saves (`allMatched`), it calls `saveBoxScoreBatting` or `saveBoxScorePitching` only — neither marks the game completed nor triggers season-stat recalculation. The UI still tells the user "All matched — stats saved!"

## Evidence
- `src/app/baseball/actions/games.ts` (lines 986-992): auto-saves via side-specific save actions only; `markGameCompleted` + `recalculate_baseball_season_stats` live in a separate path (lines 639-700)

## Why it matters
Coaches can believe a game is finalized and season totals updated, while Stats Center / season tables remain stale until a separate manual save path runs.

## Acceptance criteria
- Successful CSV auto-save either runs the same atomic path as `saveFullBoxScore` or explicitly completes the game and recalculates affected players' season rows.
- Season stats and game status reflect the upload without a second manual action.
- UI copy distinguishes "lines saved" vs "game finalized" if completion stays optional.

body:

body:
## Problem
The player stats page labels the section "{currentYear} Game Log" but the query returns every box-score line for that player/team with no season/date filter and sorts by `created_at`, not game date.

body:
## Problem
Team pitching totals add `ip` values with `+` (e.g. `6.1 + 6.2 → 12.3`). In baseball notation `.1`/`.2` are thirds of an inning (outs), so summed IP and derived ERA/WHIP/K9 are wrong whenever multiple partial innings exist.

## Evidence
- `src/components/baseball/box-score/BoxScoreView.tsx` (lines 58-72): `ip: acc.ip + r.ip` then `teamERA = 9 * pitchTotals.er / pitchTotals.ip`
- Same pattern in `src/components/baseball/box-score/BoxScoreEntry.tsx` (line 448)
- `src/components/baseball/season-stats/PlayerGameLog.tsx` (lines 63-68, 306-309)
- `src/lib/baseball/read-models/stats-center.ts` (line 920: `dst.ip += line.ip ?? 0` before `finalizePitching` at lines 427-434)

## Why it matters
Multi-pitcher games show incorrect team ERA/WHIP on the box-score view, player game log totals, and Stats Center season pitching rates.

## Acceptance criteria
- Introduce a shared `sumInningsPitched(lines)` helper that converts to outs and back (e.g. `6.1 + 6.2 → 4.1`).
- Unit tests cover partial-inning sums and resulting ERA/WHIP.
- Box Score view, game log footer, and Stats Center pitching splits all use the helper.
title: BaseballHelm: Sum innings pitched in outs, not as base-10 decimals

body:
## Problem
On a completed game with stats, the "Update Box Score" manual form is rendered with empty defaults instead of the saved batting/pitching lines. `BoxScoreEntry` supports `initialBatting`/`initialPitching`, but nothing passes them, and save only submits non-zero rows — so saving can wipe the existing box score.

## Evidence
- `src/app/baseball/(dashboard)/dashboard/stats/games/[gameId]/page.tsx` (lines 89-99): renders `<BoxScoreUpload game={...} teamPlayers={...} />` with no box-score props
- `src/components/baseball/box-score/BoxScoreUpload.tsx` (lines 181-182): calls `<BoxScoreEntry game={game} teamPlayers={teamPlayers} />`
- `src/components/baseball/box-score/BoxScoreEntry.tsx` (lines 125-134): filters to `nonZeroBatting` before `saveFullBoxScore`

## Why it matters
A coach opening "Update Box Score" to tweak one pitcher line can accidentally delete the entire batting box score (and vice versa) on save.

## Acceptance criteria
- Opening manual entry on a game with existing lines pre-fills batting and pitching from `getGameBoxScore`.
- Saving after a single-field edit preserves all other existing lines.
- Add a regression test that re-saving without edits does not reduce row counts.
title: BaseballHelm: Preload existing box-score lines when editing a completed game

Discover fetches one paginated page sorted by `updated_at` server-side, then re-sorts only that page client-side (`velo_desc`, `gpa_desc`, etc.). Changing sort does not reorder the full result set — only the players on the current page.

body:
## Problem
`getDiscoverTeams` paginates orgs at the DB, then filters out orgs without a named head coach and returns `count: teams.length` / `pages` from that post-filter page slice. Totals reflect the current page only (often 0-1 pages), and high-value programs on later DB pages never surface.

## Evidence
- `src/app/baseball/actions/discover.ts` (lines 355-357): `.range(offset, offset + perPage - 1)`
- `src/app/baseball/actions/discover.ts` (lines 524-532): `.filter((org) => Boolean(org.head_coach_name))`
- `src/app/baseball/actions/discover.ts` (lines 537-540): `count: teams.length`, `pages: Math.ceil(teams.length / perPage)`

## Why it matters
Teams Discover shows a wrong "N programs found", broken pagination, and can hide most programs from coaches browsing by state/search.

## Acceptance criteria
- Total count and page math are computed on the filtered discoverable set before slicing the current page.
- Page 2+ returns new programs when more exist.
- Header count in `DiscoverClient` matches server total, not page-local length.

body:
## Problem
Discover's watchlist toggle optimistically mutates local `watchlistIds` after calling server actions that return `{ success: false }` without throwing. Failed adds/removes (recruitability denial, duplicate, permission) still flip the star state in the UI.

## Evidence
- `src/components/coach/discover/DiscoverView.tsx` (lines 363-374): updates `setWatchlistIds` after `await addToWatchlist` / `removeFromWatchlist` with no `result.success` check
- `src/app/baseball/actions/watchlist.ts` (lines 111-113, 122-124): returns `{ success: false, message: '...' }` without throwing

## Why it matters
Coaches believe a prospect is watchlisted (or removed) when the server rejected the action — downstream pipeline/compare state diverges from reality.

## Acceptance criteria
- Toggle only updates local state when `result.success === true`.
- On failure, show the server `message`/`error` via toast and keep the prior watchlist state.
- Bulk "add all to watchlist" reports per-player failures and does not mark failed IDs as watched.
title: BaseballHelm: Revert Discover watchlist UI when server actions fail

body:
## Problem
After kanban drag, `PipelineClient` always fires a success toast even though `updateStage` returns `false` on error (and already shows its own error toast). Coaches get contradictory feedback and may think the move persisted.

## Evidence
- `src/app/baseball/(dashboard)/dashboard/pipeline/PipelineClient.tsx` (lines 250-255): awaits `updateStage(...)` then unconditionally `showToast(..., 'success')`
- `src/hooks/use-watchlist.ts` (lines 114-117): returns `false` and calls `toast.error` on failure

## Why it matters
False-positive success toasts make pipeline state appear updated when the database write failed.

## Acceptance criteria
- Kanban drag handler checks the boolean return from `updateStage` (or migrates to the server action) before showing success.
- Only one toast per action (success OR error).
- Failed drag reverts the card to its prior column without a success message.
title: BaseballHelm: Stop showing pipeline drag success when stage update fails

body:
## Problem
On drag end, the kanban handler casts `over.id` directly to `PipelineStage`. With `closestCorners`, `over` is often another draggable card (watchlist row UUID), not a column stage id — so the code attempts to write an invalid `pipeline_stage` value.

## Evidence
- `src/app/baseball/(dashboard)/dashboard/pipeline/PipelineClient.tsx` (lines 246-251): `const newStage = over.id as PipelineStage`
- `src/components/features/pipeline-card.tsx` (line 27): draggable `id: item.id` (UUID)
- `src/components/features/pipeline-column.tsx` (lines 20-22): droppable `id: stage`

## Why it matters
Dropping a card onto another card can corrupt or fail the stage update, and the UI still celebrates success (see related issue on false success toasts).

## Acceptance criteria
- Resolve the target stage from the droppable column container (e.g. `over.data.current.droppableContainer` or explicit stage lookup), ignoring card UUIDs.
- Drops onto invalid targets are no-ops with no DB write.
- Manual QA: drag card onto another card vs onto empty column behaves correctly.

body:
## Problem
A legacy Baseball stats seed script targets a fixed Supabase project/team/coach and deletes existing `baseball_player_stats` rows before inserting generated sessions.

## Evidence
- `scripts/seed-baseball-stats.mjs` hardcodes project/team/coach values and constructs a service-role Supabase client.
- The script loops roster members and deletes each player’s `baseball_player_stats` rows for the fixed team before inserting generated sessions.
- This bypasses the safer dry-run/confirmation/idempotent pattern used by newer seed tooling.

## Why this matters
Running this helper against the configured project can destroy real stat history for that team. It is a production-readiness hazard even beyond the credential issue already tracked elsewhere.

## Acceptance criteria
- Remove hardcoded project/team/service-key values.
- Require environment variables plus explicit `--confirm` and target environment/team confirmation.
- Replace destructive delete/reinsert with deterministic upserts or a clearly scoped rollbackable run.
- Refuse to run against production unless an explicit production override is set.
- Add a smoke/test guard for dry-run behavior.

## Duplicate check
#391 covers hardcoded credentials. This issue tracks destructive seed behavior and missing execution safety gates.

## Problem
The stat event import commit path says it revalidates the review/hold decision server-side, but the current hold logic still trusts client-supplied `detectionAutoCommit`.

## Evidence
- `src/app/baseball/actions/stat-event-imports.ts` computes `requiresReview` from `entry.requiresReviewByDefault` plus `args.detectionAutoCommit`.

- `applyEventImportPlan()` then skips row-level validation errors and writes valid rows, so a stale or tampered client can potentially turn a hold/no-commit preview into a commit request.

Low-confidence or untrusted baseball stat files should not power stats, CoachHelm, or dashboards just because the browser echoed a permissive band. The server must own the final review decision.

- `commitEventImport` recomputes detection from the committed raw file body or validates a signed/server-issued preview decision.
- `do_not_commit` never writes rows.
- `hold_for_review` always stages rows for review instead of auto-writing.
- Tests cover tampered/missing `detectionAutoCommit`, low-confidence parse, required-review source, and normal auto-commit.

## Duplicate check

- `src/app/baseball/(dashboard)/dashboard/travel/page.tsx` catches load errors, logs `[Baseball Travel] Error loading`, then can render `No Team Found` or an empty itinerary state.

This is the product-trust failure mode: outage, RLS denial, or partial data can look like “no announcements,” “no travel,” “no players,” or a no-op success. Coaches and players cannot tell missing data from broken data.

## Problem
Calendar/Event server actions use ad hoc authorization instead of the BaseballHelm `withBaseballAction` pattern used by newer production surfaces. Create/update/delete/check-in paths do not consistently enforce team membership and staff capabilities.

## Evidence
- `src/app/baseball/actions/calendar.ts` performs direct `createClient()` + `auth.getUser()` checks.
- `createBaseballEvent` only checks capability when an explicit `teamId` is supplied.
- `updateBaseballEvent` relies on `created_by = coach.id`, which can block authorized staff and ignore team capability policy.
- Attendance/check-in mutations verify a coach profile but need explicit event-team and target-player membership checks.

## Why it matters
Calendar is shared by coaches and players. Inconsistent action gates create IDOR risk, staff-permission drift, and hard-to-debug behavior differences between UI paths.

## Acceptance criteria
- Calendar mutations use `withBaseballAction` or an equivalent shared guard.
- Every mutation validates target team, actor role, required capability, and target player/event membership.
- Authorized staff can perform capability-appropriate updates even if they did not create the row.
- Unauthorized staff/players receive sanitized failures, not raw DB errors.
- Add action-level tests for create/update/delete/check-in/attendance denial and success paths.
- Add at least one RLS/pgTAP or integration test for cross-team denial.

The player Calendar route can resolve the wrong team context by comparing `baseball_team_members.player_id` to the auth user id instead of the baseball player profile id. A valid player can pass auth and still see an empty/no-team Calendar.

This is a silent product-trust bug: the player sees missing schedule data rather than an explicit failure. Calendar is one of the core player daily surfaces.

- A player with a valid baseball team membership sees that team's events.

Non-showcase BaseballHelm coaches can see an Organization hub because `events` is registered as visible to both roles/programs, and the sidebar shows the Organization hub when any of `organization`, `teams`, or `events` is visible. This creates a polished-looking nav link that routes users into a guard bounce. It makes the shell feel broken and hides real route contract drift.

- Showcase/academy/club coaches still see the correct org routes.

## Problem

`git ls-files -ci --exclude-standard` still reports the generated Capacitor iOS bundle:

- `ios/App/App/config.xml`
- `ios/App/App/public/**`

Tracked ignored files create confusing repo hygiene signals. The bundle is generated by `npx cap sync ios`, and Xcode Cloud already runs that in `ios/App/ci_scripts/ci_post_clone.sh`, but removing it should be verified against the native build flow first.
